desc: Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to access code-protected shares because share codes are enforced only client-side. Attackers knowing a share ID can call the share items and download endpoints to list and download files without the code, even on preview-only shares.
title: Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 Share Code and Permission Scope Bypass

desc: Keep 0.34.10 through 0.55.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in its CEL-to-SQL converter, which inserts bracket-indexed JSON keys from CEL filters unescaped into JSON path expressions for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Authenticated users with read:alert permission can submit crafted CEL expressions to /alerts/query or the cel parameter of /incidents, using result counts as a boolean oracle to extract other tenants' alerts and password hashes.
title: Keep 0.34.10 through 0.55.0 Blind SQL Injection via CEL Bracket-Indexed JSON Keys

desc: Seafile SeaDoc converter 2.0.4 before 2.0.11 and 3.0.0 before 3.0.8 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers holding a public share token to execute code. Attackers supply an absolute filename to /api/v1/confluence-to-wiki/ to extract a ZIP from download_url into the Python library path, then trigger the module's import via a file-convert request.
title: SeaDoc converter 2.0.4 before 2.0.11 and 3.0.0 before 3.0.8 Path Traversal RCE via confluence-to-wiki

desc: Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains an improper restriction of authentication attempts vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to brute-force six-digit password reset codes via PUT /apis/user/forget-password. Attackers can request a code for a known email and submit unlimited guesses during its 300-second lifetime to set a chosen password and take over the account.
title: Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 Password Reset Code Brute-Force Account Takeover

desc: Tactical RMM 0.17.0 through 1.6.1 contains an arbitrary file read in the /reporting/templates/preview/ endpoint because WeasyPrint resolves file:// links in user-supplied template_md and embeds the files in the returned PDF. Users with report management permission can read the Django SECRET_KEY, reused as the NATS password, and publish runscript commands to every managed agent.
title: Tactical RMM 0.17.0 through 1.6.1 Arbitrary File Read via Report Preview

desc: DjangoBlog 2.0.0.0 through 2.1.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the class_filter comment sanitizer passes event-handler attributes on span, div, pre and code tags. Authenticated commenters can post a div with autofocus and onfocus attributes, executing script without interaction for every visitor, including administrators.
title: DjangoBlog 2.0.0.0 through 2.1.0.0 Stored XSS via Comment Sanitizer class_filter

desc: ragent 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in RagTraceController that allows any logged-in user to view all users' RAG traces. Attackers can page through /rag/traces/runs and related node endpoints to read other users' usernames, user ids, conversation ids, questions, and per-node execution details.
title: ragent 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 Missing Authorization via /rag/traces/runs

desc: ragent 1.1.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject scripts by uploading SVG knowledge-base documents served inline as image/svg+xml. Attackers can upload a script-bearing SVG via /knowledge-base/{kb-id}/docs/upload so that victims opening /knowledge-base/docs/{docId}/file execute it in the application origin, enabling account takeover.
title: ragent 1.1.0 Stored XSS via SVG Knowledge-Base Document Upload

desc: free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in FileShareServiceImpl.getPages, which passes the orderBy parameter of the /apis/share/pages endpoint verbatim into the ORDER BY clause via MyBatis-Flex without a column whitelist. Authenticated users can supply CASE WHEN subquery expressions that use share ordering as a boolean oracle to read arbitrary database contents, such as share codes.
title: Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 SQL Injection via orderBy Parameter

desc: DjangoBlog commit d186b1c through commit 6134ed6 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated OAuth users to inject script via an unescaped nickname in comment reactions. Attackers can set their OAuth display name to a payload closing the single-quoted data-reactions attribute, then react to a comment to execute script in article visitors' browsers.
title: DjangoBlog commit d186b1c through 6134ed6 Stored XSS via Comment Reactions

desc: paicoding 1.0.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the ArticleRestController article detail endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to read restricted articles. Attackers can enumerate article IDs via GET /article/api/data/detail/{articleId} to retrieve full content of paid, login-only, member-only and draft articles.
title: paicoding 1.0.3 Missing Authorization via Article Detail API Endpoint

desc: paicoding 1.0.3 contains a payment bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to unlock paid articles by guessing weak payment confirmation codes. Attackers can start a payment, enumerate roughly 2000 IdUtil.genPayCode counter values, and submit the matching verifyCode to the unauthenticated callback to mark it paid.
title: paicoding 1.0.3 Payment Bypass via Guessable Codes in /article/api/pay/callback

desc: SurveyKing 1.13.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in result lookup: the anonymous survey view leaks the lookup configuration, including its password, and the lookup password check is skipped when no answer is sent. Unauthenticated attackers with a public survey link can inject a % wildcard into the MyBatis LIKE condition to match all responses, then call loadProject with an answerId to read complete responses including hidden fields.
title: SurveyKing 1.13.2 Unauthenticated Survey Response Disclosure via Result Lookup

desc: SurveyKing 1.12.0 through 1.13.2 contains an authorization bypass in the linked survey feature that fails to verify the referenced linkSurveyId belongs to the caller's own project. Authenticated attackers can point a linked option at another user's survey so that loadLinkResult and updateLinkSurveyAnswer read, rewrite, or create responses in that survey.
title: SurveyKing 1.12.0 through 1.13.2 Authorization Bypass via Linked Survey linkSurveyId

desc: SurveyKing 1.13.0 through 1.13.2 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the server accepts a respondent-supplied survey snapshot and the frontend renders its titles via innerHTML. Anonymous respondents can submit a forged snapshot embedding event handlers such as img onerror that execute in an administrator's browser session when the response is viewed.
title: SurveyKing 1.13.0 through 1.13.2 Stored XSS via Response Survey Snapshot

desc: SurveyKing 1.12.0 through 1.13.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit survey responses because AnswerServiceImpl.saveAnswer skips login-required and survey password checks. Attackers can submit responses to protected surveys and set createBy in the request body to impersonate other users, corrupting survey results.
title: SurveyKing 1.12.0 through 1.13.2 Authentication Bypass via saveAnswer Response Submission

desc: paicoding from commit b8206b9 through commit 903adce uses predictable credentials for accounts created via ZSXQ login, because loginByZsxq derives both the username and password solely from the member's ZSXQ number. Unauthenticated attackers can read that number from the victim's /user/{userId} profile page, compute the credentials, and log in via /login/username to take over the account.
title: paicoding commit b8206b9 through 903adce Predictable ZSXQ Account Credentials

desc: paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in image upload because ImageServiceImpl.validateStaticImg accepts SVG files, which are then served from the site origin when local storage is used. Authenticated attackers can upload script-bearing SVG images that execute when victims view them, stealing the non-HttpOnly f-session cookie to hijack accounts.
title: paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 Stored XSS via SVG Image Upload

desc: paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because SeoInjectService embeds user profile text without escaping in an inline JSON-LD script element. Authenticated attackers can add a closing script tag followed by HTML to their profile, executing scripts for visitors of their profile page and stealing the non-HttpOnly f-session cookie.
title: paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 Stored XSS via JSON-LD Profile Description

desc: paicoding commit 766c48b through commit 903adce contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in payment notifications, where NotifyMsgListener inserts the payer's display name unescaped and notify-system-item.html renders it via th:utext. Authenticated attackers can set a malicious display name and start a pending payment on a paid article, executing script in the author's browser when the author views notifications.
title: paicoding commit 766c48b through 903adce Stored XSS via Payment Notifications

desc: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.21.6 to before 4.0.0 and from 4.4.6 until 4.6.4, the /__nuxt_island path hash uses ohash serialization that does not escape quotes in string values or delimiters in object keys, allowing different island-prop tuples to produce the same path. For prerendering, substituted content is written into the generated page only if the crawler reaches a colliding URL before rendering the page with the legitimate props. Separately, a CDN or reverse proxy that keys island responses by path alone can be primed with the colliding response. If the substituted prop reaches v-html, innerHTML, or another unsafe HTML sink, the response can execute script in the application origin; otherwise the impact is content substitution. Applications that do not use server components or NuxtIsland, islands without attacker-influenced string props, and responses not cached by path alone are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
title: Nuxt: Colliding island props can share one `/__nuxt_island` path (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-46342)

desc: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, Nuxt parses a request path beginning with // as a URL host before rendering a page, while Nitro server/middleware and routeRules continue to evaluate the original path. An unauthenticated request such as //x/admin can therefore resolve to the /admin page without route-scoped serverHandlers, server/middleware path checks, redirects, or security headers configured for /admin. API handlers in server/api and server/routes, appMiddleware, page middleware are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
title: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-119200: a leading `//` in the request path bypasses `server/middleware` path checks and server route rules on page routes

desc: GLPI is a free asset and IT management software package. From 9.5.0 until 10.0.27 and 11.0.9, authenticated users could access ITIL followups, tasks, or solutions generated from templates without a read-permission check on the parent ticket, problem, or change. Depending on the template configuration, this could reveal information from parent items the user could not otherwise read. This issue is fixed in versions 10.0.27 and 11.0.9.
title: GLPI: Unexpected access to followups/tasks/solutions generated from templates

desc: envd provides reproducible development environments for humans and agents. In versions starting with 0.3.38 and before 1.3.6, insufficient containment of host-side requirements-file reads in  install.python_packages(requirements=...)  could allow access to files outside the build context. An attacker able to influence build input could cause file contents interpreted as dependency entries to appear in debug logs or build-step metadata, subject to the envd process’s permissions. Exploitation in version 1.3.5 additionally requires concurrent modification of relevant filesystem paths. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.6.
title: envd: Host file disclosure through requirements path traversal and TOCTOU

desc: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, _payload.json URL generation and the experimental early-404 path use a trailing-slash regular expression whose work grows quadratically with a long run of slash characters. An unauthenticated request can synchronously occupy the Node.js event loop and delay other requests when server-side rendering uses isr, swr, or cache route rules, or when experimental.early404 is enabled. Applications without those route rules and without experimental.early404, fully prerendered applications, and client-only applications are unaffected; the impact is limited to availability. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
title: Nuxt payload URL generation has quadratic cost for repeated slashes in the request path

desc: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.0.0 until 4.6.4, Nuxt wraps non-HTTP errors thrown during server rendering with createError and incorrectly treats the result as an error deliberately exposed by the application. In production, the error page payload (__NUXT_DATA__) and JSON error response can therefore disclose the original message and data, including an upstream $fetch URL, query-string secrets, response bodies, database hosts, or similar sensitive details, regardless of what a custom error.vue renders. Errors deliberately created with createError or showError, errors returned by useFetch or useAsyncData, and server/api routes are not affected because their client-visible behavior is intentional or follows a different path. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
title: Nuxt exposes the message and data of unhandled errors thrown during server rendering

desc: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. Nuxt from 3.0.0 until 4.6.4, @nuxt/nitro-server from 3.20.0 until 4.6.4, and @nuxt/vite-server from 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, routeRules matching leaves an encoded slash (%2F) in the request path while a catch-all page such as app/pages/[...slug].vue or a custom multi-segment page route decodes it into a route parameter. The getRouteRules result is therefore incomplete, and an unauthenticated request can render the page without the redirect, headers, proxy, SSR, noScripts, appMiddleware, or appLayout rules configured for the decoded path. Protected content is resolved only when the page interprets the decoded parameter accordingly: a custom multi-segment parameter can contain the decoded path, while a repeatable catch-all must join the slash-containing array element; route.path remains encoded and does not resolve that resource. Static pages, single-segment parameters, server/api handlers, and server/routes handlers are not affected because they do not have the same encoded-path mismatch. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
title: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for GHSA-6gq8-jgmh-3ffp: an encoded slash (`%2F`) in the request path bypasses route rules on catch-all page routes

desc: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From @nuxt/webpack-builder 3.0.0 and @nuxt/rspack-builder 3.12.2 until 4.6.4, the development middleware trusts Origin, Referer, or Sec-Fetch-Site when the Host header names the same attacker-controlled hostname. After DNS rebinding changes that hostname to a loopback address, a malicious page opened by a developer can read /_nuxt/*.js client chunks and inline source maps, exposing compiled application source, local filesystem paths, and developer-controlled values embedded in the client bundle. The attacker must know or guess the development-server port and induce the developer to open the malicious page; Chrome 142 and later and other Chromium-based browsers that enforce Local Network Access restrictions prompt before a public page can reach the loopback address. The default Vite builder and production builds are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
title: @nuxt/webpack-builder and @nuxt/rspack-builder dev server serves built source to DNS rebinding pages

desc: rails-html-sanitizer is responsible for sanitizing HTML fragments in Rails applications. From 1.0.3 through 1.7.1, Rails::HTML::PermitScrubber checks SVG href and xlink:href local references with a pattern whose line-start anchor and whitespace class cause an all-whitespace value to be rescanned from each line start. An attacker who supplies HTML can cause quadratic CPU consumption when an application customizes its allowed tags to include an SVG reference element such as use and permits href or xlink:href. The default allowed tag configuration is not affected. CRuby 3.2 and later uses linear-time regular expression matching for this pattern, while CRuby 3.1 and earlier and JRuby are affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.2.
title: rails-html-sanitizer: Possible regular expression denial of service with certain configurations

desc: rails-html-sanitizer is responsible for sanitizing HTML fragments in Rails applications. Before 1.7.2, the HTML4 and HTML5 variants of Rails::HTML::SafeListSanitizer reuse one Rails::HTML::PermitScrubber across calls and mutate its tags and attributes without synchronization. In a multithreaded process, concurrent sanitize calls using different tags: or attributes: options can interleave and cause one call to use the other call's allowlist. If a permissive call admits a script element or event-handler attribute, output expected to be sanitized under a stricter policy can retain it and cause cross-site scripting when rendered. Applications that are single-threaded, use one identical allowlist everywhere, or provide a separate scrubber: are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.2.
title: rails-html-sanitizer: Possible XSS via shared scrubber state in concurrent calls

desc: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.5.0 until 4.6.4, Nuxt can choose a parent directory as the default workspaceDir in either of two cases: a stray parent lockfile when the project is outside a Git repository and has no workspace file above it, or a parent pnpm or Deno settings file that does not declare packages or a workspace, including when the project is inside a Git repository. When the development server is reachable from an untrusted network, Vite permits /_nuxt/@fs/ requests beneath that widened directory, allowing unauthenticated clients to read files such as credentials and SSH keys. The issue affects the development server only; production builds and projects whose parent directories contain no qualifying files are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
title: Nuxt dev server serves files from a parent directory that contains a lockfile

desc:
Relative Path Traversal, with Unintended Proxy vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



A caller of the MCP endpoint can invoke endpoints the OpenAPI document
never declared, under the declared tool's HTTP method, using the credentials the
Route adds. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.19.0 before 3.20.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache APISIX: openapi-to-mcp tool call can reach an API path the document does not declare

desc: Dental practice sites hosted with iDentalSoft send a JSON response to any user who loads certain pages containing sensitive information, including OAuth credentials, password hashes, and PII. Fixed in iDentalSoft 14.0.3.
title: iDentalSoft website information exposure

desc: Catalis/Patriot Properties WebPro 5.0 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries against the underlying MSSQL database, enabling exfiltration of sensitive property and  taxpayer information.
title: Catalis WebPro SQL Injection

desc:
Authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



On a route where multi-auth falls back from wolf-rbac to another successful authenticator, client-supplied Wolf identity headers can remain in the request. A downstream service that relies on those documented headers may therefore receive an identity that was not established by the successful authenticator.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.8.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache APISIX: Multi-auth preserves client-supplied Wolf identity headers

desc:
Authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



On routes using jwe-decrypt with strict: false and a
forward_header distinct from the token header an unauthenticated
client can supply the value the upstream treats as gateway-decrypted
plaintext. Similar can happen when forward-auth is configured with allow_degradation: true, and the auth service is unavailable.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.18.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache APISIX: jwe-decrypt and forward-auth may pass a client-supplied identity header

desc:
Interpretation Conflict, resulting in (Incorrect Authorization) vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



An unauthenticated client can reach upstream paths protected
by a route-level auth plugin when a route without auth exists on the
same upstream and the upstream does not collapse encoded dot segments.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 0.9 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache APISIX: Route-level authentication bypass via path normalization mismatch between routing and upstream forwarding

desc:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



An authenticated user who holds any one of a route's required permissions or scopes can reach the protected upstream without the others, including HTTP methods the authorization server denied.



This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 1.4.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache APISIX: authz-keycloak authorization scope mismatch

desc:
Authentication bypass by spoofing vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



When a Route's configured headers carry a caller identity and the OpenAPI document declares
the same header, a caller can act as another identity against the
upstream API. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.19.0 before 3.20.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache APISIX: identity spoofing in openapi-to-mcp

desc:
Interpretation Conflict, leading to Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache APISIX.



With match_uri_encoded_slash enabled and skip_mtls_uri_regex
configured, a client without a certificate can reach an upstream
behind a route that requires one, limited to request paths that decode
to an exempted URI. This issue affects Apache APISIX: from 3.18.0 through 3.19.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.20.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache APISIX: unauthorized access to mTLS protected resources

desc: A flaw was found in dnf5daemon-server. Unauthenticated D-Bus methods pass caller-controlled URL or .rpm path patterns into a root-privileged cmdline package loader that may store fetched content in a world-readable cache without size limits, or open local paths as root, allowing a local attacker to disclose privileged content and to deny service via disk exhaustion.
title: Dnf5: dnf5daemon-server: dnf5daemon-server: unauthenticated privileged cmdline package fetch/open via add_cmdline_packages

desc: A prompt injection vulnerability in all versions of Jet Admin Cloud Platform allows a remote attacker with a free account to expose sensitive .env configuration files and exfiltrate critical credentials. Mitigated via sandbox component around October 29, 2026.
title: Jet Admin cloud platform prompt injection

desc: Indico is a feature-rich event management system. Prior to version 3.3.14, due to a path traversal vulnerability when building an "offline copy" of an event, a malicious event manager has the ability to retrieve the content of any local file that's readable by the user running Indico on the server. This issue has been patched in version 3.3.14.
title: Indico: Local file disclosure through offline-copy path traversal

desc: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can submit an error-based extractvalue payload through personsSort to leak database information, such as the MariaDB version, via the user and space listing pages.
title: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 SQL Injection via personsSort Session Value

desc: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge the shared-calendar iCal share token by deriving md5Id() from predictable fields such as object creation time, which is self-disclosed through autorDate and the iCal CREATED field. Attackers can compute the creation minute and forge the md5Id token to access and read a shared calendar's iCal feed without authorization.
title: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 Predictable Share Token via md5Id

desc: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge privileged actions such as administrator user creation by merging $_GET and $_POST parameters without requiring an anti-CSRF token. Attackers can craft a malicious link or auto-navigating page that issues a plain GET request, exploiting the lack of CSRF protection and SameSite=Lax cookie behavior on top-level navigations to create unauthorized administrator accounts.
title: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 CSRF via Administrator Account Creation

desc: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private calendar data by exploiting a missing dateCrea value that causes the md5Id token to collapse to md5(calendarId.userId), both small enumerable integers. Attackers can compute valid tokens and request the misc&action=DisplayIcal endpoint with a forged md5Id to read any user's private calendar events without authentication.
title: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 Predictable Token Information Disclosure via DisplayIcal

desc: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to redirect users to arbitrary external URLs by manipulating the objUrl parameter in Ctrl.php's redir() function. Attackers can craft login links with objUrl set to a malicious site, causing the application to issue an HTTP 302 redirect to that external URL, which can be abused for phishing and credential theft.
title: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 Open Redirect via objUrl Parameter

desc: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious HTML markup by controlling imported directory data or an uploaded CSV file, as values are rendered into table cell text and value attributes after only Txt::utf8Encode() with no HTML escaping in VuePersonsImportExport.php. Attackers can craft a CSV cell containing an attribute-breakout payload that is rendered verbatim and executed in the browser of the administrator performing the import, leading to arbitrary script execution in the administrative context.
title: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 Stored XSS via CSV Import Preview

desc: Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to access another user's private mail by supplying a crafted reloadMailTypeId parameter to Ctrl::getCurObj() without a readRight() ownership check in CtrlMail.php. Attackers can manipulate the mail identifier value, such as reloadMailTypeId=mail-1, to retrieve the title and body of private messages belonging to other users, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive communications.
title: Omnispace Agora Project 26.10.0 IDOR via reloadMailTypeId Parameter

desc: MRBS before 1.13.0 contains an LDAP injection vulnerability in web/lib/MRBS/Auth/AuthLdap.php that interpolates unescaped login usernames into DN search and group-membership filters. Attackers with valid directory credentials outside the required group can submit crafted usernames that make the group filter always true, bypassing access restrictions.
title: MRBS before 1.13.0 LDAP Injection via AuthLdap.php Authentication Filter

desc: MRBS before 1.13.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject spreadsheet formulas because the escape() function in web/report.php fails to neutralize leading formula characters. Attackers can store formulas in booking names, descriptions or custom fields that execute when privileged users open exported CSV reports, enabling data exfiltration or command execution via DDE.
title: MRBS before 1.13.0 CSV Formula Injection via Report Export

desc: MRBS before 1.13.0 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect reset links by forging the Host header when $url_base is unset. Attackers can request a reset for a victim so AuthDb::notifyUser() emails a link pointing to their host, capturing the reset key when opened to take over accounts including administrators.
title: MRBS before 1.13.0 Password Reset Poisoning via Host Header Injection

desc: picoquic before 2026.11.05.3e2e3d3 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in picoquic_decode_time_stamp_frame() that allows remote QUIC peers to corrupt stored timestamps by sending oversized TIME_STAMP values. Attackers on connections negotiating the TIME_STAMP extension can send large values shifted by ack_delay_exponent to wrap the result, corrupting RTT and bandwidth estimation and degrading congestion control.
title: picoquic before 2026.11.05.3e2e3d3 Integer Overflow via TIME_STAMP Frame Decoder

desc: SQLBot through 1.10.3 contains a weak password hashing vulnerability that stores local account passwords in sys_user.password as unsalted MD5 digests via md5pwd() in security.py. Attackers who obtain the user table can recover passwords, including administrator passwords, using precomputed tables or GPU cracking, since identical passwords produce identical hashes.
title: SQLBot through 1.10.3 Weak Password Hashing via Unsalted MD5

desc: Goose CLI 1.35.0 before 1.53.0 contains a local code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands by setting diff.external in a repository's .git/config. Attackers can ship a crafted repository that, when the victim runs goose review, executes git diff without --no-ext-diff, running commands as the user and exposing credentials and provider API keys.
title: goose CLI 1.35.0 before 1.53.0 Command Execution via goose review diff.external

desc: AiSOC 12.1.0 before 23.3.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to query the enrichment service through Next.js console rewrite routes. Attackers can send requests to /api/v1/enrichment/lookup or /api/v1/enrichment/bulk to retrieve threat-intelligence results and set force to true to consume commercial provider API quota.
title: AiSOC 12.1.0 before 23.3.0 Missing Authentication via Enrichment Console Proxy Routes

desc: agent-device from 0.21.36 before 0.21.37 contains a local file disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated remote callers to read daemon-host files by opening file:// URLs. Attackers can send an open command with a file:// target through /rpc, then issue snapshot to read any plaintext file readable by the daemon account.
title: agent-device 0.21.36 Local File Disclosure via file:// Navigation in Open Command

desc: Gameyfin before 2.6.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass login-required mode by calling Hilla endpoints annotated with @AnonymousAllowed. Attackers can POST to synchronous endpoint methods such as GameEndpoint.sync, which LiveSubscriptionSecurity never checks, to retrieve game catalog metadata, libraries, platforms, plugins and game requests.
title: Gameyfin before 2.6.2 Missing Authorization in Hilla Endpoints

desc: C-Kermit 11.0.506 before 11.1.515 contains a RECEIVE CONFIRM bypass vulnerability that allows malicious Kermit servers to write unrequested files without prompting by abusing recursive GET root computation in ckcfns.c. Attackers can send files such as .ssh/authorized_keys or shell startup files under the current directory, which rq_under_root() accepts silently, enabling persistent access or code execution.
title: C-Kermit 11.0.506 before 11.1.515 RECEIVE CONFIRM Bypass via Recursive GET

desc: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 contains a path traversal vulnerability in doftpget() in ckcftp.c that allows malicious FTP servers to write files outside the intended directory. Attackers can return absolute paths, tilde names, or dot-dot components in NLST or MLSD listings during MGET /RECURSIVE to overwrite files like .bashrc, leading to code execution.
title: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 Path Traversal via FTP MGET /RECURSIVE

desc: C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in tn_snenv() in ckctel.c that allows malicious Telnet servers to corrupt client memory via crafted NEW-ENVIRON SEND subnegotiation. Malicious or machine-in-the-middle servers can send oversized variable names before authentication, overflowing a 16-byte stack buffer and a miscomputed heap buffer to corrupt stack and heap memory.
title: C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 Buffer Overflow via Telnet NEW-ENVIRON Negotiation

desc: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in getreply() in ckcftp.c that allows malicious FTP servers to overwrite client memory by sending overlong security replies. Attackers controlling or intercepting an FTP server can send long PBSZ replies after AUTH TLS, or long ADAT replies in GSSAPI, Kerberos 4, and SRP builds, overflowing the static reply_buf with attacker-controlled bytes.
title: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 FTP Client Buffer Overflow via PBSZ and ADAT Replies

desc: C-Kermit before 11.1.515 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows remote clients to execute shell commands by supplying unquoted arguments to REMOTE WHO or REMOTE SPACE. Attackers can append shell metacharacters to arguments passed through WHOCMD or SPACM2 to syscmd(), executing commands on the server host even when DISABLE HOST is set.
title: C-Kermit before 11.1.515 OS Command Injection via REMOTE WHO and REMOTE SPACE

desc: C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows Kermit clients to run shell commands on servers with host commands disabled by abusing REMOTE QUERY evaluation. Attackers can send a REMOTE QUERY invoking the command function, or define a macro via REMOTE ASSIGN and call execute to reach RUN, bypassing the nopush restriction and DISABLE HOST.
title: C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 Command Execution via REMOTE QUERY

desc: C-Kermit before 11.1.515 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in putsrv() in ckcfns.c that allows malicious peers to write past the srvcmd buffer by sending crafted packets. Attackers can use Kermit repeat-count compression in server command, GET, or file-header packets to write attacker-chosen bytes beyond the heap buffer on servers or receiving instances.
title: C-Kermit before 11.1.515 Heap Buffer Overflow via putsrv() Packet Decoding

desc:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.3, ABAC-enabled deployments match `ROUTE` access rules against the fully decoded request path, while the router routes on the raw, still encoded path. An encoded slash (`%2F`) inside a path value is a segment separator for the access check but part of the value for the router, so a request can match a narrow `ROUTE` rule while the handler returns a different, larger resource.



An authenticated caller whose rules grant READ only on parts of a resource can therefore read the whole resource. In the DPP API, a rule such as `/v1/dpps/*/elements/*`, meant to grant only passport elements, also grants the complete passport whose identifier contains `/elements/`. In the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment, a rule such as `/submodels/*/submodel-elements/*/attachment`, meant to grant only file attachments, also grants the complete element whose stored idShort contains `%2F`.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.4.

C-Kermit from 7.0.197 before 11.1.515 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the IKSD SSL build that leaves Telnet authentication state at AUTH_VALID after a refused certificate login. Attackers holding a trusted certificate mapped to a refused account can log in as any other account with any password, gaining that account's shell access.
title: C-Kermit 7.0.197 before 11.1.515 IKSD Authentication Bypass via Refused Certificate Login

desc: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability that allows machine-in-the-middle attackers to impersonate Telnet servers because ssl_reply() never calls ssl_check_server_name(). Attackers can refuse START-TLS, offer Telnet AUTHENTICATION SSL, and present any trusted CA certificate to capture user credentials and session data.
title: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 Missing Hostname Verification in AUTHENTICATION SSL

desc: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 contains an improper certificate hostname validation vulnerability that allows attackers to impersonate hosts by abusing wildcard matching in dNSName_cmp() in ck_ssl.c. Attackers holding a trusted certificate with over-matching names containing asterisks, question marks, brackets, or empty labels can intercept credentials and data over Telnet, FTP, and HTTP TLS connections.
title: C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 Improper Certificate Hostname Matching via dNSName_cmp

desc: C-Kermit from 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 contains a file collision protection bypass that allows malicious senders to append data to existing files by marking transfers as RESEND. The gattr() function in ckcfn3.c clears the REJECT discard flag and switches to APPEND without a RECEIVE CONFIRM prompt, letting attackers modify files such as shell startup files.
title: C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 File Collision Protection Bypass via RESEND

desc:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming requests.

The streaming read clause of GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.Handler.info/3 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy/handler.ex) asks Cowboy for up to 8,000,000 bytes per read and compares the running total with max_body_size only after the read returns. The gRPC length prefix of a message is not checked before the message is buffered. Each stream can therefore buffer up to one full read beyond the configured limit before it is refused, and many concurrent streams exhaust node memory. Releases before 1.0.6 apply no limit to streaming requests at all.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.
title: Streaming request body limit enforced only after an 8 MB read in elixir-grpc grpc_server

desc:
Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to occupy a BEAM scheduler indefinitely via a client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming request whose body ends inside a gRPC message.

GRPC.Server.Adapters.Cowboy.read_stream/1 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server/adapters/cowboy.ex, and the Cowboy adapter in grpc before the package split) asks for more data whenever the buffer does not hold a complete message. Once the request body has ended, every further read returns an empty chunk, so the buffer never changes and the function retries without end. A single 5-byte length prefix sent with END_STREAM keeps one scheduler busy for as long as the connection stays open, and repeated requests exhaust all schedulers.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0; grpc: from 0.3.1 before 1.0.0.
title: CPU exhaustion via a truncated gRPC message on streaming RPCs in elixir-grpc grpc_server

desc: The pREST database REST API in Zenitel Connect firmware before 1.11.0 signs and verifies JWTs with the platform CA private key, which is stored on a data volume shared between containers, and sets the PostgreSQL session role from the unvalidated sub claim of each request while connected to the database as the "postgres" superuser, which allows local attackers who can read the platform CA private key from the container filesystem to execute database operations as the PostgreSQL superuser, including reading the master encryption key and password hashes, via a forged JWT with sub=postgres sent to the pREST API.
title: Zenitel Connect pREST API adopts arbitrary PostgreSQL role from unvalidated JWT sub claim

desc: The host configuration watcher in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 applies a rsyslog configuration file written to a data volume that is shared with the hiatus application container, which allows local attackers with write access to the hiatus container filesystem to execute arbitrary OS commands as root on the host operating system via a crafted rsyslog configuration file.
title: Zenitel Connect host applies rsyslog configuration written to a volume shared with the hiatus container

desc: OS command injection vulnerability in audio messages API in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary OS commands as root in the hiatus application container via filename parameter to the /api/system/audio_messages endpoint.
title: Zenitel Connect OS command injection in hiatus container via unsanitized filename in audio messages API

desc:
Path traversal in the certificate.deleteCertificate JSON-RPC method (POST /api/rpc) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to delete arbitrary files as root via a relative path (../) in the file_name parameter.



This can be used to cause denial of service or render the device inoperable by removing critical system files, and to weaken device security by removing files such as firewall rules or certificate trust stores.
title: Path traversal in Zenitel turbineweb certificate delete RPC allows arbitrary file deletion as root

desc:
OS command injection in the TFTP provisioning module of Zenitel EdgeAudioClient before 9.6.3.0, and 10.x before 10.1.3.0, on VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root via a crafted DHCP option 66 (TFTP Server Name) value supplied by a rogue DHCP server on the same network segment. The DHCP-supplied value is passed to a shell without sanitization. Devices using DHCP, the default configuration, are affected on every boot and lease renewal.



The same injection is also reachable via the config_update_tftp_server and sw_update_tftp_server configuration fields by an attacker able to modify the device configuration.
title: OS command injection via DHCP option 66 in Zenitel EdgeAudioClient TFTP provisioning

desc:
Path traversal in the certificate upload endpoint (/api/certificate/upload) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to write arbitrary files as root via a crafted filename parameter in a multipart upload request when the type field is set to any value other than https_certificate. In that case, both path validation and certificate content validation are skipped.



This can be escalated to arbitrary code execution as root, for example by overwriting startup scripts or planting SSH keys.
title: Path traversal in Zenitel turbineweb certificate upload allows arbitrary file write as root

desc: Dell PowerStore contains a content-injection vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to display misleading text on the genuine login page for phishing.

RBH Access Technologies Integra32 Security Management System 5.1.11 R5.0 contains an unauthenticated deserialization vulnerability in its deprecated .NET Remoting service, exposed on TCP port 2001 via the AxcvcLt.dll library using BinaryServerFormatterSinkProvider at TypeFilterLevel.Full without requiring authentication. A remote unauthenticated attacker can send a malicious serialized gadget payload (such as a ysoserial.net TypeConfuseDelegate chain) to the IntegraURI object endpoint, or exploit MarshalByRefObject/MarshalByValue unmarshalling for arbitrary file read/write and SMB/NTLMv2 credential coercion, to achieve remote code execution as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and fully compromise the host.
products: rbh access technologies:integra32 security management system
title: RBH Integra32 5.1.11 .NET Remoting Deserialization RCE

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a malformed but non-empty BACnet WriteProperty request can drive the official server demo into a non-terminating request-processing loop with repeated heap-backed side effects. This results in a remote unauthenticated denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption and a non-terminating request path. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: Remote unauthenticated DoS in `Life_Safety_Zone` `PROP_ZONE_MEMBERS` WriteProperty parsing

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, lighting_command_decode in src/bacnet/lighting.c decodes its first field with the bounded apdu_size - apdu_len, but every nested decode in the operation switch is called with the original full apdu_size while the read pointer has been advanced to &apdu[apdu_len]. The leaf decoders bound their reads against the size they are told, so they read up to apdu_len bytes past the end of the caller's buffer, resulting in an out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: Out-of-bounds read in lighting_command_decode (full APDU size passed to nested tag decoders)

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a remote out-of-bounds read exists in the official BACnet client application apps/readpropm in bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6. When readpropm sends a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request to a malicious BACnet/IP peer, the peer can reply with a malformed but structurally valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK that drives the client into a global-buffer-overflow read on the global receive buffer Rx_Buf. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: Remote Global-Buffer-Overflow Read in readpropm via Malformed ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a BACnet/SC peer can trigger a heap out-of-bounds read (up to 3 bytes), pre-authentication, in the BACnet/SC header-option decoder. bvlc_sc_decode_proprietary_option() reads the vendor-id and option-type at fixed offsets [3],[4],[5] before checking the option's declared header length, and the option-list validator never enforces a minimum length for proprietary options. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: Out-of-bounds read in BACnet/SC proprietary header-option decode (bvlc_sc_decode_proprietary_option)

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, there is a remote global-buffer-overflow in the official router-ipv6 application shipped with bacnet-stack, this results in an out-of-bounds write to the global transmit buffer under ASan. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: Remote global-buffer-overflow in apps/router-ipv6/main.c routed APDU forwarding path

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2, a reachable out-of-bounds write exists when encoding the device.address-binding property. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2.
title: BACnet Stack: Global APDU transmit buffer out-of-bounds write in device.address-binding response encoding via address_list_encode()

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, the bsc_node_parse_urls() function in src/bacnet/datalink/bsc/bsc-node.c contains three distinct bugs when parsing space-separated WebSocket URIs from a BACnet/SC Address Resolution ACK message. Two bugs cause out-of-bounds writes past the utf8_urls[10][129] array in the static BSC_ADDRESS_RESOLUTION structure. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: Buffer overflows in bsc_node_parse_urls() (BACnet/SC Address Resolution ACK URL parser)

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the BACnet stack's ReadPropertyMultiple (RPM) handler. When processing a malformed RPM request packet that lacks the expected closing tags, the function handler_read_property_multiple enters an infinite loop. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: Denial of Service (Infinite Loop) in handler_read_property_multiple via malformed RPM requests

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, there is a library-level memory safety issue that is reachable from an unmodified official sample server (apps/server-basic/main.c) over BACnet/IP resulting in a stack-use-after-return in writable Device string properties. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
title: BACnet Stack: bacnet_device.c stack-use-after-return in writable Device string properties

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, there is a remotely reachable denial-of-service vulnerability in bacnet-stack affecting the default demo server built from the unmodified apps/server/main.c. This issue has been patched in version 1.5.1.
title: BACnet Stack: Uncontrolled recursion in Timer object writeback path leads to remote server stack overflow

desc: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.2 to before 1.4.5, and 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, a signed fileStartPosition taken from AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile stream-access requests is not validated tightly enough before it reaches the RAM file backends. Practical impact includes: reliable denial of service via process crash, out-of-bounds read that may expose adjacent memory contents, or out-of-bounds write that may corrupt heap memory and destabilize the process. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5 and 1.5.1.
title: BACnet Stack: AtomicReadFile/AtomicWriteFile stream fileStartPosition validation flaw causes out-of-bounds read/write in RAM file backends

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a dnsmasq configuration injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject directives by embedding a newline in the net.set_dhcp leasetime field. Attackers can append address= entries via /etc/init.d/dnsmasq to alter DNS answers for LAN clients, or insert invalid lines that stop dnsmasq.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 dnsmasq Configuration Injection via net.set_dhcp

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an option injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject arbitrary pppd options by embedding quotes and newlines in L2TP credentials. Attackers can submit crafted usernames or passwords to the net.set_wan RPC method, which l2tp.sh writes into a pppd options file, adding options like logfile to the root pppd process.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 pppd Option Injection via net.set_wan L2TP Credentials

desc: sysPass 3.0.1 through 3.2.11 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reinstall an already-installed instance by POSTing to the install/install handler, which never checks isInstalled(). Attackers can overwrite config.xml, point the application at an attacker-controlled database, create an administrator account, and plant serialized PublicLink gadget chains triggered via account/viewLink to execute commands.
title: sysPass 3.0.1 through 3.2.11 Unauthenticated Reinstallation RCE via install/install

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by injecting newlines into reboot_time. Attackers can submit a reboot_time value followed by a newline and crontab line, which /etc/init.d/autoreboot writes to the root crontab for crond to run.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Command Injection via Scheduled Reboot Time

desc: In gittuf 0.10.0 through 0.15.0, when a minimum threshold global rule and a policy rule protect the same namespace, verification gives the global rule's check over all trusted users in the policy precedence over the policy rule's own authorized users. A user listed in the policy file but not authorized by the policy rule, or fewer users than the rule's threshold, can make changes to the protected namespace that pass verification.
title: gittuf: Policy rules bypassed in the presence of global rules

desc: @utcp/http before 1.1.14 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows remote manuals to reach loopback services by bypassing the remote-loopback check with a {host} placeholder. Attackers can supply host arguments like 127.0.0.1 or register tools via Streamable HTTP and SSE discovery to access internal services on the agent machine.
title: @utcp/http before 1.1.14 SSRF to Loopback via Host Placeholder in Call Templates

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by uploading crafted OpenVPN private or tls-auth keys. Attackers can close the inline key block with </key>, inject directives such as tls-verify that bypass the .ovpn denylist, and have OpenVPN execute the hook as root.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Root RCE via OpenVPN Key Upload Injection

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a mass assignment vulnerability in the vpn.set_conf App RPC method that allows authenticated administrators to inject arbitrary OpenVPN server options. Attackers can set enabled=1 and a malicious up option in the openvpns object, which the openvpn-hotplug wrapper executes via /bin/sh as root.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Authenticated RCE via vpn.set_conf Mass Assignment

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by injecting newlines into the IPsec keyexchange field of the vpn.set_conf RPC method. Attackers can append a second leftupdown directive to ipsec.conf, which StrongSwan's updown plugin runs as root when an attacker-controlled peer establishes the CHILD_SA.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Command Injection via vpn.set_conf IPsec keyexchange

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to run root commands by importing a malicious OpenVPN client configuration. Attackers can include tls-verify or ipchange directives, which the incomplete denylist does not filter, to execute commands as root when the router connects to an attacker-controlled VPN endpoint.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Root RCE via OpenVPN Configuration Import

desc: In gittuf before 0.18.0, verification of file protection rules uses the quoted, escaped pathnames that Git prints by default for files with special characters (for example non-ASCII characters) instead of the raw paths. Such paths do not match patterns like file:internal/*, so the files are treated as unprotected, and a user who is not authorized by a file protection rule can change a protected file whose name contains special characters and still pass verification.
title: gittuf: File protection rules bypassed for filenames with special characters

desc: In gittuf 0.10.0 through 0.17.0, the verification workflow does not load policy updates that are propagated from an upstream (controller) repository and recorded in the reference state log after the first entry being verified. Only the propagated policy in effect at the start of verification is applied, so later controller changes to global rules, such as threshold requirements and force-push blocks, are ignored and changes that these rules should block pass verification.
title: gittuf: Propagated controller policies not loaded during verification

desc: In gittuf 0.4.0 through 0.16.0, when a policy update appears within the range of reference state log entries being verified, verification checks only the root of trust signatures of the new policy and not the signatures of its other metadata (rule files). A user trusted to push to the repository who bypasses gittuf policy apply and writes the policy reference and reference state log directly can make an invalid policy apply during verification, weakening or strengthening the rules for later changes. The update is still recorded in the reference state log.
title: gittuf: Invalid intermediate policies trusted when the policy apply workflow is bypassed

desc: A flaw in the automatic client-side encryption schema generation of the Mongoid ODM may cause values that an application declared for encryption to be written and stored as cleartext when more than one model is mapped onto the same storage location. No error or warning is raised. A party holding an ordinary read-only database account, with no access to the encryption key material, may then obtain those values in clear form.
title: Mongoid stores encrypted fields in plaintext when two models share a collection

desc: A Ruby object-document mapper does not apply its automatic field-level encryption configuration to certain fields when the data model uses class inheritance. Values the application designated for encryption are written to the database in readable form without any error or warning. A database account holding only read access to the application's collections, and no access to the encryption key store, may obtain those values.
title: Mongoid 9.1.1 incomplete CVE-2026-93764 fix stores descendant-only encrypted fields in plaintext

desc:
Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server and grpc allows an attacker to make a handler act on a resource other than the one named in the URL of an HTTP-transcoded route, via a request with a gRPC Content-Type.

Only the transcoding clause of GRPC.Server.do_handle_request/4 (grpc_server/lib/grpc/server.ex, and lib/grpc/server.ex before the package split) applies the route's path bindings to the request message. The Cowboy handler picks that clause from the request Content-Type, not from the route. A request to a transcoded URL with application/grpc or application/grpc-web is decoded from the body alone, so every path-bound field takes its value from the body. A gateway, proxy rule or WAF that authorizes on the URL path sees one resource while the handler receives another.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0; grpc: from 0.8.0 before 1.0.0.
title: Path bindings ignored for gRPC Content-Types on transcoded routes in elixir-grpc grpc_server

desc:
Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_server allows a client to stall all later calls on a shared HTTP/2 connection via calls that the server refuses while their DATA frames are in flight.

The stream handler grpc_stream_h (grpc_server/src/grpc_stream_h.erl) requests flow from Cowboy only for request data that has arrived. When the server refuses a call early, for example because the body exceeds max_body_size or the method is not implemented, Cowboy drops the DATA frames still in flight for that stream. Their bytes are not returned to the connection flow-control window. After enough refused calls the window is empty. No call on that connection can then send a request body, and each call waits until its deadline. Other connections are not affected.

This issue affects grpc_server: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.
title: Refused calls drain the HTTP/2 connection flow-control window in elixir-grpc grpc_server

desc:
Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_core and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via a compressed Erlang external term in a gRPC message body.

GRPC.Codec.Erlpack.decode/2 (grpc_core/lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex, and lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex before the package split) passes the message body to :erlang.binary_to_term/2. That function inflates a compressed term in full before it returns. The codec sets no limit on the decoded size, and its type checks run only on the decoded term. The server's max_body_size limit counts the compressed bytes of the request. A request with Content-Type: application/grpc+erlpack can therefore make the server allocate a term much larger than the request body.

This issue affects grpc: from 0.4.0 before 1.0.0; grpc_core: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.
title: Memory exhaustion via compressed Erlang terms in the elixir-grpc Erlpack codec

desc: Dell PowerStore contains a SQL Injection vulnerability. An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to disclosure of stored private keys and tampering with trusted certificates.
A buffer overflow in handling EDID Display-Range descriptors in X.Org xwayland before 24.1.15 and X Server before 21.1.26 could be used by malicious monitors to crash the x server or execute cote.
title: X.Org Server EDID DS_RANGES Out-Of-Bounds Write

desc: The web interface in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 loads an integration iframe without sandboxing or origin restrictions, which allows remote attackers to present phishing content to authenticated users via a crafted frame source.
title: Zenitel Connect web interface loads integration iframe without sandboxing or origin restriction

desc: The login flow in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 returns different error responses depending on whether a submitted username exists, which allows remote attackers to enumerate valid user accounts via crafted login requests.
title: Zenitel Connect login allows username enumeration via verbose error responses

desc: The login flow in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 applies per-account lockout on repeated failed login attempts, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (temporary lockout of targeted user accounts from the web interface, repeatable for as long as the attack continues) via repeated failed login requests for a known or guessed username. Intercom call handling is not affected.
title: Zenitel Connect login allows account-lockout denial of service

desc: The web interface in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 serves production JavaScript source maps without authentication, which allows remote attackers to obtain the complete front-end source code, including API usage and internal client logic, via requests for the source map files.
title: Zenitel Connect web interface serves production JavaScript source maps without authentication

desc: Improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts in the WAMP-CRA (challenge-response) authentication path in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 allows remote attackers to guess user passwords via unlimited authentication attempts, because the path, in which the broker issues a challenge and the client returns an HMAC of it keyed with the user's secret, applies no account lockout or rate limiting. Affected releases enforce a password policy of at least 12 characters including upper-case, lower-case, numeric and special characters, so practical exploitation requires a reused or predictable password rather than exhaustive guessing. The WAMP-CRA authentication path is removed in 1.11.0.
title: Zenitel Connect missing lockout and rate limiting on the WAMP-CRA authentication channel

desc: Dell PowerStore contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. An authenticated user with limited privileges could potentially exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to privilege escalation to root on the appliance.

Huatian Dynamic OA8000 collaborative office system contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in /OAapp/jsp/trace/ntkodownload.jsp, where the filename request parameter is used to locate a file without restricting access to an intended directory or rejecting traversal sequences. Attackers can supply ../ sequences to read arbitrary files from the server, such as the Tomcat configuration at ROOT/WEB-INF/web.xml, exposing sensitive configuration, source, and credential material that can enable further compromise. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-11-20.

desc: Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition before 7.5.1 do not require accepted group membership when authorizing deletion of group share-rights. The DELETE /share/right/ endpoint checks for a membership matching the target group, the authenticated user, and share_admin=True, but omits accepted=True. An authenticated remote attacker who has been invited to a group with share-admin privileges, and who knows a group share-right UUID, can therefore delete that group's share-right record without accepting the invitation or after declining it. Pending invitations have accepted=None, while declined invitations retain accepted=False and the share_admin flag. Deletion revokes the group's access to the affected share and its contained secrets for all accepted group members, without deleting the underlying data or disclosing secret contents. The issue was fixed in version 7.5.1 of both editions, released on 2026-10-13.
title: Missing membership acceptance check permits group share-right deletion by invitees in Psono Server

desc:
In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.
products: eclipse foundation:eclipse aas model for java (eclipse aas4j)

desc:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment return Submodel Elements that the caller is not authorized to read from `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/submodel-elements`.



If an access rule grants READ on a single Submodel Element through a `$sme` `REFERABLE` object, the list route returns every element of that Submodel, including its value, as soon as one element matches the caller's rules. The single-element route and the full Submodel read enforce the same rule and deny access to the other elements. An authenticated caller with a READ grant for one element of a Submodel can therefore read all other elements of that Submodel.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306) in the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to read device information, such as the serial number, MAC address, IP address and radio configuration, and to change configuration settings. The service accepts commands in DJI's proprietary DUML protocol without any authentication. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. The same commands are also accepted over the USB operator port. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.
title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: Missing authentication on the management interface

desc:
OS command injection (CWE-78) in the network-configuration handling of the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to execute arbitrary commands as root. Configuration values that can be written without authentication over the management interface are inserted unquoted into shell commands. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. The injected command persists across reboots. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.
title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: OS command injection leads to root code execution

desc:
Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347) in the firmware update handler of the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to install modified firmware, which gives persistent code execution as root. The device accepts any image that matches an MD5 checksum supplied in the same request and does not verify a signature. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. Reproduced by running the unmodified device binaries in emulation; not tested on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.
title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: Firmware updates are not signature-verified

desc:
Use of hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) on the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an attacker with physical access to the board's serial console to log in as root. The same password hash is present on every unit and uses DES crypt, so the password can be recovered offline from the distributed firmware. No network login service accepts this password by default. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.
title: DJI AeroScope Mobile: Hard-coded root password on the serial console

The AVRCP browsing channel's L2CAP receive-buffer callback, browsing_avrcp_l2cap_alloc_buf() in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/avrcp.c, allocated from the shared avctp_browsing_rx_pool with K_FOREVER. L2CAP invokes that callback from the Bluetooth RX work queue thread (bt_workq, "BT RX WQ"), both for the head buffer of a new SDU and — through l2cap_br_alloc_frag() and net_buf_append_bytes() — for every further fragment of a reassembled SDU. That same thread is the only context that ever releases these buffers, after bt_l2cap_br_recv_seg() delivers a completed SDU and calls net_buf_unref(), so a wait taken there can never be satisfied.

The pool holds CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN + 1 buffers of CONFIG_BT_AVRCP_BROWSING_L2CAP_MTU bytes (two buffers of 339 bytes in the default configuration). A connected browsing peer can drain it because bt_l2cap_br_recv_seg() in subsys/bluetooth/host/classic/l2cap_br.c accepts the SDU length declared in an SAR_START segment without bounding it by br_chan->rx.mtu: a peer that announces a large SDU and then streams continuation segments forces one pool buffer per segment-worth of data. Once the pool is empty the next allocation blocks forever inside the callback.

Triggering the flaw requires a build with CONFIG_BT_CLASSIC and the experimental CONFIG_BT_AVRCP_BROWSING option, an application that registers AVRCP callbacks, and a BR/EDR peer that has established the AVRCP control channel and then the browsing channel, which requires an encrypted (paired) link. No malformed packet is needed — a few hundred bytes of ordinary segmented L2CAP traffic suffice.

The consequence is a permanent hang of the whole Bluetooth host, not just of AVRCP: the blocked thread drains bt_dev.rx_queue for all HCI ACL data and low-priority events and also runs the host's internal work items, so all connections stop being serviced and the state is unrecoverable without a reboot. There is no memory-corruption or information-disclosure component. The fix allocates with K_NO_WAIT, so an empty pool now yields a local-busy indication or a channel disconnect that the application can recover from.
title: Bluetooth Classic AVRCP browsing channel can deadlock the Bluetooth receive thread, hanging the host

desc: Dell PowerStore contains an authorization bypass vulnerability. An authenticated administrator could exploit this vulnerability to bypass multi-approver controls on critical operations.
