In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment do not apply an access rule's `FILTERLIST` fragment filters to single Submodel reads.



`GET /submodels` removes the fields that a rule's `FILTERLIST` hides, but `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}` and `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$metadata` return them unfiltered. An authenticated caller with READ access to a Submodel can therefore read fields that the access rules hide from them, for example `supplementalSemanticIds` keys that name the other parties allowed to read the Submodel.



If versioning is enabled (`history.mode` set to `api` or `audit`), `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$history` and `GET /shells/{aasIdentifier}/$history` in the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment return the complete stored version without applying the rule's formula or fragment filters. A caller whose rules grant READ on these routes can read fields that the access rules hide, and Submodels and Asset Administration Shells that the direct read does not return to them at all.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

P-Net before 1.0.4 aborts the Application Relationship of an RPC session when a fragment of a response has been resent without being acknowledged, without checking that the session has an Application Relationship. A request for an existing Application Relationship that is sent on another activity than its Connect, and gets a fragmented response, is handled on a session without one. If the response is not acknowledged, a NULL pointer is dereferenced and the device crashes. A conformant IO-controller does not send such requests. The attacker must have observed the AR UUID of an established Application Relationship and requires ADJACENT network access.
title: NULL pointer dereference when a response fragment is not acknowledged

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the number of MCR request blocks in a Connect request against the number of multicast communication relations that an Application Relationship has room for (PNET_MAX_MC_CR, 1 by default). Each further block is written past the end of the array, into the rest of the Application Relationship and, with more blocks, into the following one. The written data comes from the request. No established Application Relationship is needed, and the attacker requires ADJACENT network access. Builds with PNET_OPTION_MC_CR disabled are not affected.
title: Out-of-bounds write with too many MCR blocks in a Connect request

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 releases the Application Relationship of an RPC session, without the abort procedure, when a fragment of a request has another data representation (endianness) than the first fragment of the call. The application is not told that the Application Relationship is gone, the cyclic data stops, and the resources of the Application Relationship are left referencing a cleared structure. Another host can then connect in its place. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can do this with one PDU.
title: Fragment with another data representation releases an Application Relationship

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 keeps the RPC session that is allocated for a fragment of a request with an unknown activity UUID, without a timeout, when the rest of the request never arrives. A session that does not get an Application Relationship is also kept after the response. Repeated fragments or requests with different activity UUIDs exhaust the available sessions, one UDP packet per session. Once they are exhausted the device no longer answers a Connect request until it is restarted. An unauthenticated attacker with ADJACENT network access can use this to cause a denial of service.
title: RPC session pool exhausted by unfinished fragmented requests

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 routes a received RTA alarm frame to an Application Relationship using only the destination alarm reference in the frame, without checking the source of the frame. A host with ADJACENT network access can abort an established Application Relationship with a single alarm ERROR frame, or deliver forged alarm notifications with chosen type, slot, subslot, USI and payload to the application.
title: Alarm frames are accepted from any source address

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 copies the IP suite of a DCP Set request to the current and the non-volatile configuration, and starts saving it, before the state of the device is checked. If the request is refused, for example because an Application Relationship is active, the configuration is not restored and is still saved. After a restart the device uses the refused address, and may not answer the controller or may use its address. A host with ADJACENT network access can use this while an Application Relationship is active.
title: A DCP Set of the IP suite that is refused is still stored

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user record index against the size of the record block header. The 32-bit length is reduced by the header size before it is passed to the record handlers, so a length smaller than the header underflows and the handlers receive a data length of about 65530. The fixed-size reads of the I&M and PDPort handlers can then read past the end of the session buffer. The result of the write is discarded. The attacker must have an established Application Relationship or be able to send in the context of one, and requires ADJACENT network access.
title: Integer underflow of the record data length in IODWrite requests

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 sets the alarm receiver state to waiting for confirmation before the data of a received alarm notification is parsed. If the parsing fails the state is not restored, and later alarm notifications of the same priority are discarded without acknowledge until the Application Relationship is released. The Application Relationship and the cyclic data exchange keep working. The attacker must be able to send an alarm notification in the context of an established Application Relationship and requires ADJACENT network access.
title: Alarm receiver stops delivering alarms after a malformed alarm notification

desc: P-Net before 1.0.4 finds the RPC session of a received PDU by its activity UUID only, and a reject, fault or cancel PDU for the session aborts the Application Relationship, without checking that the PDU is the answer to a call of the device or where it comes from. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can abort the Application Relationship with one PDU. It also allocates a session for an unknown activity UUID and changes the address stored for an existing session.
title: RPC reject, fault and cancel PDUs abort an Application Relationship

desc: In FRRouting, bgpd frees the same memory twice when dynamic BGP neighbors disconnect, if the peer-group used by a "bgp listen range" also has a Site-of-Origin configured ("neighbor PG soo"). Each dynamic neighbor shares the peer-group's SoO value instead of getting its own copy, but frees it as its own when the neighbor is deleted, which happens as soon as its connection closes. The first disconnect leaves the peer-group pointing at freed memory, and the second disconnect frees it again, causing bgpd to abort and drop all BGP sessions on the router. Any host whose address falls inside the listen range can trigger this by opening and closing two TCP connections to the BGP port, without sending any BGP message and without knowing the AS number, and can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. If the peer-group has a TCP-MD5 password, only hosts that know the password can trigger it. Two ordinary flaps of legitimate dynamic neighbors have the same effect. Between the two frees, displaying the configuration ("show running-config") or establishing a dynamic neighbor also reads the freed memory, which can crash bgpd after a single disconnect. Only configurations that combine a listen range with a SoO on the same peer-group are affected.
title: frr: bgpd double free of peer-group Site-of-Origin when dynamic neighbors disconnect

desc:
This vulnerability exists in the eMudhra emBridge due to missing authorization checks in the FileBrowser API endpoints. These endpoints perform file system enumeration using the LocalSystem account without adequately validating the requesting caller's authorization. An unauthenticated attacker on the same LAN could exploit this vulnerability by sending malicious webpage to the local HTTPS Web API.

 

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate file and directory names and obtain information about the directory structure of the targeted system. 



The vulnerability however, does not provide access to file contents or permit file modification, deletion, or code execution, or access to cryptographic keys and hardware token PINs.
title: Information Disclosure Vulnerability in eMudhra emBridge

desc: A buffer overread caused by an integer-overflow in Proc/SProcXResQueryClientIds in X.Org xwayland before 24.1.15 and X Server before 21.1.26 could be used by attackers on authenticated X clients to crash the server or leak out information.
title: X.Org Server XRes QueryClientIds Request Size Overflow

desc: Unauthorization vulnerability in the management of workflow definitions in OpenKM Community Edition. The REST endpoints `registerProcessDefinition` and `runProcessDefinition` require authentication but do not verify roles in the WorkflowService or in lower layers. An attacker with the `ROLE_USER` role can register and execute a process definition containing BeanShell scripts, allowing them to execute Java code and operating system commands with the service’s privileges. In the official Docker image, the process runs as root.
title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in OpenKM Community Edition

desc: A buffer overread caused by casting a negative integer to CARD32 in XvQueryImageAttributes in X.Org X Server before 21.1.26 and xwayland before 24.1.15 could be used to causes crashes by authenticated X clients.
title: X.Org Server XvQueryImageAttributes Negative Size Reply

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows a malicious or compromised ACS to execute commands as root by supplying a crafted InternetGatewayDevice.User.{i}.Password value. Attackers can send a SetParameterValues request with shell metacharacters that obuspa_system.lua concatenates into a luci.util.exec() command string, gaining root command execution.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 OS Command Injection via TR-098 User Password Parameter

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root via an unvalidated multipart filename in the CBI FileUpload handler. Attackers can upload a valid OpenVPN configuration file through the VPN client config page with a filename containing $() shell substitution, which is passed through Lua %q to /bin/sh -c.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Command Injection via VPN Configuration Upload Filename

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by storing a malicious WireGuard private key. Attackers can save a private_key containing $() shell substitution and call the vpn.export_conf method on the /cgi-bin/luci/rpc/app JSON-RPC endpoint, which passes the key to a wg pubkey shell command.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Command Injection via vpn.export_conf WireGuard Private Key

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows a malicious or compromised ACS to inject curl options through unfiltered Username and Password values in the easycwmpd Upload handler. Attackers can embed whitespace to add options like -o and --url to the root-run curl command, writing attacker-controlled HTTP responses to arbitrary files on the device.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Curl Argument Injection via TR-069 Upload

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability in luci/model/cbi/vpn/openvpn/client.lua, which embeds the shellquote()-quoted remote host token of an uploaded OpenVPN configuration inside an already single-quoted sed program run by os.execute(), so the nested quotes terminate the outer quote. Authenticated administrators can upload an .ovpn file whose remote host token contains a semicolon to execute arbitrary commands as root.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Command Injection via OpenVPN Client Configuration Upload

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root via the WireGuard server private_key option. Attackers can save a private key containing $() command substitution, which runs when action_wireguards_export() passes it to luci.sys.exec during configuration export.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Command Injection via WireGuard private_key Export

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in the CWMP client that allows a malicious ACS to corrupt stack memory via oversized credentials. Attackers controlling the ACS can send Username and Password values up to 256 bytes in TR-069 Download or Upload requests, overflowing 128-byte stack buffers and crashing the CWMP process.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Stack Buffer Overflow via CWMP Basic Authorization Builder

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an insufficient verification of data authenticity vulnerability in the mt_wifi Smart Mesh Technology (SMT) onboarding, which protects messages only with an AES-CBC key derived from public values and a CRC32 check. Adjacent unauthenticated attackers can forge SMT messages in Probe Request vendor IEs carrying an attacker-chosen SSID and pre-shared key, forcing unpaired devices to join attacker-controlled access points.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 SMT Message Forgery via Probe Request Vendor IE

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the Mosquitto plugin auth_plugin_jwt.so that accepts unsigned JWTs using alg none. Attackers holding any Cudy-trusted client certificate can authenticate as admincudydevice on port 8883 and publish batchcmd requests to execute commands as root.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 MQTT JWT Authentication Bypass via alg none Tokens

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an unauthenticated stack buffer overflow vulnerability in the stun_client TR-111 UDP Connection Request parser that parses requests before verifying username or HMAC. Remote attackers can send a single crafted UDP datagram lacking a space in the request line, causing strncpy() to overflow a 10-byte stack buffer and crash stun_client for denial of service.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Stack Buffer Overflow via stun_client UDP Parser

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in an obuspa getter for the TR-098 WLANConfiguration KeyPassphrase parameter, which copies the stored value with strcpy() into a 4,096-byte stack buffer without a length check. A malicious or compromised ACS can set a 5,000-byte passphrase via SetParameterValues, and a later read of the parameter overflows the buffer and crashes obuspa, causing denial of service.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Stack Buffer Overflow via obuspa KeyPassphrase Getter

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to run root commands by advertising a rogue automesh controller over mDNS. Attackers on the upstream Ethernet segment can advertise _cudycmagent._tcp records pointing to a malicious MQTT broker, then send commands encrypted with a fixed AES key that router/batchcmd.lua executes as root.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 Unauthenticated RCE via mDNS Automesh Broker Adoption

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in slideFormula in lib/utils/shared-formula.js when translating shared formulas to child cells. Attackers can supply a crafted spreadsheet with very long master formulas, such as runs of hyphens, causing quadratic regex backtracking that blocks the Node.js event loop.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 ReDoS via slideFormula Shared Formula Translation

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a resource leak vulnerability in the streaming WorkbookReader.parse that leaves temporary files and open descriptors when sheet parsing fails or iteration stops early. Attackers can repeatedly upload malformed multi-sheet workbooks with worksheets placed before xl/sharedStrings.xml to fill the temporary directory and exhaust file descriptors.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Resource Exhaustion via Streaming WorkbookReader Temporary Files

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a formula injection vulnerability in the totals row formula getter in lib/doc/table.js that fails to escape [, ], # and ' characters in structured reference column names. Attackers can supply column names containing ] via untrusted input like imported CSV headers to inject formulas such as HYPERLINK that exfiltrate cell values when users open and click the generated workbook.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Formula Injection via Table Totals Row Column Names

desc: Dell SmartFabric OS10 Software, versions prior to 10.6.0.10, contains an Improper Access Control vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability in the streaming WorkbookWriter that allows attackers to read local files by supplying crafted image filenames to addImage. Attackers can inject ../ path segments into user-controlled image paths, causing addMedia to embed any file readable by the Node.js process under xl/media in the generated workbook.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Arbitrary File Read via WorkbookWriter addImage Filename

desc: Dell SmartFabric OS10 Software, versions prior to 10.6.0.10, contains an Incorrect Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command execution.

exceljs through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a worksheet col element with an unbounded max attribute. Attackers can craft a small workbook with a huge max value, causing xlsx.load() to allocate hundreds of millions of Column objects and abort the process with an uncatchable heap out-of-memory error.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Memory Exhaustion via Unbounded Worksheet Column Range

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in data-validations-xform.js that allows attackers to exhaust CPU and memory by supplying unbounded sqref ranges. Attackers can provide a small crafted workbook with a sqref of A1:XFD1048576 to make xlsx.load() iterate billions of addresses, blocking the event loop and crashing the process with an uncatchable out-of-memory error.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Denial of Service via Oversized Data Validation sqref

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows attackers to block the event loop by supplying an unbounded sheetId in xl/workbook.xml. Attackers can provide a workbook with a huge sheetId, making the sparse worksheet array walk stall worksheets, getWorksheet and writeBuffer for seconds.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Denial of Service via Oversized Worksheet sheetId

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a workbook with an oversized defined-name range. DefinedNames.addEx expands ranges such as S!$A$1:$XFD$1048576 from xl/workbook.xml cell by cell, causing an uncatchable fatal heap out-of-memory error during xlsx.load().
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Memory Exhaustion via Oversized Defined Name Range

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a workbook with an unbounded image anchor column in the drawing part. Attackers can set an anchor column such as 300000000 in xl/drawings/drawing1.xml so reading getImages() anchor positions makes Worksheet.getColumn allocate millions of Column objects and abort with a heap out-of-memory error.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Memory Exhaustion via Oversized Image Anchor Column

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in Worksheet._parseMergeCells that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying unbounded mergeCell ranges. Attackers can craft a small workbook with a mergeCell ref like A1:XFD1048576, causing xlsx.load() to create billions of Row and Cell objects and abort the process.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Memory Exhaustion via Oversized Merged Cell Range

desc: exceljs through 4.4.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows attackers to block the event loop by supplying unbounded row r attributes parsed in row-xform.js. Attackers can craft an XLSX file with a row numbered far beyond Excel's limit, making getSheetValues(), workbook writes and CSV export consume time proportional to that number.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Denial of Service via Oversized Row Number

desc: listmonk 6.0.0 before 7.0.0-beta.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in doResetPassword that skips TOTP verification after a password reset. Attackers who can complete a reset, such as by reading the victim's reset email, obtain fully authenticated sessions including Super Admin without the TOTP code.
title: listmonk 6.0.0 before 7.0.0-beta.2 2FA Bypass via Password Reset Flow

desc: listmonk 6.2.0 before 7.0.0-beta.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit Azure Event Grid bounce webhooks when no shared secret is configured. Attackers can POST forged EmailDeliveryReportReceived events with Bounced status to /webhooks/service/azure to blocklist, unsubscribe, or delete arbitrary subscribers.
title: listmonk 6.2.0 before 7.0.0-beta.2 Missing Authentication via Azure Bounce Webhook

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in mergeConditionalFormattings that allows attackers to modify Object.prototype by supplying an x14:cfRule id of __proto__. Attackers can craft an xlsx file that, when loaded with xlsx.load(), sets properties such as type, direction, border and cfvo on every object in the process until it restarts.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Prototype Pollution via x14 Conditional Formatting Rule ID

desc: Listmonk 6.0.0 before 7.0.0-beta.2 contains a 2FA bypass vulnerability that allows attackers with a valid password to brute-force TOTP codes because the attempt counter resets on every new password login. Attackers can repeatedly submit credentials to POST /admin/login to obtain fresh tokens, each allowing 15 more guesses, gaining sessions for 2FA-protected accounts including Super Admin.
title: listmonk 6.0.0 before 7.0.0-beta.2 TOTP Brute-Force via /admin/login/twofa

desc: Contao 4.6.0 before 5.3.54, 5.4.0-RC1 before 5.7.17, and 6.0.0-RC1 before 6.0.6 fails to invalidate existing user sessions when two-factor authentication is enabled or disabled. Because Contao\User::isEqualTo() and serialized session data omit two-factor state, attackers already holding a session keep it after the owner changes 2FA settings.
title: Contao before 5.3.54, 5.7.17, and 6.0.6 Session Invalidation Failure on 2FA Change

desc: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability that allows attackers to add numeric keys to Object.prototype through a crafted defined name referencing a __proto__ sheet. Attackers can supply an xlsx whose xl/workbook.xml definedName range targets __proto__, causing CellMatrix to write empty arrays onto Object.prototype process-wide when workbook.xlsx.load() runs.
title: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 Prototype Pollution via __proto__ Defined Name

desc: The xmlwf tool in libexpat through 2.10.0 contains a symlink following vulnerability because -d output mode opens files with fopen("wb"), which follows symbolic links. Local attackers with write access to the output directory can plant a symlink at the expected output name to truncate or overwrite files writable by the xmlwf user.
title: libexpat xmlwf through 2.10.0 Symlink Following via -d Output Directory

desc: Dokploy 0.28.0 before 0.31.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated organization members to read arbitrary files by supplying ../ sequences in the filePath of patch.readRepoFile. Attackers with service read permission can read /etc/shadow, SSH private keys, and secret environment files on the Dokploy host or managed remote servers.
title: Dokploy 0.28.0 before 0.31.1 Path Traversal via patch.readRepoFile

desc: Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because password changes do not revoke existing web sessions. Attackers holding a leaked password or copied session cookie keep access for up to 30 days, reading integration credentials, creating API keys, or registering passkeys.
title: Miniflux before 2.3.5 Insufficient Session Expiration After Password Change

desc: Dokploy 0.28.0 before 0.31.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated organization members to list tracked files of any git repository by supplying an arbitrary repoPath to patch.readRepoDirectories. Attackers with read access to one service can enumerate file and directory names of other tenants' application and compose source trees on the host or managed servers.
title: Dokploy 0.28.0 before 0.31.1 Path Traversal via patch.readRepoDirectories repoPath

desc: Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an unverified password change vulnerability that allows holders of a signed-in session to change the account password without supplying the current password. Attackers with a stolen session cookie or unattended device can submit new password fields via updateSettings to lock out the owner and take over the account.
title: Miniflux before 2.3.5 Password Change Without Current Password via Settings Form

desc: actix-http before 3.20.1 and actix-web before 4.18.2 contain an unbounded decompression vulnerability in encoding::Decoder that lets remote attackers exhaust memory and CPU via compressed bodies. Attackers can send small highly compressed gzip, deflate, Brotli or zstd request bodies to Json, Form, Bytes or String extractors, or serve them to awc clients, causing denial of service.
title: actix-http before 3.20.1 and actix-web before 4.18.2 Decompression Bomb DoS via encoding::Decoder

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in its error pages, which print SCRIPT_NAME-derived URLs built by errors/processor.php without escaping. Unauthenticated attackers can craft links that trigger uncaught exceptions on servers deriving SCRIPT_NAME from the request path, executing script in the storefront origin within victims' browsers.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Reflected XSS via Error Pages SCRIPT_NAME

desc: Scapy before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in BER_num_dec() and BERcodec_OID.do_dec() that allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying oversized OID arcs. Attackers can send ASN.1/BER data with many base-128 continuation bytes to cause quadratic CPU consumption or an uncaught ValueError crash on Python 3.11+.
title: Scapy before 2.8.0 Denial of Service via Quadratic BER OID Decoding

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_sg_proto_del() in src/scenegraph/vrml_proto.c because gf_sg_reset() frees unregistered prototypes still referenced by scene commands. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT/BT scene declaring prototypes via commands, processed by MP4Box -chap, to trigger freed memory access and crash the process.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 Use-After-Free in gf_sg_proto_del During Scene Teardown

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.19.0 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the template filter's {{layout}} directive, which renders arbitrary layout handles without enforcing the admin/block whitelist that the {{block}} directive applies. Administrators with rights to edit email, CMS, widget or newsletter content can embed {{layout}} with arbitrary handles to render disallowed blocks and disclose limited information.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.19.0 Block Whitelist Bypass via {{layout}} Directive

desc: Scapy before 2.8.0 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in the BER/ASN.1 decoder in scapy/asn1/ber.py that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to crash parsing applications. Attackers can send a single 833-byte packet with 250 nested ASN.1 SEQUENCE structures to trigger an unhandled RecursionError, terminating TLS, SNMP, X.509, or LDAP parsers even with safe=True.
title: Scapy before 2.8.0 Uncontrolled Recursion DoS via BER SEQUENCE Decoder

desc: GPAC through 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the MPEG-4 Form spatial-constraint handlers in src/compositor/mpeg4_form.c that lets attackers crash the process via unchecked group lookups. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene whose Form constraints reference a non-existent group, crashing tools like MP4Box during chapter import for denial of service.
title: GPAC through 26.07.0 NULL Pointer Dereference via MPEG-4 Form Handlers

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.x before 21.0.0-beta3 validates OAuth 1.0a oauth_callback URLs with a string-prefix check and falls back to accepting any well-formed URL. Attackers holding a leaked consumer key and secret can supply host-suffix, userinfo, or arbitrary callback URLs to capture an approving administrator's or customer's request token and verifier, then obtain an access token with the victim's API privileges.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 OAuth Callback URL Allowlist Bypass

desc: OpenMage Magento-LTS before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an authorization bypass in the /rss/order/status feed because its URL key is unsigned Base64-encoded JSON of the order, increment, and customer ids. Unauthenticated attackers can forge keys from enumerated sequential ids to read other customers' names, items, prices, totals, and status comments when order-status RSS is enabled.
title: OpenMage Magento-LTS before 20.18.2 Authorization Bypass via Forgeable RSS Order Key

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 lets restricted administrators read decrypted configuration secrets because the store.getConfig email template directive's encrypted-path check missed config.xml-declared paths, case variants of the getConfig method name, and parent paths. Administrators with Transactional Emails access can preview a crafted template to expose PayPal, payment gateway, and carrier credentials.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Information Disclosure via Email Template getConfig

desc: OpenMage Magento LTS before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the admin and storefront OAuth confirm and confirmSimple actions, which accept GET requests without form-key validation. Attackers holding OAuth consumer credentials can lure a logged-in administrator or customer to a crafted confirm URL that authorizes the attacker's request token, then exchange it at /oauth/token for a persistent REST API access token bound to the victim.
title: OpenMage Magento LTS before 20.18.2 CSRF via OAuth Authorization Confirm

desc: OpenMage magento-lts 20.17.0 before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability because the general/file/protected_extensions blocklist omits phar, php8, and phps. Unauthenticated attackers can upload a .phar file through a product File custom option to a predictable media/custom_options path and request it directly to execute code on servers that map .phar to PHP and serve that directory.
title: OpenMage magento-lts 20.17.0 before 20.18.2 Unrestricted File Upload RCE via Custom Options

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta pre-releases before 21.0.0-beta3 generate customer email-confirmation keys with md5(uniqid()) and customer and administrator password-reset tokens with the non-cryptographic uniqHash(). Unauthenticated attackers can brute-force the roughly 20-bit confirmation key via the unrate-limited confirmAction endpoint to log in as pending customers, or predict administrator reset tokens after recovering generator state.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Account Takeover via Predictable Confirmation Key

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because storefront MSRP/MAP popup and Qty Increments notice templates output product names without proper escaping. Attackers with admin product-edit rights can store a malicious product name that executes script when shoppers view product, category, or wishlist pages.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Stored XSS via Product Name in MSRP Popup

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability because admin controllers' _isAllowed() checks fall back to, or only check, parent ACL resources instead of finer per-action permissions. Authenticated restricted administrators can mass cancel or hold orders, rewrite order shipping addresses, export customer report data, or create REST roles despite their role denying those permissions.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Incorrect Authorization in Admin Controllers ACL

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because admin pages render Dataflow profile link variables, tax rate titles, OAuth consumer names, and PayPal certificate filenames without escaping. An administrator restricted to one affected area can store script that runs when another administrator, including a full administrator, opens the page, reading the form key and performing actions with that administrator's privileges.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Stored XSS via Admin Dataflow, Tax, OAuth, PayPal Fields

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 serves RSS feeds with a text/html content type and does not escape feed entry data, leading to stored cross-site scripting. An unauthenticated guest can submit a product review with script in the nickname, title or text that executes when an administrator opens the pending-reviews feed, enabling admin account takeover.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Stored XSS via RSS Review Feed

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 accepts the free (No Payment Information Required) payment method on orders with a non-zero total because the zero-total check runs only when payment data is imported. An API user with cart permissions can select free via cart_payment.method while the total is zero, raise it with cart_coupon.remove, and submit cart.order to place an unpaid full-price order.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Payment Bypass via Free Payment Method

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in Mage_Rss_Model_Resource_Order::getAllCommentCollection(), which omits the is_visible_on_front filter for invoice, shipment and credit-memo comments. Authenticated customers can open the /rss/order/status feed for their order to read internal staff comments, such as fraud-review and payment notes.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Information Disclosure via Order-Status RSS Feed

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.19.0 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a race condition in shopping cart price rule usage limits, because Mage_SalesRule_Model_Validator checks coupon limits without locking and the usage counters are later incremented non-atomically. Unauthenticated attackers, including guest shoppers, can submit concurrent checkouts to redeem a limited coupon more times than its cap allows.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.19.0 Race Condition in Coupon Usage Limits

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.19.0 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in PayPal cancel and decline return handlers that trust only the checkout session without verifying the request came from PayPal. Attackers can lure a shopper into a cross-site GET to paypal/standard/cancel to cancel their recent uninvoiced order, void pending authorizations, and restore items to the cart.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.19.0 CSRF via PayPal Cancel Return Handlers

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in goArray() that allows remote attackers to abort the server process via arrays with null integer-keyed elements. Attackers can send crafted JSON passed to frankenphp_log() or returned from worker callbacks, triggering an unrecovered cgo panic that terminates every vhost and in-flight request.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.0 Denial of Service via goArray Nil Type Assertion

desc: FrankenPHP from 1.5.0 before 1.13.0 contains an incomplete environment sandbox vulnerability in which putenv writes to the process-wide OS environment via os.Setenv, leaking values across concurrent requests. Attackers reaching a request path that spawns child processes with the default environment through proc_open or exec can read secrets such as database passwords set by other requests.
title: FrankenPHP 1.5.0 before 1.13.0 Cross-Request Environment Leakage via putenv

desc: FrankenPHP Docker images before 1.1.11 were rebuilt only when new base image tags were created, so security fixes that Alpine, PHP, and Go applied under existing tags were not propagated. Remote attackers could exploit known flaws in the stale system libraries, such as CVE-2025-15467 in libcrypto3, to execute code.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.1.11 Delayed Propagation of Base Image Security Fixes

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability because Mage_Api_Model_Session::_renewBySessId() never checks api_user.is_active and REST OAuth authorization never checks whether the admin user is active. Attackers holding an existing SOAP/XML-RPC session or OAuth access token retain API access after deactivation or API key rotation, reading and modifying customer, order and catalog data.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Insufficient Session Expiration After API User Deactivation

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.0 contains a path-split interpretation conflict in splitPos in cgi.go that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute protected PHP scripts by embedding .php inside a filename component. Attackers can request paths like /uploads/a.php.txt/b.php to execute uploads/a.php despite route-level or WAF deny rules and forge PATH_INFO, SCRIPT_NAME, and PHP_SELF values.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.0 CGI Path-Split Boundary Bypass via splitPos

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Mage_Catalog_Model_Product_Option_Type_File, which accepts guest SVG, XHTML, or XML uploads through product File custom options with an empty allowed-extension list. Unauthenticated attackers can send the file URL under media/custom_options/ to victims, executing script in the store origin and exposing administrator sessions when the admin panel shares that origin.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Stored XSS via Product Custom Option SVG Upload

desc: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Dataflow profile run page, which inserts catalog product import row errors into the page without escaping. Unauthenticated attackers can place markup in the store, type, or attribute_set columns of an import file to run script in the session of the administrator who imports it.
title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Stored XSS via Dataflow Import Row Errors

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 contains a denial of service vulnerability in worker mode where frankenphp_handle_request() returns false without finishing the dequeued request after a fatal error during request startup. Attackers who trigger startup fatal errors against worker scripts that keep calling frankenphp_handle_request() can leave client requests hanging indefinitely while the worker continues running.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 Pending Worker Request Denial of Service

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in worker mode that leaks per-request environment variables into later requests on the same PHP thread. Attackers can read values set via env directives with request placeholders or WithRequestEnv() through getenv() or $_SERVER, causing applications to act on another user's routing, tenant, or authorization values.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 Information Disclosure via Per-Request Environment Variable Leak

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.2 contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in its PHP-to-Go array converter that fails to detect circular references in PHP arrays. Passing a self-referential array to frankenphp_log() or returning one from a worker callback triggers a fatal Go stack overflow, terminating the entire server process.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.2 Denial of Service via Cyclic Array Conversion

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.2 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows unauthenticated clients to tie up PHP threads because queued requests are not cancelled when clients disconnect. Attackers can send many requests and close connections immediately, forcing handleRequestWithRegularPHPThreads and worker handlers to execute them and delay all clients sharing the thread pool.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.2 Denial of Service via Queued Disconnected Requests

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to spoof trusted headers by sending dot-form header names that PHP rewrites to underscores. Attackers can send headers like X.Authenticated.User or X.Forwarded.For that map to $_SERVER keys, spoofing user identity, client IP, or scheme.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.0 Authentication Bypass via Dot-Form Header Name Aliasing

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows later clients to read earlier clients' libxml errors because worker mode never resets LIBXML(error_list) between requests. Attackers sending requests to the same worker thread can call libxml_get_errors() or libxml_get_last_error() to obtain other clients' parsed-document fragments and server filesystem paths.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.2 Information Disclosure via libxml Error State in Worker Mode

desc: Rustrak before 0.26.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows users with integrations update permission to send requests to arbitrary destinations by supplying routing_override.url to POST /api/integrations/{id}/test. Attackers can target loopback, private-network and cloud metadata addresses with custom headers and redirects followed, reading non-2xx response bodies returned in the API response.
title: Rustrak before 0.26.0 SSRF via Alert Integration Test routing_override.url

desc: FrankenPHP standalone static binaries 1.8.0 before 1.13.2 bundle the PHP brotli extension statically linked with Brotli 1.2.0, whose decoder contains an out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-111497). Unauthenticated remote attackers can send crafted data to applications that pass it to brotli_uncompress_add() to crash the entire FrankenPHP process, and possibly cause memory disclosure or code execution.
title: FrankenPHP 1.8.0 before 1.13.2 Out-of-Bounds Write via Bundled Brotli Decoder

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that leaves a dangling pointer to a freed environment table when putenv() is called during request shutdown. Attackers triggering putenv() in shutdown functions, destructors, or session handlers can crash the process on the next getenv() call or leak previous request environment values.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 Use-After-Free via putenv() During Request Shutdown

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in worker mode that frees internal streams of SplTempFileObject or SplFileObject on php://temp instances surviving across requests. Remote clients can send requests reaching code that uses such persisted objects, causing reads of freed memory that leak garbage data or crash the process.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 Use-After-Free of SplTempFileObject Streams in Worker Mode

desc: Pagelayer 2.1.7 before 2.2.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Abilities API abilities registered in main/abilitiesregister.php that only require the edit_posts capability. Contributor-level attackers can overwrite, publish, delete, or duplicate other users' private posts and pages to read them, and modify site-wide theme templates like headers and footers.
title: Pagelayer 2.1.7 before 2.2.1 Missing Authorization via Abilities API

desc: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 contains a double free vulnerability in worker mode that frees SG(request_info).content_type_dup twice when a worker script ends its loop after a non-form POST request. Unauthenticated attackers can send repeated JSON POST requests until the worker loop ends, aborting the whole process when USE_ZEND_ALLOC=0 is set.
title: FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 Double Free in Worker Mode via Non-Form POST

desc: Ryot before 10.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to take over other users' collections by supplying an updateId to the createOrUpdateCollection GraphQL mutation. Attackers who know a collection id can trigger ownership reassignment without checks, read its items, rewrite metadata, and evict the original owner and collaborators.
title: Ryot before 10.5.6 Authorization Bypass via createOrUpdateCollection updateId

desc: Ryot before 10.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to revoke other users' access links by supplying an arbitrary accessLinkId. Attackers can obtain access link ids from public share URLs and revoke them without ownership checks, breaking shared access for all link users.
title: Ryot before 10.5.6 Authorization Bypass via revokeAccessLink GraphQL Mutation

desc: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, contain an improper path equivalence flaw in VirtualFileFactory.canonicalisePath that bypasses mount-level access policy. Authenticated users can supply paths with duplicate separators or dot segments to route operations to a less restrictive parent mount and read or write files the child mount denies.
title: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, VFS Mount Policy Bypass via Non-Canonical Paths

desc: BuildAdmin 1.0.1 through 2.3.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to store javascript: URLs in the admin operation log via the X-Rewrite-URL header. When an administrator clicks the log entry's url open button, the script runs in the backend origin and steals the adminInfo token from localStorage, enabling account takeover.
title: BuildAdmin 1.0.1 through 2.3.9 Stored XSS via X-Rewrite-URL in Admin Log

desc: Ryot before 10.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to remove entries from other users' collections by supplying arbitrary collectionName and creatorUserId values. Attackers can obtain user ids from the usersList query and target fixed collection names like Watchlist to delete collection_to_entity rows belonging to other users.
title: Ryot before 10.5.6 Authorization Bypass via deployRemoveEntitiesFromCollectionJob

desc: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, contain an authentication bypass vulnerability in SSH public key authentication that reuses cached key authorization decisions across usernames. Attackers holding a key authorized for one account can authenticate it, then send a signed SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_REQUEST with a different username on the same connection to log in as that account.
title: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, SSH Public Key Cross-User Authentication Bypass

desc: 2FAuth before 9.0.1 contains a weak password recovery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to poison reset links by forging the HTTP Host header. Attackers can request password or WebAuthn recovery emails with an attacker-controlled host, capture the victim's token, and take over accounts exposing stored TOTP/HOTP secrets.
title: 2FAuth before 9.0.1 Password Reset Poisoning via Host Header

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 lacks rate limiting on password-reset OTP verification, allowing unauthenticated attackers to brute force 6-digit OTPs. Attackers can initiate a reset and submit unthrottled guesses to the check_otp endpoint, resetting the target's password and taking over the account.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 OTP Brute Force via password_reset/check_otp

desc: Huginn before 2026.11.09 contains an information exposure vulnerability in JqAgent that allows authenticated users to read the server process environment because the jq child process inherits it. Attackers who can create, configure or dry-run a JqAgent can supply a filter using env or $ENV to disclose APP_SECRET_TOKEN, database, SMTP and OAuth secrets.
title: Huginn before 2026.11.09 Information Exposure via JqAgent jq env Builtin

desc: Huginn from 2026.09.09 before 2026.11.09 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability because OutboundProxy.configure! applies the egress proxy only to Faraday and Typhoeus. Authenticated users can configure JiraAgent or WeiboPublishAgent to send HTTParty, open-uri or Net::HTTP requests directly to internal services, with JiraAgent returning response data as events.
title: Huginn from 2026.09.09 before 2026.11.09 SSRF via OUTBOUND_PROXY Bypass

desc: Teable before 2026-10-12T12-45-53Z.3331 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to upload SVG or HTML attachments with an attacker-chosen content type. Attackers can send the same-origin /api/attachments/read URL, served inline with an empty Content-Security-Policy, to run script with the victim's session and perform API actions.
title: Teable before 2026-10-12T12-45-53Z.3331 Stored XSS via Attachment Uploads

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to link pipeline stages to environments of other projects by supplying a foreign project_env_id. Attackers can submit another project's environment identifier to the POST /api/v1/pipeline/{pipeline_id}/stages/ endpoint, persisting cross-project associations that bypass project separation.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Authorization Bypass via Pipeline Stage project_env_id

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated deploy users to define arbitrary Kubernetes hostPath volumes without allow-list or policy checks. Attackers can set the host path to / in the Define HostPath Volume configuration to mount the worker node root filesystem read-write, breaking container isolation and enabling node and cluster compromise.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Container Escape via Unrestricted HostPath Volumes

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users with build configuration permission to read files on the build worker by supplying unvalidated dockerfile_path and build context values. Attackers can set traversal or absolute paths such as /etc/passwd via the CI configuration endpoint, then trigger a build to disclose file contents in the build log.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Path Traversal via Dockerfile Path and Build Context

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read arbitrary files by supplying traversal sequences in Additional Manifest file paths. Attackers can enter paths like ../../../../etc/passwd so the renderer embeds file contents in generated manifests and logs, exposing configuration files and service-account tokens.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Path Traversal via Additional Manifest Rendering

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to attach another application's environment to their service by supplying a foreign project_env_id. Attackers can configure CI and trigger builds and deployments through the component env endpoints using the other application's configuration, registries and deployment infrastructure.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Authorization Bypass via project_env_id Parameter

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows project users to gain Kubernetes cluster-admin rights by submitting unrestricted manifests through the Additional Manifest feature. Attackers can deploy a ClusterRoleBinding binding a service account to cluster-admin, which the pipeline applies with cluster-wide credentials, granting control over all workloads and secrets.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Privilege Escalation via Additional Manifest

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to create environments on unassigned Kubernetes clusters by tampering with cluster_id and namespaces values. Attackers can modify requests to POST /api/v1/project/{project_id}/env/ to target another project's cluster, then trigger builds and deployments into it, bypassing project isolation.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Authorization Bypass via Environment Creation API

desc: Glance from 0.8.0 before 0.8.8 contains an observable response discrepancy in handlePageRequest and handlePageContentRequest that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate configured page slugs. Attackers can request candidate names against /{page} or /api/pages/{page}/content/ and compare 303/401 versus 404 status codes to discover hidden page names.
title: Glance 0.8.0 before 0.8.8 Page Slug Enumeration via Response Discrepancy

desc: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows authenticated users to list and build from Git repositories restricted to other projects. Attackers can enumerate repositories via GET /api/v1/git_repo/?all=true and submit any git_repo_id to the ci endpoint, cloning other projects' source code, manifests, and committed secrets.
title: OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 Broken Access Control via git_repo API

desc: Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the PATCH /api/user/files/:id rename endpoint that allows authenticated users to overwrite existing uploads by supplying unsanitized names. Attackers can submit names like ../uploads/victim.txt that bypass the raw-string database uniqueness check but normalize via path.join(), causing fs.rename() to replace other files' contents.
title: Zipline through 4.4.0 Path Traversal File Overwrite via PATCH /api/user/files/:id

desc: Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to delete arbitrary server files by injecting traversal sequences via the x-zipline-file-extension header. Attackers can upload a file with a poisoned stored name and short expiry so LocalDatasource deletion removes chosen files, causing denial of service or data loss.
title: Zipline through 4.4.0 Path Traversal Arbitrary File Delete via x-zipline-file-extension

desc: Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read arbitrary server files by abusing a fallback treating the :id parameter as a datasource key. Attackers can send encoded traversal sequences in the :id of GET /api/user/files/:id/raw to escape the Local datasource uploads directory and read files like /etc/shadow.
title: Zipline through 4.4.0 Authenticated Path Traversal via /api/user/files/:id/raw

desc: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows a malicious or compromised ACS to execute commands as root by supplying an unvalidated InternetGatewayDevice.User.{i}.Username value. Attackers can send a SetParameterValues request with shell metacharacters that set_UserUsername() in obuspa_system.lua passes to os.execute(), gaining root command execution.
title: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 OS Command Injection via TR-098 User Username

desc: Glance from 0.7.9 before 0.8.8 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious extension endpoints to inject javascript: URLs via the Widget-Title-URL response header. Attackers controlling an extension endpoint can execute script when users click the widget title, reading dashboard pages through same-origin requests and exfiltrating content.
title: Glance 0.7.9 before 0.8.8 Stored XSS via Widget-Title-URL Header

desc: Zipline before 4.5.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability caused by missing ownership verification in the PATCH and DELETE handlers for /api/user/folders/:id. Authenticated attackers can supply another user's folder ID to rename it, make it public, enable uploads, or delete it.
title: Zipline before 4.5.0 IDOR via Folder PATCH and DELETE Endpoints

desc: Zipline through 4.4.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the WebAuthn login endpoint that creates sessions for a supplied registered credential ID without verifying the assertion. Attackers who obtain a target's passkey credential ID can impersonate that account without its authenticator, potentially gaining administrative control over SUPERADMIN accounts.
title: Zipline through 4.4.0 WebAuthn Authentication Bypass via Passkey Login

desc: Zipline through 4.6.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to read superadmin secrets because GET /api/users and GET /api/users/:id lack the canInteract check. Attackers can retrieve plaintext totpSecret and OAuth tokens to bypass 2FA and take over superadmin accounts, while any authenticated user can enumerate other users' folders via GET /api/user/folders.
title: Zipline through 4.6.2 Privilege Escalation via Missing Role Checks on User Endpoints

desc: Zipline from 4.2.0 before 4.6.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that logs sensitive environment variable values, such as OAUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, without redaction at startup. Attackers with access to system journal or docker logs can obtain OAuth2 client secrets and use them to exchange intercepted OAuth2 callbacks for valid tokens.
title: Zipline 4.2.0 before 4.6.2 OAuth2 Client Secret Leakage in Startup Logs

desc: Zipline before 4.6.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in LocalDatasource that allows SUPERADMIN users to read or delete files outside the upload directory by importing records with traversal filenames. Attackers can trigger the unchecked range-read path with byte-range requests or set expired deletion times to delete files accessible to the Zipline process.
title: Zipline before 4.6.1 Path Traversal via Imported Filenames in LocalDatasource

desc: Zipline before 4.5.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the HighlightCode component that renders unescaped file content before highlight.js finishes loading. Authenticated attackers can upload text files containing HTML/JavaScript payloads that execute in viewers' browsers, enabling API calls such as account changes on the victim's behalf.
title: Zipline before 4.5.1 Stored XSS via HighlightCode Component

desc: Zipline before 4.5.0 contains a stored open redirect vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set arbitrary short URL destinations by abusing missing scheme validation in POST /api/user/urls. Attackers can store javascript: URIs or attacker-controlled URLs as destinations, causing visitors of the trusted short link to be redirected to phishing or malware pages.
title: Zipline before 4.5.0 Stored Open Redirect via POST /api/user/urls

desc: Zipline before 4.6.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in POST /api/user/folders that allows authenticated users to reparent other users' files by supplying their file IDs. Attackers can harvest file IDs from public folders and create a folder seeded with them, disclosing victims' file URLs and removing those files from their folder views.
title: Zipline before 4.6.2 Missing Authorization via POST /api/user/folders

desc: Zipline from 4.3.0 before 4.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to inject HTML through unescaped embed settings in SSR meta tags. Attackers can set malicious embedTitle, embedDescription, embedSiteName, or embedColor values via PATCH /api/user to execute JavaScript in browsers of visitors opening their file view pages.
title: Zipline 4.3.0 before 4.5.0 Stored XSS via SSR Embed Meta Tags

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in ScopeRepository::finalizeScopes() that allows read-only SMART/OAuth clients to obtain write scopes because ScopeEntity::containsScope() ignores registered permissions. Attackers with a client registered for user/<resource>.read can request user/<resource>.write to create, update, and delete appointments or patient data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Privilege Escalation via SMART/OAuth Scope Finalization

desc: Zipline before 4.7.0 contains a race condition vulnerability that allows users to bypass invitation usage limits, upload storage quotas, and shortened-URL quotas through concurrent requests. Attackers can send overlapping registration, upload, or URL creation requests that pass checks against stale state, creating extra accounts and exceeding administrator-configured resource quotas.
title: Zipline before 4.7.0 Race Condition in Invite and Quota Limits

desc: Zipline before 4.6.5 contains a TOCTOU race condition in the POST /api/setup endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to create multiple SUPERADMIN accounts by racing concurrent requests before the firstSetup flag is reset. Attackers can send simultaneous requests with spoofed X-Forwarded-For headers during the argon2 hashing window to gain full administrative control of the instance.
title: Zipline before 4.6.5 TOCTOU Race Condition via /api/setup

desc: Zipline before 4.6.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in GET /api/server/folder/:id that allows unauthenticated attackers to list files in non-public upload-only folders. Attackers who know the folder UUID can supply the page query parameter to bypass the metadata-only early return and enumerate file names, IDs, MIME types, sizes, and view counts.
title: Zipline before 4.6.4 Unauthenticated File Listing via page Query Parameter

desc: Zipline before 4.6.4 contains a rate limit bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to evade request limits by varying query strings or supplying the x-zipline-p-filename header. Attackers can append differing query parameters to login and file or short-link password verification endpoints to perform credential guessing beyond the intended rate limits.
title: Zipline before 4.6.4 Rate Limit Bypass via Query String and Header

desc: Zipline before 4.6.4 contains a resource allocation vulnerability that allows authenticated users to bypass chunked-upload size and quota checks by forging Content-Range offsets and totals. Attackers can send tiny chunks to the partial upload endpoint with large declared offsets, causing the server to create oversized files and exhaust disk space.
title: Zipline before 4.6.4 Upload Quota Bypass via Forged Content-Range Headers

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the patient portal OnsiteDocument.Query endpoint, where mass-assigned _BitwiseAnd criteria parameters are placed unquoted into SQL with only quote-character escaping. Authenticated portal patients can inject SQL outside their per-patient scope to read the entire database, including other patients' demographics and users_secure password hashes.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via OnsiteDocument.Query _BitwiseAnd

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a second-order SQL injection vulnerability in the IPPF contraceptive issue feature because issue_ippf_con_save concatenates layout_options field_id values into a REPLACE INTO query as column names. Authenticated administrators can add a malicious field_id via edit_layout.php, then trigger issue_ippf_con_save through add_edit_issue.php to execute arbitrary SQL.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via IPPF Contraceptive Issue Feature

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains active debug code in interface/fax/fax_view.php that executes passthru("groups") and discloses the web server's Unix group memberships. Authenticated attackers with fax module access can supply a nonexistent jid value to reveal groups such as adm or shadow, aiding privilege escalation planning.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Information Disclosure via Debug Code in fax_view.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored SQL injection vulnerability in getByPatientDemographics() where layout_options field_id values are concatenated into the patient search WHERE clause. Attackers with Layout Editor access can plant a malicious field_id, allowing any authenticated low-privilege user to exfiltrate data from patient_data and users_secure tables.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via getByPatientDemographics in patient.inc.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a second-order sql injection vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to store malicious SQL via library/ajax/addlistitem.php. Attackers can persist a SQL fragment in the recent_patient_columns option_id value, which dynamic_finder.php concatenates into a SELECT query and executes as SQL.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Second-Order SQL Injection via dynamic_finder.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privileged patient portal users to inject JavaScript via the tableArgs field of the onsiteportalactivity API. Attackers can store a payload with spaces that breaks out of an unquoted data-delete-id attribute, executing script when providers click the delete button on the audit review page.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Stored XSS via OnsitePortalActivity tableArgs

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in SLEOB::slInvoiceNumber() in src/Billing/SLEOB.php, which concatenates the CLP01 claim identifier from uploaded X12 835 ERA files into a query without escaping or parameter binding. Authenticated users with billing permissions, or a malicious payer whose ERA file a clerk uploads, can execute arbitrary SQL to read any table, including users_secure password hashes, and modify data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via CLP01 element of X12 835 ERA upload

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated report users to manipulate queries by supplying a crafted form_facility value to interface/reports/ippf_statistics.php. Attackers can close the string literal in the facility_id WHERE clause and use boolean or time-based payloads to read sensitive database contents.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via form_facility in ippf_statistics.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in printed_fee_sheet.php that allows authenticated portal patients to inject script by setting unescaped appointment comments (pc_hometext). Attackers can submit HTML payloads via the form_comments field in add_edit_event_user.php that execute when staff open the patient's fee sheet, acting within the staff session.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Stored XSS via Printed Fee Sheet Appointment Comments

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in ObservationController::deleteAction that allows attackers to delete observation form records without a CSRF token. Attackers can lure a logged-in clinician to a page issuing a GET to delete.php with guessed id values, soft-deleting observations in the victim's open encounter.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 CSRF via Observation Form delete.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in portal/import_template.php, where several portal document template modes lack admin/forms ACL and CSRF checks. Any authenticated staff user can send mode=save_profiles to delete all template profile assignments, use other unguarded modes to push templates to patients or change categories, and read template bodies via mode=get or getPdf.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Missing Authorization via portal/import_template.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to override system-wide global configuration values by storing global-prefixed keys through library/ajax/user_settings.php. Attackers can submit lab or target parameters with global: prefixed setting names to disable audit logging, weaken password policies, or alter security-sensitive settings persistently for their sessions.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Global Configuration Override via user_settings.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Application module's auto-suggest endpoint, which echoes the searchMode POST parameter unencoded into a single-quoted onClick attribute. Attackers can induce an authenticated user to submit a single-quote payload to application/index/search, executing arbitrary JavaScript in that user's session to steal session cookies or disclose patient data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Reflected XSS via auto-suggest searchMode parameter

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the Syndromic Surveillance report because the form_icd_codes[] POST array is concatenated into an unquoted numeric IN() clause without integer validation. Authenticated users can submit quote-free payloads that bypass add_escape_custom to perform blind or UNION-based injection and exfiltrate patient health information.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via form_icd_codes in Syndromic Surveillance

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in five Module Manager InstallerController actions that lack the admin/manage_modules ACL check and CSRF validation. Low-privilege users such as Front Office accounts can POST to saveConfig or SaveHooks to overwrite any module's configuration, retarget CCDA and HIE settings, and delete module hooks.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Missing Authorization in Module Manager Installer Actions

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability in CcrTable::insertApprovedData() that allows authenticated users to inject SQL through request parameter names used as column names. Attackers can send crafted patient_data-*-sel parameters to the revandapprove route, lacking ACL and CSRF checks, to copy password hashes into patient fields or corrupt records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via CCR revandapprove Parameter Names

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Eye Exam (eye_mag) module that allows administrators to inject JavaScript through unencoded Eye_defaults list option titles. Attackers can store a crafted title via edit_list.php that breaks out of a jQuery string in eye_base.php, executing script in any authenticated user's session when they click Defaults.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Stored XSS via Eye Exam Defaults in eye_base.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in era_payments.php and sl_eob_search.php that allows authenticated billing users to write files outside the ERA directory. Attackers can embed traversal sequences in the GS04 element of an uploaded X12 835 file to overwrite .edi or .835 files with attacker-controlled content anywhere writable by the web server.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Path Traversal via ERA 835 File Upload

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the Carecoordination module that allows authenticated users with send_to_hie permission to access any patient's CCDA/CCR/QRDA documents. Attackers can supply arbitrary document or patient IDs to download, transmit, or export patient health records, inject falsified clinical data, and delete audit records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 IDOR in Carecoordination CCDA/CCR/QRDA Document Actions

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in print_referral.php and trend_form.php that allows low-privileged Front Office users to access patient PHI without patients:med permission. Attackers can directly request these endpoints with arbitrary patient_id values to retrieve patient demographics, insurance data, and vitals history, enumerating IDs to expand disclosure.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Missing Authorization via print_referral.php and trend_form.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ccdaservice/ccda_gateway.php that allows any authenticated low-privilege staff user to retrieve other patients' C-CDA documents. Attackers can request the view or dl action with sequential pid values and their own CSRF token to enumerate and exfiltrate medications, problems, allergies, and immunizations.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Missing Authorization in ccdaservice/ccda_gateway.php C-CDA Disclosure

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the ACL module that allows attackers to execute JavaScript in authenticated sessions via the module_id parameter. Attackers can deliver crafted acl/index or acl/acl links that inject unencoded input into inline script blocks, stealing non-HttpOnly session cookies and modifying ACL configuration.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Reflected XSS via ACL Module module_id Parameter

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to execute JavaScript by injecting payloads into the searchEleNo POST parameter of the application/index/search endpoint. Attackers can break out of unencoded HTML attributes in auto-suggest.phtml to inject event handlers that fire on DOM insertion, stealing non-HttpOnly session cookies and patient data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Reflected XSS via searchEleNo in Auto-Suggest Endpoint

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains OAuth scope canonicalization and containment flaws that allow unauthenticated attackers to obtain unapproved system-level FHIR access. Attackers can register a colon-form system:Patient.read client that bypasses approval, then request unregistered system/Patient.write scope to read, modify, and create Patient records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 OAuth Authorization Bypass via Scope Canonicalization

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in PatientPortalPDFDocumentCreator::createPdfObject() that allows authenticated patients to make the server issue HTTP GET requests. Attackers can submit img src, inline style url(), or reinserted unpurified style blocks via the content parameter of portal/lib/doc_lib.php to probe internal ports and cloud metadata endpoints.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SSRF via Patient Portal PDF Generation

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to create patient records and enumerate patients by omitting aclCheckCore() checks. Attackers can POST to new_comprehensive_save.php to create patients with insurance PHI, or query new_search_popup.php and patient_select.php to leak names, SSNs and DOBs.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Missing Authorization in Patient Create and Search Endpoints

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a mass assignment vulnerability in ObservationController::processEnhancedFormSave() that allows authenticated low-privilege users to forge authorization flags through an incomplete field blacklist. Attackers can submit authorized=1 or override the id field alongside observation_id to mark observations as Provider-signed and overwrite clinical fields of other observations within the same patient encounter.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Mass Assignment via Observation Form save.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated low-privilege user to access reports, dated reminders, and batch reminder endpoints lacking AclMain::aclCheckCore() checks. Attackers can request patient_list.php, amc_full_report.php, dated_reminders_add.php, or batch_reminders.php directly to export patient PHI, send unauthorized reminders, and trigger batch reminder processing.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Missing Authorization on Reports and Reminder Endpoints

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the patient portal api/onsiteactivityviews endpoint that allows any authenticated staff user to inject SQL through unquoted Id_BitwiseAnd Criteria values. Attackers can close the bitwise parenthesis and append OR or UNION SELECT clauses to read patient PHI, staff password hashes, MySQL authentication strings, and API tokens.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 SQL Injection via OnsiteActivityView _BitwiseAnd Criteria

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in several custom/ scripts that rely only on session authentication and never call AclMain::aclCheckCore(). Any authenticated low-privilege user can request export_labworks.php, chart_tracker.php, or export_registry_xml.php to disclose patient SSN, DOB, and insurance data or provider NPI/tax IDs, and forge chart-tracker records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 Missing Authorization in custom/ Export and Chart-Tracker Scripts

desc: OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in authorizations_full.php that allows any authenticated staff user to authorize arbitrary patients' clinical records.
