Custom pl-do, pl-func, and writing sql tools therefore ran without confirmation on allow_writes connections, including when a model followed instructions in retrieved content. The affected control is a bundled-client warning rather than a server authorization boundary, and other MCP clients do not inherit that prompt. This issue is fixed in 1.1.0.
title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server custom tools performed writes without user confirmation

desc: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server enables SQL queries against PostgreSQL databases through Model Context Protocol compatible clients. Prior to 1.1.0, custom pl-do tools interpolated JSON arguments into a PostgreSQL DO block delimited by fixed dollar-quote tags. An argument containing $mcp_custom_tool$ could terminate the block and inject arbitrary SQL statements, while $mcp_args$ could inject procedural code into a plpgsql block. Because the statement used the simple query protocol, injected text could include additional statements and transaction control, bypassing read_only and accessing data or modifying resources available to the connecting role. The issue requires at least one pl-do custom tool; sql and pl-func tools pass arguments as bind parameters and are not affected by this injection mechanism. This issue is fixed in 1.1.0.
title: pgEdge Postgres MCP Server SQL injection through custom pl-do tool parameters

desc: In Telerik UI for WinForms, versions prior to 2026.4.1111, an untrusted URL redirection vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to launch arbitrary operating system protocol handlers with attacker-controlled arguments via crafted documents and hyperlinks with a non-allowlisted URI scheme that the user opens.
title: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site in Progress Telerik UI for WinForms

desc: In Telerik UI for WPF, versions prior to 2026.4.1110, an untrusted URL redirection vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to launch arbitrary operating system protocol handlers with attacker-controlled arguments via crafted documents and hyperlinks with a non-allowlisted URI scheme that the user opens.
title: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site in Progress Telerik UI for WPF

desc: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Missing authorization on subscription changes in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1 - An unauthenticated attacker who knows a subscriber's email address can unsubscribe that subscriber from one mailing list or from every mailing lists, without proving that the address is theirs. The affected feature also lets an attacker determine whether a given email address belongs to a subscriber of the site.
products: datasolution:acymailing extension for joomla and wordpress
title: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Missing authorization on subscription changes in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1

desc: Joomla Extension - acymailing.com - Unauthenticated disclosure of mailing list metadata in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1 - An unauthenticated attacker can retrieve every mailing list of the site, including lists that are not publicly visible and lists restricted to an access level, together with their descriptions, access levels, owning user account and subscriber counts. The WordPress plugin is not affected.
title: Joomla Extension - acymailing.com - Unauthenticated disclosure of mailing list metadata in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1

desc: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Open redirect on the subscription and unsubscription endpoints in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1 - On a default configuration, an attacker can craft a link on the affected site that redirects the visitor to an arbitrary external site, which is usable for phishing under the trusted domain.
products: datasolution:acymailing extension for joomla and wordpress
title: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Open redirect on the subscription and unsubscription endpoints in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1

desc: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Online version of an email readable without the visibility check in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1 - An unauthenticated attacker can read the online version of campaigns that were never made public, including campaigns unpublished after being sent and campaigns sent to a restricted audience.
products: datasolution:acymailing extension for joomla and wordpress
title: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Online version of an email readable without the visibility check in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1

desc: Joomla Extension - acymailing.com - Site modules rendered outside their access level in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1 - An unauthenticated visitor can cause a site module to be rendered regardless of the Joomla access level that module is restricted to, which discloses content reserved for a higher view level. The WordPress plugin is not affected.
title: Joomla Extension - acymailing.com - Site modules rendered outside their access level in AcyMailing 1.0.0 - 11.1.1

desc: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor in AcyMailing 6.0.0 - 11.1.1 - Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor in AcyMailing 6.0.0 through 11.1.1. An unauthenticated attacker who knows a subscriber's email address can read that subscriber's record, including the per-subscriber secret key that authorises the subscription management links. Holding that key, the attacker can act as that subscriber on those endpoints, which includes triggering the GDPR data export and the GDPR account deletion where those options are enabled.
products: datasolution:acymailing extension for joomla and wordpress
title: Joomla / WordPress Extension - acymailing.com - Exposure of sensitive information to an unauthorized actor in AcyMailing 6.0.0 - 11.1.1

desc: Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the XLSX invoice-import workflow. An authenticated Manager can import a child invoice whose invoice number contains HTML and is linked to a recurring invoice. When a victim opens that recurring invoice, Akaunting raw-renders the stored child number in an anchor, causing attacker-controlled markup to execute in the victim's browser.
title: Akaunting 3.3.0 - Stored XSS through imported invoice numbers

desc: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - SSRF via external download URL field jDownloads < 4.1.8 -  HTTP redirects when retrieving external download URLs could bypass validation of the original destination. This allowed server-side requests to internal or otherwise prohibited destinations and disclosure of their responses (SSRF).
title: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - SSRF via external download URL field jDownloads < 4.1.8

desc: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - Publishing of files without approval in jDownloads < 4.1.8 -  Manipulated frontend submission parameters could bypass the intended publication and ownership rules. In particular, submissions could be published despite automatic publication being disabled, and ownership could be assigned contrary to the intended policy.
title: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - Publishing of files without approval in jDownloads < 4.1.8

desc: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - RCE through file upload in jDownloads < 4.1.8 -  Insufficient validation of frontend thumbnail uploads allowed users with upload permission to place executable files on the server. This results in PHP code execution.
title: Joomla Extension - jdownloads.com - RCE through file upload in jDownloads < 4.1.8

desc: In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET MVC versions `2012.2.710` through `2026.3.1015`, server-side filter processing does not properly validate descriptor types, null values, or stack state in FilterNodeVisitor and does not catch FilterParserException within the affected assembly. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an endpoint reachable without authentication that accepts crafted filter parameters. Affected requests can trigger uncaught cast, null-reference, or empty-stack exceptions and return HTTP 500. The report does not demonstrate worker-process termination or disruption of unrelated requests. The issue is fixed in version `2026.4.1111`.
products: progress software:telerik ui for asp.net mvc
title: Uncaught Exceptions in Telerik UI for ASP.NET MVC Filter Processing

desc: In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET Core versions `2015.1.318` through `2026.3.1015`, the server-side FilterParser processes nested expressions in untrusted filter parameters through recursive parsing without a recursion-depth limit, while FilterLexer does not enforce an input-length limit. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an endpoint using DataSourceRequest model binding that is reachable without authentication. Deeply nested filters can trigger parsing errors during model binding or cause `StackOverflowException`. This issue is fixed in version `2026.4.1111`.
products: progress software:telerik ui for asp.net core
title: Uncontrolled Recursion in Telerik UI for ASP.NET Core FilterParser

desc: Grafana's Prometheus data source passes the resource path supplied by the caller to the configured Prometheus server without restricting it to the supported API endpoints [missing path allowlist]. A user with permission to query the data source can read responses from other endpoints on that server using the data source's credentials.
title: Server-side request forgery in the Prometheus data source resource API

desc: The Elasticsearch data source resource proxy forwards the request method and path to Elasticsearch using the data source's own credentials, without restricting them to the operations the plugin needs. A user who can query the data source can alter index mappings or reach other indices on the cluster. [Improper authorization / path validation]
title: Elasticsearch data source resource proxy allows arbitrary methods and paths with the data source's credentials

desc: A user with query access to a Google Cloud Monitoring data source can use its resource proxy to send requests to other Cloud Monitoring API paths with the data source's credentials, and read data from any project those credentials can reach. When the data source forwards the user's OAuth identity or uses Workload Identity Federation, the impact depends on that credential's permissions. Fixed in Google Cloud Monitoring plugin 12.6.7.
title: Unintended API access through the Google Cloud Monitoring data source resource proxy

desc: The Plesk GoAccess statistics integration in Plesk Obsidian for Linux, versions 18.0.77 to 18.0.81.7, 18.0.82 to 18.0.82.2, allows cross-subscription information disclosure.

The http.cookies.Morsel class allows separator semicolons in attribute
values
and includes them verbatim in all output formats. An attacker who can
control
these values could use this to relax the cookie's Domain or SameSite
restrictions.
title: Cookie Attribute Injection via Unescaped Semicolons in http.cookies.Morsel

desc: AppFlowy Cloud through 0.9.64 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace members to upload blobs with unvalidated Content-Type values that are later served inline without a Content-Disposition header or authentication on the retrieval route. Attackers can upload a text/html or image/svg+xml blob via put_blob_handler, which is then rendered as an active same-origin document through the unauthenticated get_blob_handler endpoint and cached immutably for one year, enabling persistent script execution against any visitor who accesses the URL.
title: AppFlowy Cloud 0.9.64 Stored XSS via Blob Upload Content-Type

desc: A flaw was found in freeradius. An improper length validation in the EAP-FAST module allows a stack-based buffer overflow during session ticket processing. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by sending a specially crafted handshake request, causing the server process to crash and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
title: Freeradius: stack buffer overflow via unchecked eap-fast sessionticket length

desc: MLflow before 3.18.0 using the FileStore backend contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write files outside the intended run directory by supplying a malicious model_id parameter to the log outputs API. Attackers can exploit the unvalidated model_id containing ../ sequences via the POST /api/3.0/mlflow/runs/outputs endpoint to create directories and write a meta.yaml file at arbitrary filesystem locations, limited only by the server account's permissions. FileStore was the default backend before 3.7.0 and is opt-in afterward through MLFLOW_ALLOW_FILE_STORE.
title: MLflow < 3.18.0 Path Traversal via model_id in log_outputs API

desc: A flaw was found in freeradius's Extensible Authentication Protocol Method for Subscriber Identity Module (EAP-SIM) module. When handling authentication requests, the server copies a client-supplied identity into an internal structure without properly checking its length against a fixed-size buffer. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by sending specially crafted EAP-SIM messages, triggering a stack buffer overflow that crashes the service and results in a Denial of Service (DoS).
title: Freeradius: stack-based buffer overflow via unbounded eap-sim identity length

desc: The MongoDB Node.js driver does not consistently enforce its permitted-host restriction during OIDC authentication. A bearer token produced by the embedding application's own login callback may therefore be transmitted to a host outside the configured set of permitted hosts, which may result in unintended disclosure of that credential. No database account is required; the party supplying the connection configuration needs only to influence the settings the application passes to the driver.
title: [Node.js Driver] OIDC ENVIRONMENT confusion bypasses ALLOWED_HOSTS and leaks human-callback bearer tokens

desc: A validation flaw in the DNS SRV host discovery of the MongoDB Node.js driver may cause the driver to connect to a host outside the expected domain. For a mongodb+srv:// connection string, the driver checks each host name in the DNS SRV response against the domain of the connection string. The driver then builds the connection address from the original name, in which certain characters end the host name early. An unauthenticated party who can forge or change the DNS SRV response may redirect the connection to a host of their choice. TLS does not prevent this, because the driver verifies the server certificate against the redirected host name. This may result in unintended disclosure of application data and authentication credentials, and in altered query results. Applications that use mongodb:// connection strings are not affected.
title: Attacker able to redirect a client's database traffic to a host they control via special characters in an SRV target, bypassing the SRV parent-domain guard

desc: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 4.0.1, Soup Sieve repeatedly searches descendant subtrees for each candidate evaluated by :has() and repeatedly reevaluates a parent containing :has(> ...) for each child, causing quadratic matching on deeply nested or wide attacker-influenced HTML or XML. Applications using ordinary fixed selectors through select(), select_one(), or Beautiful Soup CSS APIs against untrusted documents can have a worker occupied for seconds or minutes, while applications that process only trusted documents are not affected. Selectors compiled with NOCACHE continue to use the old uncached behavior. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.1.
title: Soup Sieve: Quadratic-time denial of service when matching `:has()`

desc: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library for Beautiful Soup. From 0.4 until 3.0, deeply nested CSS pseudo-class selectors can cause recursive parsing to exceed Python’s recursion limit and raise  RecursionError . Applications accepting untrusted selectors may experience failure of the affected request or task if the exception is not handled. The demonstrated behavior is recoverable and does not establish an interpreter crash or persistent service-wide denial of service. This vulnerability is fixed in version 3.0.
title: Soup Sieve: Uncontrolled recursion in Soup Sieve CSS parser lets nested pseudo-class selectors exhaust the Python call stack

desc: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 2.10, matching a developer-authored selector that places the general sibling combinator inside :has() repeatedly scans each candidate element's following siblings when the right-hand side is absent, producing quadratic work on attacker-controlled HTML. Applications that evaluate a fixed selector such as div:has(a ~ b) over untrusted markup can have a worker occupied for minutes by a small document, while the adjacent sibling form and trusted-only document processing are not affected in the same way. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.
title: Soup Sieve: General sibling combinator inside :has() matches untrusted HTML in quadratic time

desc: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 3.0, the CSS_ESCAPES and IDENTIFIER regular-expression subpatterns can backtrack exponentially on runs of ambiguous digit escapes in an attribute-name or tag position of an otherwise valid selector. The failure occurs during selector compilation through soupsieve.compile() or Beautiful Soup select() before SELECTOR_LIMIT is applied, so an application that accepts untrusted selector strings can have a worker stalled by a short input. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.
title: Soup Sieve: Exponential ReDoS in selector compilation via \9-run in CSS_ESCAPES/IDENTIFIER

desc: Soup Sieve is a CSS selector library designed to be used with Beautiful Soup 4. Prior to 4.0, Soup Sieve repeatedly walks the same ancestors while matching descendant combinators, and each additional descendant combinator raises the polynomial degree of the work on deeply nested attacker-influenced HTML or XML. Applications using selectors such as section div div through select(), select_one(), or Beautiful Soup CSS APIs against untrusted documents can have a worker occupied for seconds or minutes, while trusted-only document processing is not affected. Selectors compiled with NOCACHE continue to use the old uncached behavior. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.
title: Soup Sieve: Polynomial-time denial of service in the descendant combinator

desc: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery, Chart shared-tooltip rendering treats bound category and series-name values as raw HTML. An attacker who can influence values consumed by an affected Chart can inject markup that executes as JavaScript when a user displays the shared tooltip. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data available in the user's browser context. Version 2016.2.607 or earlier may be affected, but earlier releases have not been verified. The latest vulnerable version is 2026.3.1015; the issue is fixed in version 2026.4.1111.
title: Cross-Site Scripting in Kendo UI for jQuery Chart Shared Tooltip

desc: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery, the Chart default tooltip renders point values as raw HTML. An attacker who can influence a string point value can inject markup that executes as JavaScript when a user hovers over the point. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data available in the user's browser context. Version 2016.2.607 or earlier may be affected, but earlier releases have not been verified. The latest vulnerable version is 2026.3.1015; the issue is fixed in version 2026.4.1111.
title: Cross-Site Scripting in Kendo UI for jQuery Chart Shared Tooltip

desc: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery Gantt, the task editor's Parent dropdown renders task titles as HTML. An attacker who can influence a task title shown in the dropdown can cause attacker-controlled markup to execute as JavaScript when a user opens or interacts with the task editor. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data available in the user's browser context. The first affected version is 2020.3.915; the latest vulnerable version is 2026.3.1015. The issue is fixed in version 2026.4.1111.
title: Cross-Site Scripting in Kendo UI for jQuery Gantt Parent Dropdown

desc: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery Form, the items[].hint option is documented as a string but is rendered as HTML. An attacker who can influence a Form item's hint can cause attacker-controlled markup to execute as JavaScript when a user views the rendered form. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data available in the user's browser context. The first affected version is 2020.2.513; the latest vulnerable version is 2026.3.1015. The issue is fixed in version 2026.4.1111.
title: Cross-Site Scripting in Kendo UI for jQuery Form Item Hints

desc: In Progress Kendo UI for jQuery, Spreadsheet sheet names are inserted into the SheetsBar menu button's data-sheet-name attribute without encoding. An attacker who can influence a sheet name can inject an event-handler attribute and execute JavaScript when a user hovers over the menu button. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality and integrity of data available in the user's browser context. The first affected version is 2024.4.1112; the latest vulnerable version is 2026.3.1015. The issue is fixed in version 2026.4.1111.
title: Cross-Site Scripting in Kendo UI for jQuery Spreadsheet Sheet Names

desc:
A flaw was found in the interaction between systemd-gpt-auto-generator and 
confidential computing guest VM images in OpenShift Sandboxed Containers 
(confidential peer pods). systemd-gpt-auto-generator automatically discovers 
and mounts GPT partitions by type GUID at boot with no user confirmation. In 
the confidential computing threat model, where the host/hypervisor is the 
adversary, a malicious host can inject partitions into the guest's virtual 
disk. Most critically, injecting a swap partition causes the guest kernel to 
page out TEE-encrypted memory to a host-controlled block device, breaking the 
confidentiality guarantee of the hardware TEE (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX).

The PodVM images use a GPT-partitioned disk with dm-verity on the root 
partition. However, the roothash= kernel parameter only disables root 
auto-discovery — non-root partitions (swap, /home, /var, /srv, /var/tmp) are 
still auto-discovered and mounted. The generator is shipped unmasked in the 
RHEL systemd-udev subpackage, and no kernel command line parameter in the 
measured UKI addon disables it. Additionally, the PodVM measurement script 
captures PCRs 3, 9, 11, and 12, but not PCR 5 (GPT partition table), so 
partition table modifications are not detected by remote attestation.
products: red hat:red hat openshift container platform 4
red hat:red hat openshift container platform 5
title: Sandboxed-containers: kernel: systemd-gpt-auto-generator: guest data leakage in confidential computing (sandboxed containers)

desc:
Incorrect default permissions and Product released in Non-Release configuration vulnerability in OpenText Identity Console on Windows, Linux, and 64 bit allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.

This issue affects Identity Console: from 1.8 through 25.2.
desc_es:
Una vulnerabilidad de permisos predeterminados incorrectos y publicación de producto en configuración de no producción en OpenText Identity Console en Windows y Linux (64 bits) permite recuperar datos sensibles embebidos.

Este problema afecta a Identity Console: desde la versión 1.8 hasta la 25.2.
title: Improper File Permissions on Private Key Files in Docker Deployments

desc:
The user-mode syscall verifiers for the charger driver API in drivers/charger/charger_handlers.c did not inspect the prop argument before copying union charger_propval across the user/kernel boundary. Two members of that union are function pointers — status_notification (CHARGER_PROP_STATUS_NOTIFICATION) and online_notification (CHARGER_PROP_ONLINE_NOTIFICATION), declared in include/zephyr/drivers/charger.h — and z_vrfy_charger_set_prop() forwarded the caller-supplied union verbatim to the driver's set_property callback for any property. z_vrfy_charger_get_prop() had the mirror defect and copied the stored kernel callback address back out to user memory.

With CONFIG_USERSPACE enabled, any user-mode thread that has been granted a charger device object could call charger_set_prop() with CHARGER_PROP_STATUS_NOTIFICATION or CHARGER_PROP_ONLINE_NOTIFICATION and an arbitrary pointer value. Drivers that implement these properties — drivers/charger/charger_max20335.c, drivers/charger/charger_pf1550.c and drivers/charger/charger_bq2518x.c — store the pointer in device data and later invoke it from their interrupt work handlers, which run in supervisor mode, on any charger state change such as a cable plug/unplug.

The result is a control-flow hijack at kernel privilege from an unprivileged thread, defeating the isolation that CONFIG_USERSPACE is meant to provide; the read path additionally disclosed a kernel code address to user mode, and clearing a notifier installed by a supervisor thread let user mode suppress charger notifications. Supervisor-mode callers of charger_set_prop()/charger_get_prop() are unaffected.

The fix makes both verifiers reject the two notifier properties outright — including when the supplied callback is NULL, since the notifiers are device state — and adds a BUILD_ASSERT on CHARGER_PROP_COMMON_COUNT so that new properties force a re-review of the union's user-mode safety.
title: Arbitrary supervisor-mode function pointer injection via charger_set_prop() syscall in the charger driver API

desc: ToolJet before 3.21.94, fixed in commit e5f387a, contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the app environments init endpoint that allows authenticated users to read app version metadata belonging to other workspaces. Attackers can send GET requests to /api/app-environments/init with an editing_version_id from another workspace to retrieve the version name, description, status, current environment ID, and app ID, because the lookup is not scoped to the caller's organization.
title: ToolJet < 3.21.94 Authorization Bypass via app-environments/init

desc: SOGo before 5.12.13 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to exhaust all worker processes by configuring an auxiliary IMAP mail account pointing to a controlled host that accepts a TCP connection but never sends an IMAP greeting response. Attackers can issue concurrent GET requests to the mail view of this account to hold workers indefinitely without an effective timeout, occupying every SOGo worker and denying service to all users for approximately five minutes until the watchdog kills and respawns the stuck workers.
title: SOGo before 5.12.13 Denial of Service via Auxiliary IMAP Account Greeting Wait

desc:
The user-mode system call verifier z_vrfy_charger_get_prop() in drivers/charger/charger_handlers.c declares an uninitialized union charger_propval k_val on the kernel (privileged) stack, passes it to the charger driver back end via z_impl_charger_get_prop(), and then copies the full sizeof(union charger_propval) back into the calling user thread's buffer with k_usermode_to_copy(). That discloses kernel stack contents on two paths:

On error. The copy-out ignores the driver's return code. In-tree back ends return an error without writing through the value pointer for properties they do not implement: charger_gpio_get_prop() returns -ENOTSUP unconditionally, and bq24190_get_prop() has a default: return -ENOTSUP; arm that never touches val. The whole union is then stack residue.
On success. A back end writes only the one union member the requested property selects (for example sbs_charger.c writes the one-byte val->present for CHARGER_PROP_PRESENT and returns 0), yet the handler still copies the whole union, so every byte beyond that member is uninitialized.

The handler is compiled only when CONFIG_USERSPACE=y and is reachable by any user-mode thread that has been granted access to a charger device object. K_SYSCALL_DRIVER_CHARGER() validates only the device object and its API pointer, not the property identifier, so an unprivileged thread can choose prop freely: an unimplemented property forces the error path, a narrow one the success path, and the call can be repeated at will.

Each call discloses up to the size of the union (12 bytes on a 32-bit target, 16 bytes on 64-bit targets where the function-pointer members widen it) of supervisor-stack memory. The bytes are residue of earlier kernel-side frames on the thread's privileged stack and can contain kernel object addresses and saved return addresses, which an unprivileged thread cannot otherwise observe and which help defeat address-layout assumptions when exploiting a separate memory-safety defect. There is no integrity or availability impact.

Two commits fix it, and both are needed. 5054384e983c skips the copy-out when the back end reports an error. c31cac727d02 zeroes the union before the driver call, so the bytes copied out on success are driver-written data or zeros. A tree carrying only the first still leaks on every successful call.
title: Kernel stack information disclosure in the charger_get_prop() system call handler

desc: SOGo before 5.12.13 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to make the server connect to arbitrary internal host:port destinations by supplying a user-controlled URL to the Calendar/addWebCalendar endpoint. Attackers can trigger a reload of the subscribed web calendar via the reload endpoint and distinguish response outcomes such as connection failures, timeouts, authentication prompts, or invalid content to probe the internal network from the server's position.
title: SOGo before 5.12.13 SSRF via Web Calendar Subscriptions

desc: SOGo before 5.12.13 contains a Sieve script injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject arbitrary Sieve directives by inserting unescaped notification address values into a generated Sieve script. Attackers can embed Sieve redirect or discard statements within the notificationAddress preference to bypass the administrator-configured forwarding-domain constraint and redirect or discard incoming mail.
title: SOGo before 5.12.13 Sieve Script Injection via Notification Address

desc: A code injection vulnerability in promzard’s template-loading functionality allows an attacker who can control property names in the context object (ctx) to execute arbitrary code with the privileges of the Node.js process. The library inserts context property names into a generated function’s parameter list without validation or escaping and evaluates the resulting source using `vm.runInThisContext()`. A crafted property name can escape the parameter list and inject JavaScript code, even when the template file is fully trusted.
title: CVE-2026-127109

desc: SOGo before 5.12.13 contains an improper cryptographic signature verification vulnerability that allows remote attackers to replace a victim's contact S/MIME certificate by sending a spoofed multipart/signed message with a mismatched signature and an impersonated From address. Attackers can deliver a crafted CMS signedData object containing their own self-signed certificate, which SOGo's UIxMailView stores on the contact card without validating signature authenticity or certificate identity, enabling subsequent encrypted communications to be decrypted with the attacker's private key.
title: SOGo before 5.12.13 S/MIME Certificate Spoofing via UIxMailView

desc: SOGo before 5.12.13 contains a missing rate limiting vulnerability in its web login TOTP verification that allows attackers who already possess a victim's password to brute-force the second-factor code without triggering any lockout. Attackers can send repeated POST requests to /SOGo/connect with wrong verification codes at high speed since failed TOTP attempts never increment the failed-login counter and SOGoMaximumFailedLoginCount does not apply, enabling indefinite guessing across 30-second code windows to bypass two-factor authentication.
title: SOGo before 5.12.13 Missing Rate Limiting on TOTP Verification

desc: SOGo before 5.12.13 contains an improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reset account passwords by repeatedly guessing secret-question answers via the passwordRecoveryCheck endpoint without lockout or rate limiting. Attackers can submit unlimited candidate answers to obtain a valid recovery JWT, then use it to change the account password without the old credential and log in via the connect endpoint, achieving full account takeover on accounts without TOTP enabled.
title: SOGo before 5.12.13 Unauthenticated Password Recovery Brute Force

desc: Docker Sandboxes reuses existing state and configuration directories without verifying their ownership. If sbx or sandboxd is run as root with HOME or, on Linux, XDG_STATE_HOME pointing to an attacker-controlled location, a local unprivileged user can substitute control-plane sockets and configuration trusted by the root process, potentially executing commands as root. Exploitation requires a privileged invocation with an attacker-influenced environment. The issue affects Linux and macOS and is fixed in version 0.53.0.
title: Docker Sandboxes privilege escalation through untrusted state directories

desc: Docker Sandboxes can silently republish a sandbox service after an operator removes its automatically assigned host-port mapping. The daemon removes the active binding but retains the original publication request, allowing a later port change or sandbox restart to publish the service again on a new host port. An attacker able to reach the restored endpoint may regain access to the service. Both TCP and UDP mappings are affected. Exposure is limited to the original bind address, which defaults to loopback. The issue is fixed in version 0.53.0.
title: Docker Sandboxes restores removed automatically assigned port publications

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL SQL-language functions allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via an output parameter of type "any".  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL output parameter type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE primarily.  Other DDL attack routes exist, such as "ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN; ROLLBACK; ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN".  The system had inadequate tracking of typed values, and values were not self-identifying.  Stale values could appear in data dictionary entries, PL/pgSQL variables, and many other parts of the system.  PostgreSQL Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL type confusion after ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE executes arbitrary code

desc: Uncontrolled search path element in PostgreSQL CREATE EXTENSION allows an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege to execute arbitrary code as the bootstrap superuser, via ALTER SCHEMA ... RENAME or CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA "$user".  ALTER EXTENSION was also affected.  A trusted-extension script located the wrong object and executed arbitrary SQL of the attacker's choice.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL extension script schema mishandling executes arbitrary SQL

desc: Improper protection in PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on auto-updatable views allows an attacker having INSERT and UPDATE privileges on the view to read and modify every row in the view's base table, via iterated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.  This bypasses the view's WHERE condition, whether or not the view is a security_barrier view.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT can read or modify rows despite auto-updatable view WHERE condition

desc: Use of externally-controlled format string in PostgreSQL pg_basebackup allows an attacker having already compromised a server to achieve disclosure from pg_basebackup memory, via backup manifest bytes.  The vulnerability does not return the improperly-read bytes back to the attacker's server, so a successful attack would need separate implementation-specific secrets for that.  Integrity impact is unlikely; in particular, the applicable formatter does not support %n.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL pg_basebackup can use backup manifest content as a format string

desc: A security flaw has been discovered in JeecgBoot up to 3.9.5. This vulnerability affects the function OpenApiController.call of the file /openapi/call of the component Authentication Filter. The manipulation results in server-side request forgery. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
title: JeecgBoot Authentication Filter call OpenApiController.call server-side request forgery

desc: External control of file name in PostgreSQL dblink and CREATE/ALTER SUBSCRIPTION allows a user to achieve persistent denial of service, via appending invalid data to a chosen file.  Specifically, the "sslkeylogfile" connection parameter appends data, in NSS keylog format, to a file of the user's choosing.  This "sslkeylogfile" mechanism cannot add arbitrary bytes.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are also affected if libpq version 18 or later is installed and in use by the server.
title: PostgreSQL dblink and subscriptions can append to arbitrary files

desc: A vulnerability was identified in JeecgBoot up to 3.9.6. This affects the function RestTemplate.exchange of the file org/jeecg/modules/airag/flow/c/a.class of the component flow-run Endpoint. The manipulation leads to server-side request forgery. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
title: JeecgBoot flow-run Endpoint a.class RestTemplate.exchange server-side request forgery

desc: A vulnerability was determined in SakanaAI text-to-LoRA 0.0.1. Affected by this issue is the function get_tokenizer of the file src/hyper_llm_modulator/utils/model_loading.py of the component Checkpoint Loading. Executing a manipulation of the argument base_model_name_or_path can lead to path traversal. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.
title: SakanaAI text-to-LoRA Checkpoint Loading model_loading.py get_tokenizer path traversal

desc: ComfyUI-Easy-Use version 1.3.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the `save_preview()` handler for POST `/easyuse/save/{name}`. The handler checks the source directory before appending a user-supplied filename and allows the request to select the `custom_nodes` directory as a copy destination. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the ComfyUI server can overwrite an installed custom node’s Python entry point with an uploaded file. When ComfyUI restarts and loads the modified node, the attacker’s code runs with the privileges of the ComfyUI process.
title: Unauthenticated Path Traversal in ComfyUI-Easy-Use Allows Remote Code Execution

desc: Improper protection in PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT allows an attacker having INSERT, UPDATE, and applicable SELECT privileges on the table to read every row despite row security policies, via iterated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.  Unlike CVE-2026-16237, this does not facilitate improper writes.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT can read rows despite row security policies

desc: SQL injection in PostgreSQL extension-script substitutions allows an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege to execute arbitrary code as the bootstrap superuser, via a schema or owner name containing newlines or other special substrings.  This is similar to CVE-2023-39417, but it requires a non-bundled extension with a vulnerable script pattern.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL extension-script substitutions allow SQL injection through object names

desc: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL REASSIGN OWNED allows a role granted INHERIT but not SET to transfer objects to the granted role.  It also allows reassignment of database ownership without the CREATEDB privilege.  The equivalent ALTER ... OWNER commands block this.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL REASSIGN OWNED bypasses role SET and CREATEDB checks

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL pg_show_all_settings() allows a database user to retrieve memory contents, via loading a module while the function is scanning custom-variable placeholders that the module replaces and frees.  Within major versions 16-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, and 16.16 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL pg_show_all_settings() use-after-free discloses memory

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL plpgsql record-field assignment allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a reentrant domain CHECK that changes a RECORD variable's row type while a value is being cast.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL plpgsql record-field type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL logical replication allows a compromised publisher to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the superuser-owned subscription, via naming a system catalog as a replication target.  Only subscriptions owned by a superuser are vulnerable.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL logical replication can write to subscriber system catalogs, executing arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in the PostgreSQL dblink extension allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via type conversion code that re-enters dblink and closes a connection whose results an outer dblink call is reading.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL dblink reentrant disconnect use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL extended statistics allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a statistics expression of an anonymous RECORD type whose backend-local type identifier denotes a different row type in another session.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL extended-statistics pseudo-type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Heap-based buffer overflow in PostgreSQL foreign batch inserts allows a foreign server to execute arbitrary code, via reporting that it inserted more rows than the server supplied.  postgres_fdw can legitimately encounter this when a rule on the remote table expands an INSERT into additional rows.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL FDW batch-insert mismatch executes arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL expanded-record domain checks allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via repeated checks of a domain over a composite type that cause reuse of a dangling memory-context pointer.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL expanded-record domain-check use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL operator commutator and negator links allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via linking operators having different result types or creating inconsistent reciprocal links.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL commutator or negator result-type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Operation on a dropped index in PostgreSQL REINDEX CONCURRENTLY allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via an index expression that issues DROP INDEX.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL REINDEX CONCURRENTLY does not block DROP INDEX during index functions

desc: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL in-memory tuple-size calculations allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via oversized tuple data.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL tuple-size integer wraparound executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL materialized set-returning functions allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via returning rows having different dynamic RECORD return types.  json_populate_recordset() is one affected function.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL materialized set-returning function type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL anonymous RECORD types allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via row types having dropped attributes in the same positions but with different widths or alignments.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL dropped-column type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL trigger functions allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a cursor over a transition table.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL transition-table cursor use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion from incomplete PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a composite type change while its cache entry is being populated.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation gap executes arbitrary code

desc: Exposure of sensitive information in PostgreSQL security_barrier processing allows a database user to infer values hidden by a security_barrier view, via applying a leaky function to a CASE test value or internal parameter that indirectly represents a protected column.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL security_barrier analysis can expose hidden values through indirect expressions

desc: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL parallel B-tree scans allows an object creator to read attacker-chosen server-memory addresses, via a function incorrectly marked PARALLEL SAFE or STABLE to make participating workers build different scan-key arrays.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL parallel B-tree array scan reads beyond array bounds

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL min/max aggregate optimization allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a user-defined aggregate whose SORTOP option causes the planner to treat the aggregate's input and result as the same type when they differ.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL min/max aggregate type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL portal setup allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via running user-defined code during planning or executor startup that closes the portal currently being prepared.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL portal setup use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Uncaught exceptions in PostgreSQL plperl allow an object creator to cause use of a stale sigjmp_buf, via a tied Perl object, or a Perl object whose overloaded conversion throws while plperl is handling another error.  We have not ruled out arbitrary code execution on some platform.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL plperl tied-object exceptions follow stale sigjmp_buf

desc: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL generation memory contexts allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via freeing an allocation larger than 1 GB and causing its block to be reused for smaller chunks whose back-pointer offset cannot represent that position.  Within major versions 16-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, and 16.16 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL generation memory context integer wraparound executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL statistics import allows a table maintainer to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via nested SET DATA TYPE during conversion of values to import.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL statistics import type confusion executes arbitrary code

desc: Untrusted data inclusion in PostgreSQL pg_dump tar-format restore.sql allows a compromised origin server to execute arbitrary code as the client operating system account running psql, via the predictable restriction key in restore.sql.  This is a gap in the fix for CVE-2025-8714.  restore.sql is undocumented.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL pg_dump tar restore.sql fails to block psql command injection

desc: SQL injection in PostgreSQL reindexdb allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user running reindexdb, via a crafted index name embedded in the parallel catalog query for --jobs with --index.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL reindexdb index name quoting allows SQL injection

desc: Improper null termination in PostgreSQL array element assignment allows a database user to disclose server memory, via changing the final byte of a fixed-length name value to a nonzero byte and passing it to code that treats the value as a C string.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL unterminated name value discloses server memory

desc: Improper locking in PostgreSQL startup processing allows an unauthenticated network client to trigger a server restart, via arranging for authentication_timeout to arrive while it holds a spinlock during cancel handling.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL pre-authentication cancel request can leak a spinlock

desc: SQL injection in PostgreSQL pg_dump allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the user restoring the dump, via an inherited column having a child-local not-null constraint whose name requires quoting.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL pg_dump not-null constraint name allows SQL injection

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via reentrant return_next() calls.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL plperl reentrant return_next() use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via dropping the final reference to a Perl array or hash while PostgreSQL is converting that object.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL plperl array and hash conversion use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL pltcl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a domain CHECK that re-enters the Tcl interpreter and frees or changes a string still used by the outer result conversion.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL pltcl reentrant result conversion use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DROP OWNED allows a role to remove itself from restrictive row level security policies, thereby reading or modifying rows that the policy was intended to deny, via queries after the DROP OWNED.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL DROP OWNED can remove restrictive row security policies from non-owned tables

desc: Inconsistent transition-capture state in PostgreSQL MERGE allows a table data modifier to make an AFTER trigger process the wrong new row, via a partitioned table MERGE that performs an INSERT before an UPDATE.  Within major versions 15-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, and 15.20 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 15 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL MERGE can place the wrong row in a trigger transition table

desc: Untrusted search path in PostgreSQL vacuumdb allows a database owner to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user running vacuumdb, via shadowing operators used in the --missing-stats-only catalog query.  The pg_upgrade documentation recommends an affected vacuumdb invocation.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL "vacuumdb --missing-stats-only" lets a database owner execute code as the vacuumdb user

desc: Improper input validation in PostgreSQL pg_restore allows a non-plain archive provider to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running pg_restore, via a crafted archive.  Note a contrast: crafted archive data may legitimately cause arbitrary SQL to execute at the restore destination, but it does not legitimately confer arbitrary code execution in the pg_restore OS process.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL pg_restore executes arbitrary code due to missing non-plain archive validation

desc: Heap-based buffer overflow in PostgreSQL tsvector_delete() allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a tsvector whose lexeme data uses a nonstandard but valid ordering that requires additional alignment padding in the result.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL tsvector_delete() heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code

desc: Improper protection of alternate path in PostgreSQL security-restricted operations allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the operation's caller, via a domain, enum, or range type created in pg_temp.  The victim session must later run a query containing an unqualified type name, e.g. "SELECT '1'::bigint"; autovacuum and other common security-restricted operation users do not do so, so they are unaffected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL security-restricted operations can create types in pg_temp, which later queries of the session find

desc: Heap-based buffer overflow in PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd() may allow a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via an invalid tsvector containing duplicate positions.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd() heap buffer overflow may execute arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL COPY FROM error reporting allows a database user to disclose portions of server memory, via a longer input row following an ignored or nullified conversion error.  file_fdw reaches the same code path in affected version 18.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.
title: PostgreSQL COPY error context uses freed field storage

desc: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL dict_int allows a database user to disclose portions of server memory, via a zero-length token.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL dict_int reads beyond zero-length tokens

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL coordination of anonymous RECORD type identifiers among parallel workers allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via causing one process to free a shared tuple descriptor while another process retains and later uses its address.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL parallel RECORD typmod use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL composite-value field assignment allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via changing a composite type between deforming and reforming a value.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL composite-type change during field assignment executes arbitrary code

desc: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via re-entering plperl and freeing a prepared query while an outer invocation is executing it.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL plperl prepared-query use-after-free executes arbitrary code

desc: Type confusion in PostgreSQL plperl may allow an object creator to execute arbitrary code, via blessing a non-hash reference into PostgreSQL::InServer::ARRAY.  We have not confirmed or ruled out a way to control the pointer sufficiently to achieve security impact, but we are proceeding as though that is possible.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL plperl blessed-reference type confusion may execute arbitrary code

desc: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL type conversion allows a database user to invoke a cast function despite lacking EXECUTE privilege on that function, via foreign keys, to_json(), and others.  A successful attack requires the attacker to search each database for access-restricted cast functions and identify confidentiality impact specific to each function implementation found.  There are few or no practical examples of an access-restricted cast function or of a cast function having confidentiality impact.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
title: PostgreSQL foreign key and JSON conversions bypass EXECUTE privilege on cast functions

desc: An incorrect authorization vulnerability was found in AWX's WebSocket consumer. The consumer_access() function only enforces access controls for object-level event groups (job_events, workflow_events, ad_hoc_command_events) but does not restrict subscriptions to global broadcast groups such as 'jobs-status_changed'. When an authenticated user subscribes to a global broadcast group, the server accepts the subscription without verifying that the user has permission to view the associated resources. In multi-organization deployments, this allows a low-privilege user in one organization to receive real-time job status metadata from all organizations, including job IDs, status transitions, timestamps, and infrastructure topology details such as instance group names, bypassing the organization isolation enforced by the REST API.
products: red hat:red hat ansible automation platform 2
title: Awx: websocket broadcast groups leak cross-organization job metadata

desc:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in TÜBİTAK BİLGEM Yazılım Teknolojileri Araştırma Enstitüsü pardus-image-writer allows Privilege Escalation.

This issue affects pardus-image-writer: before 0.9.0.
products: tübi̇tak bi̇lgem yazılım teknolojileri araştırma enstitüsü:pardus-image-writer
title: Pardus Image Writer Local Privilege Escalation via Polkit Misconfiguration in TÜBİTAK BİLGEM's pardus-image-writer

desc: An uncontrolled recursion vulnerability has been discovered in the Qt QXmlSimpleReader XML parsing functionality of the Qt 5 Core Compatibility APIs module (Qt 6) and the Qt XML module (Qt 5).
title: Uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in QXmlSimpleReader XML parsing impacts Qt

desc: WonderCMS before 3.7.0 contains an unverified password change vulnerability in the saveAction functionality that allows an authenticated attacker to change the administrator password without re-authentication. Attackers can exploit this missing re-verification check during password changes to bypass re-authentication controls and maintain or escalate unauthorized access to the administrative account.
title: WonderCMS before 3.7.0 Unverified Password Change via saveAction

desc: In affected versions of Octopus Server, incorrect validation of the external identity linked to a newly registered user could result in that user receiving the LDAP-mapped team memberships and associated permissions of another user. This issue only affects instances with LDAP authentication enabled and LDAP groups mapped to Octopus teams.

In affected versions of Octopus Server, incorrect validation of changes a user made to their own LDAP identity allowed them to edit that identity even when an Administrator had disabled self-service identity editing. This could result in the user gaining membership of teams mapped to external LDAP groups they do not belong to, and potentially escalating to full administrative privileges if any of those teams are privileged.

A vulnerability was found in tjake Jlama up to 0.8.4/0.9.0-beta. Affected by this vulnerability is the function SafeTensorIndex.loadWeights of the file jlama-core/src/main/java/com/github/tjake/jlama/safetensors/SafeTensorIndex.java. Performing a manipulation of the argument weight_map results in path traversal. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.
title: tjake Jlama SafeTensorIndex.java SafeTensorIndex.loadWeights path traversal

desc: Gutenverse Form plugin for WordPress before 3.2.2 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject spreadsheet formula-trigger characters by submitting free-text field values to the public form-submit REST route, which sanitizes input with sanitize_text_field() without stripping characters such as =, +, @, or a leading minus. Attackers can store malicious formulas in entry-data post meta that are later exported unneutralized via fputcsv() or esc_html() in the CSV export functions, causing the formula to execute when an administrator opens the exported file, enabling data exfiltration to an attacker-controlled URL or command execution on the administrator's workstation.
products: jegstudio:gutenverse form – contact form builder, block form & booking form
title: Gutenverse Form WordPress Plugin < 3.2.2 CSV Formula Injection via Form Submission

desc: The Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket (/tmp/dynamic_socket) without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.
title: Local privilege escalation to root in the DynamicCLI daemon via local world-writable control socket

desc: Arbitrary data can be read or written through git-fast-import(1) and git-fast-export(1) features not marked unsafe
title: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control in Git

desc: Out-of-bounds write possible in Git when git-merge(1) used on tag with more than two GPG signatures
title: Out-of-bounds Write in Git

desc: Out-of-bounds read can crash git-apply(1) when binary patch inflates to very large size
title: Out-of-bounds Read in Git

desc: In affected versions of Octopus Server, insufficient validation of custom claims on OIDC accounts allowed a user with permission to edit accounts to cause Octopus Server to issue signed OIDC tokens that impersonate a different project. This could grant access to external systems, such as cloud providers or other Octopus instances, that trust that project's identity.

On Scalable Platforms, an administrator with permissions to edit and install the Access Control Policy and NAT rules can create a NAT rule that redirects traffic to the Gateway's Sync interface, bypassing the built-in Sync protection. This could allow the administrator to execute operating system commands and write files on the Gateway with superuser privileges.
title: Administrator with policy and NAT permissions can bypass Sync network protection on Scalable Platforms

desc: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication controls to access restricted resources on the Citrix NetScaler Console appliance
title: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication controls to access restricted resources on the Citrix NetScaler Console appliance

desc: An input and authorization validation vulnerability in Gaia Portal backend handlers could allow an authenticated, non-administrative user to perform privileged operations that should be restricted to administrators.
title: Input Validation Vulnerability in Gaia Portal backend handlers allows privilege escalation by an authenticated user

desc: Zohocorp ManageEngine DDI Central versions below 6301 is affected by an authentication bypass vulnerability in Windows DNS and DHCP agent synchronization APIs, allowing unauthenticated user to impersonate onboarded Windows servers and perform unauthorized DNS and DHCP modifications.
title: Authentication Bypass

desc: Zohocorp ManageEngine DDI Central versions below 6301 is affected by an improper authorization vulnerability that allowed authenticated non-administrative users to delete DNS zones outside their assigned scope.
title: Broken Access Control

desc: Zohocorp ManageEngine DDI Central versions below 6301 is affected by an authorization bypass vulnerability that allowed authenticated non-administrative users to modify Windows DHCP filter-list configurations across unauthorized clusters.
title: Broken Access Control

desc: Zohocorp ManageEngine DDI Central versions below 6301 is affected by an authorization bypass vulnerability that allowed authenticated non-administrative users to modify DHCP options on subnets belonging to unauthorized clusters.
title: Broken Access Control

desc: Zohocorp ManageEngine DDI Central versions below 6301 is affected by an authorization bypass and PowerShell command injection vulnerability that allowed authenticated non-administrative users to target unauthorized Windows DHCP subnets and potentially execute arbitrary commands on managed Windows DHCP servers through crafted DNS suffix values.
title: Authenticated command injection

desc: Backup Migration before 2.1.8 for WordPress contains a path traversal vulnerability in its PclZip restore fallback that allows an attacker to achieve arbitrary file write when an administrator restores a malicious backup archive on a server lacking the PHP zip extension. Attackers can craft a zip archive with entry names containing ".." sequences, which PclZip's extract() processes without the PCLZIP_OPT_EXTRACT_DIR_RESTRICTION option, writing a PHP file outside the intended extraction directory into the web-servable tree to achieve remote code execution.
title: Backup Migration before 2.1.8 Path Traversal via PclZip Restore Fallback

desc:
The MISP Modules website component contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the external tools management interface. The /external_tools/list endpoint returned stored API keys (the api_key field) in its JSON response via the ExternalTools model serializer. Additionally, the browser-based edit form pre-populated the API key input field with the stored credential value, exposing it in the DOM.

The /external_tools/list endpoint is accessible without authentication (the regression tests verify the response for both authenticated and unauthenticated clients), meaning any network-reachable client could retrieve the API keys for all configured external tools. These keys are used by the server to authenticate submissions to external analysis or enrichment services, so their disclosure allows an attacker to impersonate the MISP instance or directly access those external services.

The vulnerability also affected the edit workflow: the change_config endpoint previously required the API key to be present and non-empty on every save, forcing the key to round-trip through the client. The browser JavaScript stored the key in a reactive state object and updated the in-memory tool list with the credential value, further increasing the window of exposure in client-side memory and network traffic.

Affected component: the website sub-application of MISP Modules, specifically the external_tools module (serializer in models.py, list endpoint, and the external_tools_index.html template). The impact is limited to confidentiality of the stored API keys; no integrity or availability impact on the MISP Modules website itself is indicated by the patch.
title: MISP Modules Website Exposes External Tool API Keys in /external_tools/list Response

desc: A cleartext storage flaw was found in the AAP Gateway Operator. When reconciling an AutomationController, the operator reads the protected resource-server Secret (Secret/<aap-name>-resource-server, key controller_resource_server_secret) and copies its plaintext value into the generated AutomationController custom resource under spec.extra_settings (RESOURCE_SERVER.SECRET_KEY). Although the operator uses no_log to keep the value out of its own logs, serializing it into the custom resource exposes it to any principal able to read the AutomationController CR without permission to read the backing Kubernetes Secret, breaking the expected OpenShift RBAC separation between the two resources. The value may also propagate into Kubernetes API/etcd storage, GitOps and Argo diffs and history, rendered manifests, support bundles, and audit data. The resource-server secret is intended for trusted Gateway-to-Controller service authentication, and its disclosure may allow a user to impersonate a trusted Controller service and reach privileged service-index APIs.
products: red hat:red hat ansible automation platform 2
title: Aap-gateway-operator: resource-server secret exposed in plaintext in the automationcontroller custom resource

desc: A host key verification flaw was found in ansible-pylibssh and in the ansible.netcommon libssh connection plugin. When trust-on-first-use is enabled (host_key_auto_add on the libssh connection plugin, or AutoAddPolicy in ansible-pylibssh), a host that is already present in known_hosts but now presents a different key is accepted without warning. The pylibssh Session.verify_knownhost() method passes the SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_CHANGED and SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_OTHER states to the same missing_host_key() policy hook used for unknown hosts, and the bundled AutoAddPolicy/RejectPolicy classes (as well as ansible.netcommon's MyAddPolicy, which is modeled on paramiko's AutoAddPolicy) therefore add the changed key and continue the connection rather than aborting as paramiko's BadHostKeyException path would. As a result the controller authenticates to the substitute host, runs the play there, and appends the new key to known_hosts, which can disclose connection credentials to an attacker performing a machine-in-the-middle attack. Default configurations (host_key_checking enabled, host_key_auto_add unset) are not affected; non-interactive runs fail closed.
products: red hat:red hat ansible automation platform 2
title: Ansible-pylibssh: accepts a changed ssh host key when host_key_auto_add is enabled

desc: A link-following flaw was found in the authorized_key module of the ansible.posix collection, residual to the fix for CVE-2026-11837. That fix guards only the final path component (os.chown with follow_symlinks=False and O_NOFOLLOW in _safe_open_write()). When an unprivileged local user replaces their ~/.ssh directory with a symlink to a directory they do not own, and an operator subsequently runs the authorized_key task as root (a common provisioning pattern), the module resolves its path operations through the symlink: atomic_move() writes the temporary file in the symlink target and renames it to <target>/authorized_keys, creating or overwriting a file in the attacker-chosen directory, and os.chmod(sshdir, 0o700) follows the symlink and changes the target directory's permissions. The written file is chowned to the unprivileged user, so this is not a privilege escalation, but it allows an attacker to create or overwrite files (for example in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/, which APT reads regardless of file ownership) to cause integrity and availability impacts.
title: Ansible.posix: authorized_key module follows a parent-directory symlink allowing writes outside the intended directory

desc: Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the Guththila XML parser wrapper of Apache Axis2/C. On some malformed XML input the Guththila parser returned a raw input byte in place of an event code, and the AXIOM reader wrapper used that value as an index into a ten-entry lookup table without checking its range, reading heap memory past the end of the table. An unauthenticated client could trigger this by sending a crafted XML request to a server built with Guththila, the default parser, causing the request to be parsed incorrectly or, in some cases, the process to crash. The memory read is not returned to the client. This issue affects Apache Axis2/C: through 2.0.0. The fix is available in commits 23110287924e79d05a5b4712298c355d1f05c606 and f01683ec10e8fddb87279ec9351b3239021223e6 and will be included in the next release.
title: Apache Axis2/C: Out-of-bounds read in the Guththila XML reader wrapper

desc: The MISP Modules website component exposes external tool management endpoints (add, delete, change status, and change configuration) that did not enforce the optional administrator authentication policy. When ADMIN_PASSWORD was configured in the application environment, the module configuration endpoints correctly required an authenticated administrator session, but the external tools management handlers processed requests from anonymous users without any authorization check. An unauthenticated attacker with network access to the website could add arbitrary external tools, delete existing tools, toggle their active status, and modify their configurations including API keys and ingestion URLs. This inconsistency allowed bypass of the intended access control for the external tools management functionality. The vulnerability is conditional on ADMIN_PASSWORD being set; installations without an admin password intentionally permit open management access by design. The affected component is the external_tools Flask blueprint within the MISP Modules website application.

desc: An incorrect authorization flaw was found in AWX, the automation controller component of Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform. The API access classes for JobTemplate and WorkflowJobTemplate do not check the caller's Credential use_role when assigning the single-valued webhook_credential foreign key: JobTemplateAccess.can_add/can_change and WorkflowJobTemplateAccess.can_change in awx/main/access.py omit the check_related('webhook_credential', Credential, ..., role_field='use_role') call that UnifiedCredentialsMixin.can_attach performs for the normal many-to-many credentials relationship, and the serializer validates only the credential's type and namespace. A user who may administer their own job template (or workflow job template) and use its project and inventory can therefore attach a webhook token credential (for example a GitLab token) that they do not have use permission on. The template administrator can retrieve the template's webhook key; a subsequent webhook event causes AWX to decrypt the attached token and send it in the request header (for GitLab, PRIVATE-TOKEN) to a status URL derived from the event payload, disclosing the victim's token to a destination the attacker can influence. This may disclose another user's personal access token and allow whatever actions that token permits.
products: red hat:red hat ansible automation platform 2
title: Awx: webhook credential assignment omits use_role check, exposing another user's token

desc: A vulnerability in the administration REST interface of Azul Payara allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to bypass secure-admin remote-access restrictions by supplying an arbitrary value in the X-GlassFish-authToken HTTP header. The header's presence waives the remote-rejection check before the token is validated, and an invalid token falls through to password-based authentication, which succeeds without credentials on default domains configured with an empty administrative password. Successful exploitation grants execution of arbitrary administrative commands, equivalent to complete compromise of the server.
title: Azul Payara Administration REST Interface Authentication Bypass via X-GlassFish-authToken Header Leading to Remote Code Execution
