desc: The Wikidata Lookup expansion module (wiki.py) in MISP misp-modules contained a SPARQL injection vulnerability. The handler function constructed a SPARQL query by directly concatenating the user-supplied text value into the query string without any escaping or parameterization: 'SELECT ?item WHERE { ?item rdfs:label"' + request.get("text") + '" @en }'. An authenticated MISP user with access to the module could supply a crafted text attribute value containing SPARQL syntax (quotes, closing braces, UNION, SERVICE, LIMIT, etc.) to alter the structure of the query sent to the Wikidata SPARQL endpoint. This could allow an attacker to modify the query logic, extract unintended data, or cause the query to fail in ways that expose internal error details. Additionally, the old error handling path formatted raw exception objects into the response string ('wikidata API not accessible {}'.format(e)), potentially leaking internal information such as proxy credentials, query contents, or response bodies. The module also used a spoofed browser user-agent string and the deprecated Wikidata endpoint. The vulnerability required authenticated access to the MISP instance and the ability to invoke the wiki expansion module with a text attribute. The impact is limited to manipulation of the enrichment query and potential disclosure of internal error details; it does not directly compromise the MISP server or its stored data.
title: SPARQL Injection in MISP Wikidata Lookup Module via Unescaped User Input

desc: The WP Directory Kit WordPress plugin before 1.6.3 does not properly sanitise and escape a parameter used to order results on one of its admin screens before using it in a SQL statement, relying on a keyword deny-list whose replacement order can be bypassed, making it possible for users holding the WP Directory Kit WordPress plugin before 1.6.3's custom Listing Admin role, and above, to perform SQL injection attacks.
title: WP Directory Kit < 1.6.3 - Listing Admin+ SQL Injection via 'order_by' Parameter

desc: The Descope WordPress plugin before 1.2.0 does not validate the authentication token it receives before creating a WordPress session, accepting any non-empty token, so an unauthenticated attacker can obtain a session for any existing account, including an administrator, by supplying that account's email address.
title: Descope < 1.2.0 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover

desc: The Directorist: AI-Powered Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads WordPress plugin before 8.11.1 does not prevent a listing's own author from changing its status from pending to published, allowing users with a Subscriber-level account and above to bypass the administrator's listing moderation and publish their own pending listings.
products: unknown:directorist: ai-powered business directory, listings & classified ads
title: Directorist < 8.11.1 - Subscriber+ Listing Moderation Bypass via REST Status Update

desc: Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in custom invoice payment terms. An authenticated Manager can save a crafted custom payment-term value. When an authorized user opens Invoice Settings for the same company, Akaunting inserts the stored value into a client-side event-handler expression, causing attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the victim's authenticated origin.
title: Akaunting 3.3.0 - Stored XSS in custom invoice payment terms

desc: An OS command Injection issue exists in Air Terminal 6 provided by SoftBank Corp. Arbitrary commands may be executed with the root privilege by a user who can log in to the web management console of the affected product.

The Oxygen MyData for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 3.0.9 does not have proper authorisation, nor validate the authenticity of the request, on one of its payment callbacks, allowing unauthenticated users to mark arbitrary WooCommerce orders as completed.
title: Oxygen MyData for WooCommerce 3.0.0 - 3.0.8 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Order Completion via EveryPay Status Callback

desc: The Crop Thumbnails WordPress plugin before 1.10.0 does not perform object-level authorization when reading and re-cropping media attachments, allowing any authenticated user with the upload capability (the Author role by default) to read the metadata of, and overwrite the generated thumbnail files and stored metadata of, media attachments belonging to other users.
title: Crop-Thumbnails < 1.10.0 - Author+ Arbitrary Attachment Read and Overwrite via crop REST Endpoints

desc: The Photo Gallery by 10Web  WordPress plugin before 1.8.49 does not escape a shortcode attribute that sets a gallery watermark image before rendering it into an HTML image attribute, and decodes percent-encoded characters in the value, allowing users with Contributor-level access and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the browser of any user, including an administrator, who views the published gallery.
title: Photo Gallery by 10Web < 1.8.49 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via watermark_url Shortcode Attribute

UNIX symbolic link (symlink) following vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.

This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/spec/specs_mount.c.



This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.



If an attacker can get the victim or the platform to run their crafted malicious image, they can cause the iSulad daemon to copy sensitive host directories into an anonymous volume when creating a container, which the container can then read.

Use of Externally-Controlled format string vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.

This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/image/oci/oci_load.c.



This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.



When the iSulad daemon performs container lifecycle operations (such as create, start, exec, stop, etc.) through the isula runtime (shim), the daemon reads the stderr output of the shim process via a pipe for error information display. If the buffer contains format specifiers such as %s, %x, or %n, it may trigger a format string vulnerability, potentially leading to information leakage, denial of service, or the risk of arbitrary writes.

Relative path traversal vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.

This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/image/oci/oci_load.c.



This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.



In oci_load.c, oci_load_process_manifest() does not sanitize the Config path of manifest.json. A malicious tar package can enable the isulad with the root permission to read any file on the host.

Missing release of memory after effective lifetime vulnerability in openEuler iSulad on Linux.

This vulnerability is associated with program file src/daemon/modules/spec/specs_mount.c.



This issue affects iSulad: through 2.1.6.



The memory leak vulnerability causes the iSulad daemon to be triggered frequently, exhausting the host machine's memory and ultimately leading to an OOM crash of the daemon, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).

desc: An integer underflow in Zephyr's IPv4 option handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to read stack memory. When replying to an ICMP Echo Request that carries an IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp option, icmpv4_update_record_route() and icmpv4_update_time_stamp() in subsys/net/ip/icmpv4.c compute the length of the already recorded data as ptr - ptr_offset in uint8_t arithmetic. The attacker-controlled Pointer field is checked against the option length but not against the RFC 791 minimum (4 for Record Route, 5 for Timestamp), so a smaller value wraps the length to up to 252 bytes. net_pkt_write() then reads past the 40-byte opt_data stack buffer and up to 213 bytes of stack memory, which can include stack and heap pointers, are returned in the ICMP Echo Reply. A single packet triggers the leak and the device does not crash, so it can be repeated. Devices built with CONFIG_NET_IPV4_HDR_OPTIONS, which CONFIG_NET_IPV4_IGMP selects, are affected.
title: ICMPv4 Record Route / Timestamp option: stack OOB read via ptr underflow in icmpv4.c

desc_es:
Vulnerabilidad de ejecución remota de código por desbordamiento de búfer basado en memoria dinámica (heap) en el análisis sintáctico de archivos ILBM en libilbm. Esta vulnerabilidad permite a atacantes remotos ejecutar código arbitrario en las instalaciones afectadas de libilbm. Se requiere la interacción del usuario para explotar esta vulnerabilidad, ya que el objetivo debe visitar una página maliciosa o abrir un archivo malicioso.

El fallo específico existe dentro del análisis de archivos ILBM. El problema se debe a la falta de validación adecuada de la longitud de los datos suministrados por el usuario antes de copiarlos en un búfer basado en memoria dinámica (heap). Un atacante puede aprovechar esta vulnerabilidad para ejecutar código en el contexto del proceso actual. Anteriormente identificado como ZDI-CAN-27792.
title: libilbm ILBM File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write before the start of an allocated data structure. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-30736.
title: OriginLab Origin Viewer OGWU File Parsing Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

desc: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in ExpressTech Quiz And Survey Master quiz-master-next allows Code Injection.This issue affects Quiz And Survey Master: from n/a through 11.3.0.
title: WordPress Quiz And Survey Master plugin <= 11.3.0 - Content Injection vulnerability

desc: Missing Authorization vulnerability in ExpressTech Quiz And Survey Master quiz-master-next allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Quiz And Survey Master: from n/a through 11.3.0.
title: WordPress Quiz And Survey Master plugin <= 11.3.0 - Broken Access Control vulnerability

desc:
Data::Dump::Streamer versions before 3.00 for Perl allow code injection via unescaped Regexp patterns in _dump_qr.

A Regexp's pattern is written into a qr literal without escaping "$" or "@", so "@{[ ... ]}" and "${\ ... }" in the pattern run as code when the dump is evaluated. An already escaped delimiter gets a second backslash, which leaves the delimiter bare and ends the qr literal early.

An attacker who supplies a pattern that an application compiles, dumps and later restores with eval or do can run arbitrary Perl code.
title: Data::Dump::Streamer versions before 3.00 for Perl allow code injection via unescaped Regexp patterns in _dump_qr

desc: A vulnerability has been found in rmalright TR-VISION HOME 2.0.5. Impacted is the function sub_11504 in the library WFanManager.sys of the component IOCTL Handler. Such manipulation leads to incorrect default permissions. The attack must be carried out locally. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.
title: rmalright TR-VISION HOME IOCTL WFanManager.sys sub_11504 default permission

desc: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Crocoblock JetEngine jet-engine allows Stored XSS.This issue affects JetEngine: from n/a through 3.9.1.
title: WordPress JetEngine plugin <= 3.9.1 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability

desc: A flaw has been found in H3C ICG2000 Unified Communication Gateway 2023. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file /wnm/check.j of the component Web Management Module. Executing a manipulation can lead to missing authentication. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been published and may be used. The researcher claims that the vendor has acknowledged receipt of the vulnerability report. No further response has been received.
title: H3C ICG2000 Unified Communication Gateway Web Management check.j missing authentication

desc: Zipline 4.3.2 before 4.8.0 contains a rate limit bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade throttling by spoofing X-Forwarded-For headers when core.trustProxy is enabled. Attackers can send a different X-Forwarded-For value per request to obtain fresh rate-limit buckets, enabling unlimited guessing of login passwords, TOTP codes, and file and URL passwords.
title: Zipline 4.3.2 before 4.8.0 Rate Limit Bypass via Spoofed X-Forwarded-For

desc: Zipline 4.0.0 before 4.8.0 contains an upload filter bypass vulnerability that allows users with upload access to store blocked file types due to extension format mismatch. The upload and partial handlers compare dotted, case-sensitive extensions against undotted disabledExtensions entries, letting authenticated or permitted unauthenticated folder uploaders bypass administrator restrictions.
title: Zipline 4.0.0 before 4.8.0 Disabled Extensions Upload Filter Bypass via Extension Format Mismatch

desc: ClickMigrate is a database migration tool for ClickHouse with automatic SQL migration management and version tracking. Prior to version 1.0.3, a path traversal vulnerability in the revision command allowed a crafted migration name supplied via the -m argument to escape the intended migrations directory. Under specific conditions, an attacker could cause the tool to create a .sql file in an arbitrary location writable by the user executing the command. This issue is only exploitable if an attacker can influence the migration name passed to the revision command, such as through an insecure automation or CI/CD pipeline that forwards untrusted input. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.3.
title: ClickMigrate has Path Traversal in "revision -m" argument

desc: Zipline before 4.8.0 contains a race condition vulnerability in src/server/routes/raw/[id].ts that allows remote attackers to bypass file maxViews limits through non-atomic view counting. Attackers holding a file link can send parallel requests that read the same pre-increment count, viewing view-limited or delete-on-max-views files beyond their limit.
title: Zipline before 4.8.0 maxViews Limit Bypass via Race Condition

desc: Information leak in Skia in Google Chrome prior to 157.0.8103.78 allowed a remote attacker to obtain cross-origin data via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: High)

Zipline 4.6.2 before 4.8.0 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to evade administrator-disabled MIME types by editing file metadata. Attackers can upload a permitted file, then set a disabled type such as text/html through PATCH /api/user/files/:id so /raw/:id serves that Content-Type.
title: Zipline 4.6.2 before 4.8.0 Disabled MIME Type Policy Bypass via File Metadata Update

desc: A flaw was found in the Konflux UI proxy. Hostname values defined in the KonfluxUI custom resource are inserted directly into proxy configuration files without adequate validation or sanitization. An authenticated user with permissions to modify the custom resource can inject malicious configuration directives to bypass authentication and authorization controls, potentially exposing internal backend services. In addition, providing malformed input can cause the configuration generator to fail, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) by preventing the proxy from starting.
title: Konflux-ci: unvalidated hostname fields enable caddyfile config injection in the konflux ui proxy generator, allowing an unauthenticated route to be spliced ahead of the forward_auth/impersonate autho

desc: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants. From version 0.15.0 to before version 0.27.0, resolving the CSS counters(name, sep) function in generated content was bounded neither in the size of a single expansion nor in the aggregate work across an element tree. An attacker able to submit HTML/CSS to a fulgur-based conversion service can trigger CPU and memory exhaustion with a trivially small payload, denying service to the host and any co-tenants. This issue has been patched in version 0.27.0.
title: fulgur: Unbounded counters() expansion in generated content causes memory/CPU exhaustion (denial of service)

desc: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants. From version 0.4.4 to before version 0.29.0, the CSS string-set named-string values resolved from a document were accumulated per element with no memory budget, letting a small crafted document amplify into large retained memory (and the CPU to copy it) — results in a denial of service. This issue has been patched in version 0.29.0.
title: fulgur: Unbounded string-set value accumulation causes memory/CPU exhaustion (denial of service)

desc: An internal security review identified a development regression from ThinkSystem v4 XClarity Controller 3 (XCC3) versions (2.51) IHX432Y to (2.56) IHX436K which re-introduces the default OpenBMC root password upon performing an XCC Reset to Default operation.  An attacker can gain access to enabled administrative interfaces of XCC using the default OpenBMC credential re-introduced after Reset to Default. Additionally, this provides access to the underlying XCC Operating System which is not normally accessible. Only these versions are affected and are no longer available for download. Process enhancements have also been made to prevent and identify potential future regression.
title: Default OpenBMC Root Credential Reintroduced After Reset to Defaults in ThinkSystem v4 XCC3

desc: Paaster is a pastebin application. Prior to version 3.3.0, Paaster's account login has no rate limiting, lockout, or CAPTCHA of any kind, and a companion endpoint openly discloses whether a username exists along with that account's password-hashing salts. Together these let an attacker enumerate real accounts and then brute-force their passwords with unlimited, unthrottled attempts. This issue has been patched in version 3.3.0.
title: Paaster: No rate limiting on account login, combined with a public username-enumeration/salt endpoint, enables offline credential-stuffing

desc: Paaster is a pastebin application. Prior to version 3.3.0, Paaster's "view once" (burn-after-reading) paste mode can be bypassed with concurrent requests. The check that's supposed to enforce single-use is a plain read followed by a separate write, with no atomicity, so multiple simultaneous requests can all see the paste as "not yet read" and all successfully retrieve it. This issue has been patched in version 3.3.0.
title: Paaster: TOCTOU race condition defeats the 'burn after reading' guarantee on view-once pastes

desc: fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants. From version 0.6.0 to before version 0.33.0, quadratic style-list reprocessing during containing-block resolution for absolutely-positioned pseudo-elements cause denial of service. This issue has been patched in version 0.33.0.
title: fulgur: Quadratic style-list reprocessing during containing-block resolution for absolutely-positioned pseudo-elements causes denial of servicefulgur:

desc: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.73, the HTTP workflow node in Heym makes outbound HTTP requests to user-supplied URLs without validation of the target host or IP address. If a workflow author has already configured an HTTP node that targets internal addresses such as cloud metadata endpoints or private network hosts, and exposed the workflow with anonymous execution, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger the preconfigured SSRF sink. The same project has comprehensive SSRF protection in its MCP integration, which is absent from the HTTP node. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.73.
title: Heym: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in HTTP Workflow Node

desc: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.75, the same POST /api/mcp/fetch-tools endpoint (any authenticated user, lowest role) also accepts the stdio transport, which spawns the attacker-supplied command with attacker-supplied args and an environment merged over os.environ. The process executes on the shared backend host before MCP protocol validation fails — so side effects fire regardless of whether the command speaks MCP. This is a distinct weakness class and exploit primitive from the SSRF (Advisory 2) on the same endpoint, and needs a different fix (role gating / opt-in trust boundary rather than egress controls). This issue has been patched in version 0.0.75.
title: Heym: Command execution via POST /api/mcp/fetch-tools stdio transport: supplied command is spawned before MCP validation

desc: taOS is a self-hosted AI agent OS. Prior to version 1.0.0-beta.25, tinyagentos (taOS) registers all system settings routes under a single APIRouter() instance created with no admin authorization dependency. Any authenticated user—including non-admin invited users whose is_admin flag is explicitly False—can read the full system configuration, overwrite it, modify platform settings, trigger a git pull + dependency reinstall + service restart, and switch the tracked update branch. Successful exploitation of the write endpoints causes immediate configuration corruption or a denial of service for all users on the instance from a low-privileged account. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0-beta.25.
title: taOS: Non-Admin Users Can Access System Settings and Update Actions

desc: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.71, Heym's workflow engine accepts an arbitrary Python code string in the playwrightCode field of a Playwright node. This string is written to a temporary .py file and executed directly by the backend process via subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, script_path]) with no sandboxing, AST validation, or role gate. Any authenticated user — including a freshly registered account — can achieve full remote code execution (RCE) on the backend host, running as the service process user (observed as root in the default Docker deployment). This issue has been patched in version 0.0.71.
title: Heym: Playwright Custom Code Backend RCE via `playwrightCode` Field

desc: taOS is a self-hosted AI agent OS. Prior to version 1.0.0-beta.23, the POST /api/skill-exec/{skill_id}/call endpoint in taOS executes built-in skills — including the code_exec skill which runs arbitrary Python via subprocess.run(["python3", "-c", code]) — without performing any admin role check, skill ownership check, or agent assignment verification. Any authenticated non-admin user can supply attacker-controlled Python code in the request body and have it executed as the taOS backend process user on the host, achieving full remote code execution with no privilege escalation required beyond a valid (non-admin) session. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0-beta.23.
title: taOS: Authenticated Non-Admin Host Code Execution via Skill Runtime

desc: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, team-member management (add / remove / update) is gated only on team membership, not on the team creator/admin role — and TeamMember has no role column. Any non-creator member can seat an attacker account into the team; because credential team-shares are scoped only by TeamMember.user_id, the newly-added attacker can then decrypt every credential shared into that team (provider API keys, OAuth tokens. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.
title: Heym: Missing role gate in team-member management lets any member add/remove members, exposing team-shared credentials

desc: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, POST /api/mcp/fetch-tools is reachable by any authenticated user (lowest role; no admin/workflow association) and fetches an attacker-supplied URL through the sse and streamable_http transports with no scheme / private-IP / allowlist / redirect guard. The transport error is reflected in the HTTP 422 response, giving a semi-blind SSRF oracle, and the attacker also controls the outbound request headers. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.
title: Heym: SSRF via POST /api/mcp/fetch-tools: any authenticated user reaches local/private URLs through the SSE and streamable-HTTP transports

desc: Portabase is a database backup and restore tool for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MsSQL, MariaDB, Firebird SQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Redis, Files and Docker Volume. Prior to version 1.21.2, a path traversal in the TUS upload webhook handler (app/api/tus/hooks/route.ts) allowed an unauthenticated attacker to overwrite arbitrary files under the private data directory, including /data/private/keys/master_key.bin (the AES-256-GCM master key). This issue has been patched in version 1.21.2.
title: Portabase: Unauthenticated path traversal in TUS webhook overwrites AES-256-GCM master key

desc: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, get_workflow_template / get_node_template fetches a template by ID with no visibility / author / shared_with predicate, so any authenticated user can read (and use) any other tenant's private (visibility=specific_users) template — including its full node/edge graph and the email addresses it was shared with. The list endpoint enforces visibility correctly; the single-item get/use paths do not. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.
title: Heym - Horizontal IDOR: get-by-id on workflow/node templates skips the visibility check the list path enforces

desc: Livewire PowerGrid creates data tables based on Laravel Livewire library. From version 6.0.0 to before version 6.10.4, the public Livewire property sortDirection is interpolated verbatim into a raw SQL ORDER BY clause and is not restricted to asc/desc, allowing arbitrary SQL injection through POST /livewire/update. This issue has been patched in version 6.10.4.
title: Livewire PowerGrid: SQL Injection through the public `sortDirection` Livewire property in the `naturalSort` order-by path

desc: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, heym hardens one untrusted-code path but not its sibling. The Python tool executor (python_tool_executor.py) treats user code as untrusted and mandates a Docker sandbox (no network, read-only fs, non-root, no docker socket), failing closed. The skill executor (skill_python_executor.py) runs skill Python via a local backend subprocess with no Docker isolation — only a 512 MB RLIMIT and a 7-key env denylist — so a skill executes inside the backend execution context, with filesystem access, network egress, and non-denylisted environment variables that should not be exposed to untrusted/shared skills. In the shipped Docker config (backend runs as root + /var/run/docker.sock mounted), this escalates to host root. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.
title: Heym Unsandboxed skill code execution: skills run via a local backend subprocess without the Docker isolation that Python tools mandate

ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.5, ideon's link-preview endpoint requires no authentication at all and forwards any URL a caller supplies straight into a server-side fetch. The app does have a general-purpose SSRF guard (safeFetch/validateSafeUrl in src/app/lib/ssrf.ts), but this route sits behind no login check whatsoever, making it a fully open, anonymous URL-fetch relay - and the guard's IP blocklist itself has a gap that lets it reach the server's own loopback interface via the 0.0.0.0 "any address" bypass, a well-documented SSRF-filter evasion technique on Linux. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.5.
title: ideon: Unauthenticated /api/links/preview endpoint is an open SSRF relay, and its IP blocklist misses the 0.0.0.0/:: unspecified-address bypass

desc: Helio is an MCP proxy that sits between AI agents and the tools they use. Prior to version 0.8.0, the dashboard sideband (default 127.0.0.1:3100) validated CORS request origins by matching the hostname against a private-network string prefix (10., 172.16.–172.31., 192.168.) rather than validating an IP address. A public DNS name such as 192.168.attacker.com, 10.evil.io, or 172.16.pwn.example also satisfies that prefix, so the proxy echoed the attacker origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin. This issue has been patched in version 0.8.0.
title: Helio: Dashboard sideband CORS origin allowlist matches hostnames by prefix, admitting attacker-controlled origins in open mode

desc: Laradocs maintains version-controlled documentation inside a Laravel codebase. From version 0.4.0 to before version 1.0.0, Laradocs is vulnerable to local command injection in server-side KaTeX rendering via an unescaped Node.js binary path in a proc_open() command string. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.0.
title: Laradocs: Command injection via unescaped Node.js binary path in KaTeX SSR

desc: nginx-http-flv-module is a media streaming server based on nginx-rtmp-module. Prior to version 1.2.14, if a server received an HTTP/1.0 request without a header Host, which was permitted by HTTP core of Nginx, then r->headers_in.host was NULL, nginx-http-flv-module used r->headers_in.host->value to make a pseudo tcUrl, so NULL-pointer dereference happened. This issue has been patched in version 1.2.14.
title: NULL-pointer dereference (DoS) in nginx-http-flv-module

desc: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.4, validateUrlForSSRF() / safeFetch() in lib/oauth/ssrf-protection.ts (and the parallel validateMcpUrl() in lib/security/validators.ts) perform SSRF host-blocking by string/regex matching on new URL(url).hostname. Their IPv6 branch only recognises the textual forms ::1, fe80:/fc00:/fd00: prefixes, and the dotted-decimal IPv4-mapped form ::ffff:127.x. It does not recognise the WHATWG-canonical IPv4-mapped-IPv6 host that Node emits for a mapped address, which is hex-compressed and bracket-wrapped: [::ffff:7f00:1] for 127.0.0.1, [::ffff:a9fe:a9fe] for 169.254.169.254. An authenticated user who registers a STREAMABLE_HTTP / SSE MCP server with URL http://[::ffff:7f00:1]:PORT/ (loopback) or http://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/ (cloud metadata) passes both guards, and the server-side OAuth-discovery action then fetches that host, yielding server-side request forgery to loopback and to the cloud metadata service. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.4.
title: ideon: Unauthenticated SSRF in /api/proxy/image via WHATWG bracketed/hex-mapped IPv6 bypass of isSafeUrl guard

desc: blueprintUE Self-Hosted Edition before 4.3.6 contains an iframe injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to embed arbitrary third-party content by abusing the PeerTube video URL matcher in BlueprintService::findVideoProvider(). Attackers can set a blueprint video URL on an attacker-controlled host, which site.js loads in an unsandboxed iframe after consent, framing fake login forms or malware downloads.
title: blueprintUE Self-Hosted Edition before 4.3.6 Arbitrary Iframe Embedding via PeerTube Matcher

desc: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.4, several project mutation endpoints under /api/projects/[id]/* resolve the caller's project role but never enforce it, so a user who was granted only the read-only viewer role on a project can perform write operations on that project. The most severe is POST /api/projects/[id]/graph, which deletes every block and link in the project and re-inserts client-supplied ones. A viewer can silently rewrite or wipe the entire canvas of a project they were invited to read. The application clearly intends viewer to be read-only: the collaborators endpoint, the automation endpoints, and the realtime Yjs sync path all reject write attempts from viewers. These specific HTTP handlers simply omit the guard their siblings enforce. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.4.
title: ideon: Read-only project viewers can wipe and rewrite the canvas and tamper with blocks/files via role-unchecked project endpoints

desc: WWBN AVideo through 29.7.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in objects/import.json.php that allows uploaders to import other users' MP4 files by referencing any folder under videos/. Attackers can copy private, unlisted, password-protected or pay-per-view videos, read victims' .txt/.html sidecars as descriptions, list files via objects/listFiles.json.php, and delete victims' media using the delete parameter.
title: WWBN AVideo through 29.7.1 Missing Authorization via objects/import.json.php

desc: BookStack before 26.09.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to access other users' unpublished draft page images by checking only PageView permission without draft status. Attackers can read drawio data via the base64 endpoint or rename, replace, or delete draft images by sequential ID to disclose or tamper with unpublished work.
title: BookStack before 26.09.3 Incorrect Authorization via Image and Drawio Endpoints

desc: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.21 and 1.7.x before 1.7.6 contains an IMAP command injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject commands via CRLF in the _uid parameter when messages_cache is enabled. Attackers can lure logged-in victims into opening crafted GET links to mail/show or mail/get, executing IMAP commands that delete messages, change flags, or grant mailbox access via SETACL.
title: Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.21 and 1.7.6 IMAP Command Injection via _uid

desc: blueprintUE Self-Hosted Edition before 4.3.7 contains an insecure default configuration in its Docker Compose examples that sets MYSQL_ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes in database.env and publishes MariaDB on port 3306. Unauthenticated attackers reaching the Docker host on port 3306 can log in as root without a password to read, modify, or delete user accounts, blueprints, and all databases.
title: blueprintUE Self-Hosted Edition before 4.3.7 Empty MariaDB Root Password via Docker Compose

desc: WWBN AVideo 29.1.0 through 29.7.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject markup through the channel About field rendered in feed/index.php. Attackers can store an unquoted event-handler payload that bypasses feedHtmlDescription() filtering and executes via rss-style.xsl for any visitor, including administrators, viewing the channel feed.
title: WWBN AVideo 29.1.0 through 29.7.1 Stored XSS via Channel RSS Feed

desc: WWBN AVideo through 29.7.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows delegated Videos Admin users to obtain video_id_hash values bound to any video owner via encoder endpoints like aVideoEncoderStatus.json.php. Attackers can request the hash for an administrator-owned video and replay it through useVideoHashOrLogin() for password-less login, gaining plugin upload, configuration, and user management access.
title: WWBN AVideo through 29.7.1 Privilege Escalation via Encoder video_id_hash

desc: WWBN AVideo 12.4 through 29.7.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the ADs plugin deleteImage.json.php that allows authenticated users with custom ads to delete arbitrary files. Attackers can set the unvalidated is_regular_user parameter to another user's id or ../ sequences to delete other users' ads or files like videos/configuration.php, taking the site offline and re-exposing the installer.
title: WWBN AVideo 12.4 through 29.7.1 Path Traversal File Deletion via deleteImage.json.php

desc: Rote through 2.6.0 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows authenticated admins to obtain super_admin rights by reading or overwriting JWT signing secrets via /v2/api/admin/settings. Attackers can retrieve the unmasked jwtSecret from the security settings group and forge HS256 tokens for the super administrator to change user roles and escalate their own account.
title: Rote through 2.6.0 Privilege Escalation via Admin Settings API JWT Secret Exposure

desc: WuzAPI through 1.1.0 contains a cross-tenant information disclosure vulnerability in the GetHistory handler that allows authenticated users to view other tenants' chat metadata. Attackers with message history enabled can request GET /chat/history with chat_jid=index to list every user's internal ID, stored chat JIDs, and last-message times.
title: WuzAPI through 1.1.0 Cross-Tenant Information Disclosure via /chat/history

desc: weDevs ERP (WP ERP) through 1.17.11 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated employees to edit their own HR records because HRM AJAX handlers check erp_edit_employee instead of erp_manage_jobinfo. Attackers can post their own user_id with the My Profile nonce to change designation, reporting manager, pay rate, and employment type, or delete job history.
title: WP ERP through 1.17.11 Incorrect Authorization via HRM Job-Info AJAX Handlers

desc: WWBN AVideo 14.3 through 29.7.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows uploaders to inject scripts via the videoDownloadedLink value stored unescaped through objects/aVideoEncoder.json.php. Attackers can embed event-handler payloads in the URL host rendered as a Source tag in view/managerVideos_body.php, executing in administrator sessions to install plugin archives containing PHP.
title: WWBN AVideo 14.3 through 29.7.1 Stored XSS via Video Source Tag

desc: Gotenberg 8.31.0 before 8.38.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in IsPublicIP() that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass private-IP deny-list protections using IPv6 zone identifiers. Attackers can append a zone such as %25eth0 to the unspecified address or blocked IPv6 prefixes in downloadFrom, webhook, or Chromium/LibreOffice URLs to reach internal services and read responses in the returned PDF.
title: Gotenberg 8.31.0 before 8.38.0 SSRF via IPv6 Zone Identifiers in IsPublicIP

desc: NextScan 1.1.0 through 1.2.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in ns-admin that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge administrator tokens using a hardcoded JWT signing key. Attackers can sign an HS256 X-Access-Token carrying the public super administrator role ID to gain full access to user management, scan tasks and stored vulnerability results.
title: NextScan 1.1.0 through 1.2.0 Hardcoded JWT Key Authentication Bypass in ns-admin

desc: Hydro @hydrooj/ui-default before 4.59.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to inject script by placing double quotes in language- class tokens within markdown-it-xss.ts. Attackers can store a payload in their profile bio that executes when administrators or other users view it, stealing the non-httpOnly sid session cookie for session hijacking.
title: Hydro @hydrooj/ui-default before 4.59.1 Stored XSS via Markdown language- Class

desc: Rote 1.2.0 through 2.6.0 contains an authorization bypass in the OAuth bind/merge endpoint that allows authenticated users to merge any OAuth-bound account into their own. Attackers can submit a public existingUserId and GitHub or Apple user ID to take over notes, attachments, and API keys and delete the victim account.
title: Rote 1.2.0 through 2.6.0 Account Takeover via OAuth Account Merge Endpoint

desc: NextScan 1.1.0 through 1.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the ns-admin URL asset detail dialog that renders crawled form request bodies (Asset_URL.data) via innerHTML without encoding. Attackers can host crafted forms on crawled sites to store JavaScript that executes when users view asset details, stealing localStorage access tokens to hijack sessions, including administrators.
title: NextScan 1.1.0 through 1.2.0 Stored XSS via URL Asset Detail View

desc: NextScan 1.1.0 through 1.2.0 contains hardcoded HTTP Basic Auth credentials in ns-admin's AuthAgent and AuthExternal routers that allow unauthenticated attackers to access protected APIs. Attackers can call /agent/config to obtain Redis passwords, etcd details and the server token, and impersonate scan nodes via registration, heartbeat and logging endpoints.
title: NextScan 1.1.0 through 1.2.0 Hardcoded Credentials in ns-admin Agent and External APIs

desc: ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.6, the SSRF protection in safeFetch is bypassed by IPv6 transition addresses that embed private IPv4 addresses. The isPrivateIP function in src/app/lib/ssrf.ts checks only a narrow set of IPv6 ranges (loopback ::1, ULA fc/fd, link-local fe80) but does not recognize IPv4-mapped (::ffff:), NAT64 well-known (64:ff9b::/96, RFC 6052), NAT64 local-use (64:ff9b:1::/48, RFC 8215), 6to4 (2002::/16, RFC 3056), or Teredo (2001::/32, RFC 4380) encodings. An authenticated user can supply these addresses in link URLs to reach cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), localhost services, and RFC 1918 internal networks through the link preview metadata fetcher. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.6.
title: ideon: SSRF protection bypass via IPv6 transition addresses (NAT64 / 6to4 / IPv4-mapped) in link preview

desc:
Server-side request forgery (SSRF) in the server registration and update API in Amazon mcp-gateway-registry before 1.35.0 might allow an authenticated remote user to send requests from the gateway to internal network services and cloud instance metadata endpoints and read the responses via a crafted request.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 1.35.0.
title: Server-side request forgery in the server registration and update API in mcp-gateway-registry

desc:
Missing authorization in the external management API in Amazon mcp-gateway-registry 1.0.9 through 1.24.7 might allow an authenticated remote user to assign the registry administrator scope to their own identity group and obtain administrative control of every registered gateway asset via a crafted group import request.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 1.25.0.
title: Missing authorization on the external management API in mcp-gateway-registry enables privilege escalation to registry administrator

desc: A flaw was found in Cockpit. A local authenticated user with control over a target account's home directory can exploit a privileged symlink dereference vulnerability in the `ssh-add-public-key.sh` helper. When this helper runs with elevated privileges, it can be tricked into following attacker-controlled symlinks within the `.ssh` or `authorized_keys` paths. This allows the attacker to arbitrarily change file ownership and modes, potentially leading to local privilege escalation and impacting the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of the system.
products: red hat:red hat openshift dev spaces
title: Cockpit: cockpit: local privilege escalation via insecure symlink handling in public key addition helper

desc: AsiaInfo BSS Platform 9.2 before 9.2.38 has a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the menu icon upload function. An authenticated user with ordinary application privileges can upload an SVG file containing embedded JavaScript, which is served from the application origin. Normal menu rendering uses an HTML element and does not execute the SVG script; exploitation requires a victim to load the uploaded SVG as a document (by directly navigating to its URL, or via

Missing rate limiting, per-account submission quota and geographic validation in the publicar_aviso RPC function in Lagarto Chivato 0.4.1 and earlier on Web allows remote authenticated attackers to flood the moderation queue via unlimited submission of notices with arbitrary coordinates.
title: Uncontrolled resource consumption via post_notice

desc: Pre-account hijacking in the authentication flow in Lagarto Chivato 0.4.1 and earlier on Web allows remote unauthenticated attackers to take over arbitrary accounts via a password planted on an unregistered email address that becomes valid upon the victim’s first passwordless login.

title: PAN-OS: Privilege Escalation Vulnerability in GlobalProtect

Cloud NGFW is not affected by this vulnerability.

desc: A server-side request forgery vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks Checkov by Prisma® Cloud enables a local unauthenticated user to make unauthorized network requests from host to internal services.
products: palo alto networks:checkov by prisma cloud

title: GlobalProtect App: Incorrect Privilege Management Vulnerability in OPSWAT MetaDefender Endpoint Security SDK on Windows

desc: Dell Terraform Provider for PowerFlex, versions 1.5.0 through 1.8.0, contains an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the SSH client component.Terraform PowerFlex provider uses ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey() as the default SSH host key callback. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to information exposure and unauthorized access.

Dell Terraform Provider for PowerStore, versions prior to 1.3.1 , contains a  vulnerability that may cause sensitive authentication data to be insufficiently redacted in diagnostic logs. desc: Dell OpenManage Ansible Modules, versions 5.0.0 through 10.0.3, contains an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the iDRACConnection component. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to information exposure and unauthorized access.

Dell OpenManage Ansible Modules, versions 9.2.0 through 10.0.3, contains an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the SessionAPI component.
