Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, the public Trust Center GraphQL API exposes Query.node(id:) with @authentication(required: OPTIONAL) — an unauthenticated internet visitor to any published trust center can call it. Six of its type branches — Organization, Framework, Audit, ThirdParty (subprocessor), TrustCenter, and TrustCenterReference — resolve the object with a tenant scope derived from the client-supplied GID itself (coredata.NewScopeFromObjectID(id)) and load it with a bare Get(scope, id) that performs no comparison to the current trust center's OrganizationID and no showOnTrustCenter/visibility check. (The Document and File branches, by contrast, correctly pass trustCenter.OrganizationID and check visibility). This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.
title: Probo: Unauthenticated cross-tenant and hidden-item disclosure via Query.node in the public Trust Center API

desc: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, an organization ADMIN can mint an OWNER membership via createUser, bypassing the owner-only set-owner authorization gate. This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.
title: Probo: Vertical privilege escalation

desc: Fider is a feedback portal for feature requests and suggestions. Prior to version 0.34.0, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability exists in Fider due to insufficient validation of webhook URLs. The application allows user-controlled URLs to be fetched by the server without restricting access to internal or external network resources. This enables attackers with administrative privileges to make arbitrary HTTP requests from the server, potentially accessing internal services or cloud metadata endpoints. This issue has been patched in version 0.34.0.
title: Fider: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Webhook URL

desc: sync-rpc runs asynchronous commands synchronously by putting them in a separate proces. Prior to version 1.3.7, if an attacker could guess the correct port and it was not blocked via a firewall, it was possible to load and execute arbitrary JavaScript files stored on the server running sync-rpc. This issue has been patched in version 1.3.7.
title: sync-rpc: Arbitrary remote code execution vulnerability

desc: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.224.0, the public Trust Center GraphQL API exposes acceptElectronicSignature and recordSigningEvent, both gated only by @authentication(required: PRESENT) @sessionOnly — any self-provisioned trust center identity can call them. The underlying esign.Service.AcceptSignature and esign.Service.recordEvent build the tenant scope from the client-supplied signatureId GID (coredata.NewScopeFromObjectID(req.SignatureID)) and load the signature by that GID. At no point do they verify that the signature belongs to the caller or that the caller's email matches the signature's SignerEmail. As a result, any authenticated trust-center visitor who possesses another visitor's signature GID can: (1) complete that visitor's NDA signature — overwriting signer name/IP/UA with attacker data and setting status to Accepted, which triggers the sealing worker to generate a completion certificate; (2) inject arbitrary audit-trail events into any signature's log. Both attacks defeat the non-repudiation and integrity guarantees of the e-signature system. This issue has been patched in version 0.224.0.
title: Probo: Broken access control in public e-signature API

desc: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.223.1, Probo's console GraphQL API is a multi-tenant GRC platform where all data is scoped to an organization. A Finding can reference a Risk via finding.riskId. That reference is stored without validating that the risk belongs to the caller's organization, and the Finding.risk field resolver authorizes the finding (caller's org) instead of the risk, then loads the risk with a tenant scope derived from the risk's own global ID. As a result, an authenticated member of organization A can attach an arbitrary organization B risk GID to a finding they own and then read organization B's Risk (name, description, treatment, category, severity, owner) — with no membership in B. The stored cross-tenant reference also blocks B from deleting its own risk (ON DELETE RESTRICT), a cross-tenant integrity/DoS. This issue has been patched in version 0.223.1.
title: Probo: Cross-tenant IDOR via unvalidated FK references

desc: Probo is a self-hostable governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform built for engineering and security teams. Prior to version 0.222.0, the GraphQL endpoint does not enforce restrictions on alias count, query depth, or query complexity. An attacker can send a single request containing thousands of aliased resolver calls, causing excessive server-side resource consumption and service degradation. This issue has been patched in version 0.222.0.
title: Probo: GraphQL Alias-Based Application Layer Denial of Service (DoS)

desc: iopress is a native HTTP server for Node.js with platform-specific async I/O. Prior to version 1.0.5, the chunked-transfer-encoding HTTP request parser in @iopress/core reads past the end of the input buffer when a request declares a chunk size larger than the body actually received. This results in a heap-buffer-over-read. This issue has been patched in version 1.0.5.
title: iopress: buffer over-read in chunked HTTP parser

desc: Fider is a feedback portal for feature requests and suggestions. Prior to version 0.36.0, in multi-tenant mode (HOST_MODE=multi), an attacker can use an email verification key issued by Tenant A to authenticate as the same email address on Tenant B. This completely bypasses tenant isolation and allows unauthorized account takeover across tenants. Single-host deployments (HOST_MODE=single, the default) are NOT affected. This issue has been patched in version 0.36.0.
title: Fider: Cross-Tenant Authentication Bypass via Missing tenant_id Filter in getVerificationByKey

desc: REVA is an interoperability platform. Prior to versions 2.40.5 and 2.46.4, Reva exposes internal metadata folders in the spaces of an authenticated user. This can lead to unwanted ways of interaction with the data. This issue has been patched in versions 2.40.5 and 2.46.4.
title: REVA: Access to internal metadata

desc: Icinga Web 2 is an open source monitoring web interface, framework and command-line interface. Prior to versions 2.12.7 and 2.13.1, an attacker can craft a URL that, once visited by an authenticated user (or one that is able to authenticate), allows to manipulate the backend to redirect the user to any location. For this to succeed, the victim's locale in Icinga Web must be different from en_US. This issue has been patched in versions 2.12.7 and 2.13.1.
title: Icinga Web 2: Open redirect on login page, under certain circumstances

desc: geojson-vt is a JavaScript library for slicing GeoJSON data into vector tiles on the fly, primarily designed to enable rendering and interacting with large geospatial datasets on the browser side (without a server). Prior to version 6.1.1, @maplibre/geojson-vt contains an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in its GeoJSON conversion logic. When a GeoJSONVT instance is constructed with a deeply nested GeometryCollection object, the mutually recursive functions featureToInternal and convertGeometryCollection in src/convert.ts exhaust the Node.js call stack, causing an unhandled RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded that terminates the process. Because the library is widely used in server-side tile services that accept GeoJSON over the network, a remote unauthenticated attacker can trigger a denial-of-service by sending a single crafted payload. No authentication is required, and no non-default library options are needed. This issue has been patched in version 6.1.1.
title: geojson-vt: Uncontrolled Recursion in Nested GeoJSON GeometryCollection

desc: Webmin through 2.670 contains a users file injection vulnerability in acl/cert_issue.cgi that allows authenticated Webmin users to inject lines by supplying unvalidated certificate DN fields containing newlines. Attackers can end a DN field with a backslash and newline to add a second root entry with a known password hash, gaining Webmin root access after miniserv restarts.
title: Webmin through 2.670 Users File Injection via acl/cert_issue.cgi

desc: SiYuan 3.7.0 before 3.8.10 on Windows contains a path traversal vulnerability in kernel/util/webfetch.go that allows attackers to write files outside the import directory via backslash-encoded filenames. Attackers controlling a URL fetched by the MCP web_fetch or http_request tools can use %5C-encoded ..\ sequences to write chosen response bytes to directories above temp/import that are writable by the SiYuan user.
title: SiYuan 3.7.0 before 3.8.10 Path Traversal File Write via MCP web_fetch

desc: Webmin through 2.670 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in acl/save_group.cgi that allows delegated administrators to grant unauthorized modules by submitting arbitrary module lists in the mod parameter. Attackers with Webmin Users module access can create or edit groups holding modules like Command Shell and assign themselves membership to execute commands as root.
title: Webmin through 2.670 Privilege Escalation via acl/save_group.cgi

desc: Wallos 4.4.0 before 5.10.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in endpoints/cronjobs/sendnotifications.php that allows registered users to inject scripts via unescaped notification service responses. Attackers can point their Mattermost webhook URL or Web Push endpoint at a controlled server returning JavaScript, which executes in the administrator's session when sendnotifications.php is opened.
title: Wallos 4.4.0 before 5.10.3 Stored XSS via sendnotifications.php

desc: Traccar 3.15 before 6.17.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in LdapProvider.login() that fails to reject empty passwords, causing LDAP binds to be performed as unauthenticated binds when LDAP authentication is enabled. Unauthenticated attackers who know a valid username can log in via POST /api/session or HTTP Basic authentication with an empty password against directories that permit unauthenticated binds, obtaining sessions for any account including administrators.
title: Traccar 3.15 before 6.17.0 Authentication Bypass via Empty LDAP Password

desc: Social-auth-core 4.7.0 before 7.0.0 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the SAML backend that restores sessions named in the unsigned RelayState parameter. Attackers can deliver their own valid IdP response and RelayState to a victim's browser via an auto-submitting form, signing the victim into the attacker's account to capture entered data.
title: Social-auth-core 4.7.0 before 7.0.0 Login CSRF via SAML RelayState

desc: Spatie Browsershot 2.2.0 before 5.5.0 contains a local file read vulnerability that allows attackers to read server files by supplying root-relative references in HTML passed to setHtml(). Attackers can embed iframe, img, link or script elements referencing paths like /etc/passwd, which resolve to file:// URLs and render file contents into the returned PDF or screenshot.
title: Spatie Browsershot 2.2.0 before 5.5.0 Local File Read via setHtml()

desc: @tinacms/mdx before 2.4.2 contains a code injection vulnerability in its MDX serializer, which writes rich-text values into MDX expressions without escaping them. Authenticated content editors can save crafted values that break out of list field or highlightColor expressions in the stored .mdx file, executing JavaScript in visitors' browsers or on build and server-side rendering hosts.
title: @tinacms/mdx before 2.4.2 Code Injection via MDX Serializer Rich-Text Values

desc: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains a prompt injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to disclose the hidden system prompt by submitting crafted chat input to POST /api/v1/rca/chat. Attackers can instruct the assistant to ignore its rules and reveal internal orchestration instructions, aiding the crafting of further prompt injection attacks.
title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 Prompt Injection via RCA Chat Assistant

desc: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain valid JWTs by setting the client-controlled is_local_auth field. Attackers can send a POST /api/v1/user/login/ request for the admin account with an invalid password and is_local_auth true to gain SuperUser administrative access.
title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 Authentication Bypass via is_local_auth Flag

desc: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access Governance API endpoints, including /api/v1/databases. Attackers can send requests without an Authorization header, or with invalid or tampered JWT tokens, to retrieve stored database hosts, usernames, and passwords.
title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 Missing Authentication via /api/v1/databases Governance API

desc: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to inject scripts by uploading attachments with spoofed text/html Content-Type. Attackers can upload HTML files named like test.html.pdf that render in the REMS origin via Preview, executing JavaScript in victims' browsers.
title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 Stored XSS via Attachment Upload and Preview

desc: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains an improper attribution vulnerability that allows authenticated users to post comments as the incident creator via POST /api/v1/incidents/{incident_id}/comment. Lower-privileged attackers can comment on incidents owned by users such as a Super User to impersonate them and corrupt the incident timeline and audit trail.
title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 Comment Author Spoofing via Incident Comment API

desc: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to make the backend connect to arbitrary destinations through the database Test Connection feature. Attackers can set a database entry's host and port to localhost, internal addresses, or attacker-controlled servers to probe internal hosts and ports reachable from the REMS server.
title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 SSRF via Database Test Connection

desc: A deferred-callback use-after-destroy in Node.js TLS server handshake handling allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to terminate the server process. When a TLS server uses any of the SNICallback, OCSPRequest, newSession, or resumeSession hooks, or server.addContext(), the corresponding OpenSSL callbacks are deferred, and the deferred code does not handle the underlying socket being destroyed between scheduling and execution. By sending a client hello that reaches the vulnerable path (for example, no SNI together with an OCSP request) followed by padding and a socket FIN, an attacker makes OpenSSL deliver the client hello and the end-of-file in the same tick, so the socket is destroyed before the deferred callback runs and the process raises an uncaught exception instead of emitting an 'error' event. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to a remotely triggerable uncaught exception in TLS servers via deferred handshake callbacks

desc: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set an incident's reporter to another user by supplying a client-controlled reporter field. Attackers can send crafted POST /api/v1/incidents or PATCH /api/v1/incidents/{id}/status requests to falsify incident attribution and corrupt the accountability audit trail.
title: OpsTree REMS through 1.0.0 Reporter Spoofing via /api/v1/incidents

desc: Node.js discloses proxy credentials in ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages. CVE-2026-48615 established that a proxy credential must not appear in a Node.js error message and redacted the username and password from ProxyConfig.href, but that fix missed four error paths in the same subsystem, one of them inside the same constructor, which interpolate the raw proxy URL, credentials included, into an ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG message. The proxy URL comes from the environment, but the defect is the sink: a secret that Node.js redacts everywhere else is emitted verbatim into a much wider audience than the process environment, such as stderr, container logs, log aggregation, and crash reporting services. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to proxy credential disclosure via ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages

desc: A client certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS lets a client change the servername during TLS 1.2 renegotiation to reach endpoints it was not authorized for. On a server that applies different client-certificate policies per hostname, for example stricter admin-only client-cert auth on one host and ordinary client-cert auth on another, a client that authenticates for a permitted host can renegotiate the TLS 1.2 connection under a different servername and carry its existing authentication to the protected host, bypassing the stricter policy. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to a client certificate authentication bypass via TLS 1.2 renegotiation servername change

desc: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client corrupt server memory, over both TLS and cleartext, when the server serves files with respondWithFile() or respondWithFD(). A client can make the server free an Http2Stream while a write request that points to it is still queued on the socket; when that write completes, the code dereferences and makes a virtual call through the freed object. The only precondition is that the application serves a file with stream.respondWithFile() or stream.respondWithFD(), with default settings otherwise. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x (since 26.9.0) and 24.x (since 24.22.0).
title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 use-after-free via respondWithFile() stream reset during a pending write

desc: A NULL pointer dereference in Node.js HTTP/2 lets an unauthenticated client crash the server, over both TLS and cleartext, by cancelling file downloads. When the server serves a file with stream.respondWithFile() or stream.respondWithFD() and the client cancels the request, a StreamPipe used for the transfer is torn down in an order that leaves a NULL pointer which is then dereferenced, aborting the process. No crafted frames are needed, and a handful of cancelled requests against a default file-serving handler is enough. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 denial of service via a NULL pointer dereference when a respondWithFile() download is cancelled

desc: A certificate validation bypass in Node.js https.Agent lets a cached TLS session authenticated under one CA policy be reused by a later request with a stricter policy. https.Agent.prototype.getName() assigns the same Agent and session-cache key to a request that omits ca and one that explicitly supplies ca: [], because an omitted value appends nothing to the key while an empty array stringifies to an empty string. The two policies differ: omitting ca uses the default trust store, while supplying ca replaces it. Since they share a key, a TLS session authenticated under the broader default policy is handed to a new connection made under the later ca: [] policy, and TLS 1.3 session resumption carries the earlier authentication forward, so the second request reports authorized === true and transmits confidential data to a server its own CA policy would reject on a fresh connection. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to a certificate validation bypass in https.Agent via cross-policy TLS session reuse

desc: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can permanently leak Node.js server memory and file descriptors. If a peer triggers a protocol error, for example an oversized frame header, while the session is already shutting down, nghttp2 tears the session down internally but Node.js never notices, leaving a dangling session: the socket stays in CLOSE_WAIT and all of Node.js's HTTP/2 state for that connection is held in memory indefinitely, with no further cost to the attacker. The attacker can start the shutdown remotely by sending GOAWAY(NO_ERROR), so it is reliable against default HTTP/2 servers. It is an incomplete-fix case of CVE-2026-48937: that fix detected nghttp2 internal terminations by watching for GOAWAY sent while not shutting down, but missed terminations that arrive while the session is already shutting down. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 memory and file-descriptor leak via a protocol error during session shutdown

desc: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 stream teardown can leak response memory, including the contents of other connections' response buffers, to a peer. When a stream is torn down while a write is still backpressured, for example by a peer RST_STREAM or by the server's own per-stream timeout destroying the stream, the stream's response buffer is freed but a reference to it is still used, so freed or unrelated heap memory is written to the socket instead of the intended response. On Node.js 26.x and 24.x the teardown can be driven purely by a remote peer once the window-size change from 26.9.0 and 24.22.0 is present, and on all supported lines the same defect is reachable through an application-initiated teardown such as a per-stream idle timeout. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to HTTP/2 response memory disclosure via a use-after-free during stream teardown

desc: A per-host mutual-TLS authorization bypass in Node.js lets a client authorized for the default hostname reach a protected hostname it is not authorized for. When a TLS server assigns a hostname a different client-certificate CA with `server.addContext(host, { ca: protectedCA })` but no server certificate in that SNI context, the per-host client CA is never installed and the handshake falls back to the default client CA. In `src/crypto/crypto_tls.cc`, `CertCbDone` installs the SNI context's CA only when `setSniContext` succeeds, but `setSniContext` returns `false` for a context with no server certificate, so a CA-only SNI context silently keeps the default CA. A client holding a certificate trusted by the default CA, but not the protected CA, can therefore complete mTLS to the protected hostname and read its response even with `requestCert` and `rejectUnauthorized` enabled, while a client certified by the protected CA is rejected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to a per-host mTLS authorization bypass via a CA-only SNI context failing open to the default CA

desc: An unauthenticated HTTP/2 client can exhaust Node.js server memory because inbound DATA queued on an undrained stream is charged to no session budget. Each inbound DATA frame creates one JavaScript Buffer view in the receiving stream's readable queue, but nothing charges that queue to current_session_memory_: the socket read buffer is accounted only during parsing and released immediately, so whatever stays queued is accounted to nothing. A peer that fills a stream's receive window with one-byte DATA frames pays about 10 wire bytes per frame while the server retains about 114 bytes per frame, so a single stream on one connection can retain hundreds of megabytes from tens of megabytes sent. maxSessionMemory neither bounds the growth nor refuses new streams, because Http2Session::CanAddStream gates admission on the same counter that never sees the queue. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to an HTTP/2 memory exhaustion denial of service via unaccounted inbound DATA on an undrained stream

desc: A Permission Model bypass in Node.js recursive file watching discloses the names of files and directories the process is not permitted to read. On macOS and Windows, fs.watch() and fs.promises.watch() in recursive mode are backed by the native libuv watcher: FSEventWrap::Start checks kFileSystemRead only once, on the watched root, and FSEventWrap::OnEvent then forwards every filename libuv reports (relative paths at any depth) to the JavaScript callback without checking that each path is covered by the read grant. Code running under --permission with an exact read grant on a directory can therefore learn names such as sub/secret.txt even though readdir on that subdirectory is denied. The flaw exposes names and timing metadata, not file contents, and requires macOS or Windows plus files created under the watched directory by another actor. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to Permission Model file-name disclosure via recursive fs.watch

desc: An uncatchable exception in the Node.js zlib streaming API lets a peer crash a process by disconnecting while data is being compressed. zlib.params() queues a flush and completes its work in that write's callback; if the stream is destroyed first, as pipeline() does when the peer goes away, Writable still invokes the callback with an error, but the callback ignores its arguments and asserts that the native handle still exists. The handle is gone, so an ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION is thrown from inside stream internals and bypasses the stream's error event, the params() callback, and the pipeline() callback, terminating the process. An application is affected only if it calls deflate.params() while streaming to a peer, which is uncommon. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to a zlib denial of service via a stream destroy during a pending params() call

desc: A reachable assertion in Node.js HTTP/2 session teardown lets any unauthenticated client abort the server, over both TLS and cleartext. A client can arrange for an Http2Stream that still holds nghttp2-allocated header buffers to outlive its session: the stream is removed from the session's stream set but never detached, so when ~Http2Session() runs the memory accounting is nonzero and the CHECK_EQ(current_nghttp2_memory_, 0) assertion fails, terminating the process. The trigger needs only a default http2 server whose handler responds before the request body has ended, which is typical. It is a variant of CVE-2024-27983 that the earlier fix did not cover, because that fix only detached streams still tracked in the session. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x (since 26.9.0) and 24.x (since 24.22.0).
title: Node.js is vulnerable to a remote HTTP/2 denial of service via a reachable assertion in Http2Session teardown

desc: A re-entrancy flaw in Node.js HTTPS lets an unauthenticated client read memory belonging to other connections, including TLS private keys and other users' requests. TLSWrap::DoWrite() calls ClearOut() directly when asked to write zero bytes; if that write is issued from JavaScript running inside the HTTP parser's on_body callback, ClearOut() decrypts the next TLS record while the parser is still mid-body, re-entering llhttp_execute() and causing a use-after-free and an out-of-bounds heap read. The server then copies that freed or unrelated heap memory into the response for the request body. Triggering it requires a handler that calls res.flushHeaders() before the request body ends and later calls res.end() with a non-empty chunk, and reading the leaked memory requires any ordinary route that echoes or stores a request body. Cleartext node:http is not affected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to cross-connection memory disclosure via TLS write re-entrancy in the HTTPS request parser

desc: A flaw was found in pappl-retrofit. The application fails to properly sanitize user-supplied filenames when handling the upload and deletion of PostScript Printer Description (PPD) files. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this directory traversal flaw by submitting filenames containing path traversal sequences. This allows the attacker to upload or delete arbitrary files on the system, which can result in data corruption, denial of service, or arbitrary command execution.
title: Pappl-retrofit: directory traversal in the add-ppdfiles and delete-ppdfiles actions

desc: A one-byte heap buffer overflow in Node.js HTTP/2 Alt-Svc handling lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker corrupt process memory. When an application passes an attacker-controlled value such as a request's :authority header to Http2Session.altsvc(), the AltSvc implementation in src/node_http2.cc allocates a buffer sized to the origin length and then writes it with a null terminator, placing one byte past the end of the allocation. A single request carrying a long but syntactically valid :authority triggers the out-of-bounds write, which aborts the process and serves as a remote heap-corruption primitive. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x and 24.x.
title: Node.js is vulnerable to a heap buffer overflow in HTTP/2 session.altsvc() via a long origin

desc: CWE- 416: Use After Free vulnerability exists that could cause arbitrary code execution when a local attacker could trick the end user to open a specially crafted malicious SSD file.

A flaw was found in the xfs_admin utility in xfsprogs. The tool does not properly validate user-supplied parameters, allowing operating system command injection. A local attacker can exploit this issue by providing crafted input arguments, which may result in arbitrary command execution and local privilege escalation depending on how xfs_admin is executed.
products: red hat:red hat openshift container platform 4
red hat:red hat openshift container platform 5
title: Xfsprogs: xfsprogs: local privilege escalation via command injection in xfs_admin

desc: Dell Ansible Storage for PowerFlex, versions prior to 3.2.0, contains an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the API client component. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to information exposure and unauthorized access.

Dell Ansible Storage for PowerStore, versions prior to 3.9.0, contains an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the API client component. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to information exposure and unauthorized access.

Dell Ansible Storage for PowerStore, versions prior to 3.9.0,contains an Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the configuration module. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to information exposure.

Dell Ansible Storage for Unity , versions prior to 1.2.13 contains an Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the UnityRESTConnector component. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability,leading to information exposure and unauthorized access.

Dell Terraform for ObjectScale and Powerstore, versions prior to 1.1.1 (ObjectScale) and versions 1.2.1 through 1.3.0 (PowerStore) contains an insertion of sensitive information into Log File vulnerability in the client initialization component.  A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to information exposure and unauthorized access.

Dell Live Optics Collector, versions prior to 27.3.8.317 contains a Use of Insufficiently Random Values vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information exposure.

Dell Live Optics Collector, versions prior to 27.3.13.330 contains a Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information exposure.

Dell Terraform Provider for Dell PowerFlex contain(s) an OS Command Injection Vulnerability in the SDC host provisioning component. A high privileged remote attacker with access to the PowerFlex management plane could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to the execution of arbitrary OS commands on provisioned SDC hosts. Exploitation may lead to full compromise of affected SDC hosts.

A cross-site request forgery vulnerability in tracker-invocation.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an attacker to modify a tracker's name, description or advertiser assignment using an authenticated victim's permissions. A leftover state-changing handler accepts request parameters without verifying a CSRF token, although it is not used by the normal invocation-tag interface. Exploitation requires victim interaction and a request path that carries the victim's session credentials. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by removing the unused tracker-modification handler.

An authorization bypass in channel-edit.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager to create a delivery rule set belonging to another agency by changing the submitted agencyid parameter. The server trusts the submitted agency identifier when inserting the new rule set, allowing unauthorized creation of objects in another agency's account. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by obtaining the agency identifier from the authenticated account rather than submitted form data and removing the agency identifier from the form's hidden fields.

An authorization bypass in website-index.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to view another agency's website listing by changing the agencyid request parameter. Disclosed information includes website names, identifiers and timestamps. Detailed website pages continue to enforce ownership checks. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by obtaining the agency identifier from the authenticated account rather than the request.

An authorization bypass in campaign-zone linking in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager, or a trafficker with zone-linking permissions, to associate another agency's campaign with their own zone. Campaign ownership checks are missing from the bulk-linking and single-link operations in zone-include.php and the XML-RPC campaign-linking method. Although agency filtering prevents foreign banners from being linked, the unauthorized association can expose the foreign campaign's name, type and identifier in the linked-campaign listing. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by validating campaign ownership in the affected operations.

The OWASP core rule set (CRS) is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with compatible web application firewalls. Prior to versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0, regular-expression denial of service (ReDoS) affects a shared regex-assembly include used to build 12 Unix RCE detection rules in CRS v4, and the same ambiguous pattern was present in the manually-assembled regexes in 4 rules in CRS v3.3. With a single, unauthenticated, crafted request, the generated pattern drives PCRE2 past its backtracking limit. When PCRE2 exceeds that limit, the @rx operator returns an error rather than a match result, which results in detection bypass and CPU denial of service. This issue has been patched in versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0.
title: OWASP CRS: ReDoS in shared unix-shell-evasion regex-assembly include (12 RCE rules) - PCRE2 backtracking-limit exhaustion causes detection bypass and CPU DoS

desc: The OWASP core rule set (CRS) is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with compatible web application firewalls. Prior to versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0, CRS rules in the 921 (protocol-attack), 930 (LFI), 931 (RFI), 932 (RCE), 933 (PHP), 934 (generic), 941 (XSS), 942 (SQLi), and 943 (session-fixation) families inspect XML request bodies via the XPath expression XML:/*. That expression matches only element text nodes — it does not match XML attribute values. As a result, an attacker who places an attack payload inside an XML attribute (e.g. or ) bypasses CRS detection entirely. This is verified empirically against a local CRS test instance and against the public CRS sandbox. The bypass affects approximately 159 rules across 9 rule files and applies at every paranoia level (PL1 through PL4), since the variable list is more or less shared across PLs. The 944 (Java) family is the only one that correctly includes XML://@* in addition to XML:/* and is therefore unaffected. This issue has been patched in versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0.
title: OWASP CRS: XML Attribute Value Bypass

desc: aeon is a scikit-learn compatible Python library for learning from time series. Prior to version 1.5.0, a GitHub Actions workflow used pull_request_target for pre-commit checks on pull requests from forks. In this configuration, fork-controlled code could be checked out and executed in a privileged context. The vulnerable workflow also generated/used elevated credentials and could automatically commit or push fixes back to pull request branches. This created a potential token exposure and repository write path if an attacker submitted a malicious fork pull request designed to execute during the privileged workflow run. This issue has been patched in version 1.5.0.
title: aeon: Privileged GitHub Actions workflow allowed fork-controlled code execution

desc: vulnerability-operator scans SBOMs and Images for vulnerabilities. Prior to version 0.28.16, an unauthenticated information-disclosure vulnerability exposes all vulnerability scan reports served by the operator. The /report/ HTTP endpoint mounts a raw http.FileServer over the reports directory (default /reports) with no authentication, authorization, or middleware. Any client that can reach the operator's HTTP port (default 8080) can list and download every JSON vulnerability report, disclosing CVE IDs, affected package names/versions, and container image identifiers for every workload scanned in the cluster. This issue has been patched in version 0.28.16.
title: vulnerability-operator: IDOR exposing vulnerability reports via unauthenticated Report Handler

desc: Janus WebRTC Server 1.2.3 through 1.4.0 is vulnerable to Directory Traversal. The application accepts a caller supplied media path when an ondemand stream is created. The path is validated only by checking whether it contains one of the audio extensions and is then passed to the file source which opens it. No canonicalization is performed and no directory allowlist is enforced, so an unauthenticated caller can make the server open an arbitrary local file and use it as a media source, with the content delivered to viewers as RTP audio.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the invocation-tag generation interface of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. When Direct Selection is enabled, an attacker-controlled banner identifier can be included in HTML form fields without appropriate encoding. Direct Selection is disabled by default. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding banner identifier values in the invocation-option form fields.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the popup invocation options of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. The top, left, timeout and delay request parameters are included in HTML attributes without appropriate encoding. Exploitation requires an existing popup zone, which can be created through the administrator API but is not offered by the normal zone-creation interface. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding the affected popup option values.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the conversion-statistics pages of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. An incorrect ownership check validates the advertiser identifier instead of the supplied website identifier, allowing malicious website input to reach HTML output without appropriate encoding. A related output issue affects the hour parameter. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by validating the correct website identifier and normalising the hour parameter before formatting.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the iframe invocation options of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in an authenticated user's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. When generating invocation tags for an any-size zone, the frame_width and frame_height request parameters are included in HTML attributes without appropriate encoding. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding the affected values in the invocation-option form fields.

A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in updates-history.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in a victim's browser by persuading them to visit a crafted URL. Attacker-controlled values are included in XML command attributes without appropriate encoding, allowing injection of executable XHTML into the response. The preliminary session check omits GET xajax requests, exposing an unauthenticated attack path, while authenticated administrator requests also reach the unsafe output. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by applying the session check to both GET and POST requests and encoding XML command attribute values in both response serializers.

A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the report date-selection controls of Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute JavaScript in a victim's browser by persuading them to follow a crafted report URL and complete normal reauthentication. An attacker-controlled period_preset value can be saved in the victim's session and inserted into JavaScript without appropriate encoding. The payload can execute on the initial report view and subsequent report views using the stored defaults. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by applying JSON encoding appropriate for the JavaScript context to date-selection values.

A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in maintenance-appendcode-check.php in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager to execute JavaScript in an administrator's browser. A manager can store a malicious tracker name and cause the tracker to appear in the append-code maintenance results. When an administrator opens the affected maintenance page, the tracker name is included in HTML without appropriate encoding. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by HTML-encoding tracker names when displaying the maintenance results.

Spreadsheet formula injection in conversion-tracking report exports in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an unauthenticated attacker to submit conversion values that are written as formulas instead of text in an XLS workbook. When a user opens the exported report in a spreadsheet application, attacker-supplied formulas can be evaluated. The confirmed impact is formula execution within the workbook; disclosure of information to the attacker has not been established. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by sanitising conversion values before writing them to the affected XLS report sections.

In Progress® Telerik® Report Server prior to version 12.3.26.1110, an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Web Report Designer allows an authenticated attacker with low privileges to perform unauthorized operations on shared report resources, affecting their integrity and availability.
title: Incorrect Authorization in Telerik Report Server Web Report Designer

desc: In affected versions of Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET MVC `2012.2.710` through `2026.3.811`, ClassFactory updates a shared class dictionary without exclusive write protection and emits non-collectible dynamic assemblies that remain loaded for the AppDomain's lifetime. The dictionary lookup and insertion are not atomic, and case variations in aggregate descriptors can produce distinct retained types even though member resolution is case-insensitive. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an aggregation endpoint that is reachable without authentication, by submitting concurrent or repeated crafted requests. These requests may corrupt dictionary state or increase CPU and memory use, potentially degrading availability. The issue is fixed in version `2026.3.1015`.
products: progress software:telerik ui for asp.net mvc
title: ClassFactory Race Condition and Retained Assembly Memory in Telerik UI for ASP.NET MVC

desc: In Progress® Telerik® Report Server prior to version 12.3.26.1110, an external control of a system configuration setting vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to influence the server address used by Report Server when generating links and notifications. With user interaction, this can lead to disclosure of sensitive information and account takeover.
title: External Control of Configuration Setting in Telerik Report Server

desc: In Progress® Telerik® UI for ASP.NET Core versions `2015.1.318` through `2026.3.811`, repeated server-side aggregation requests, with or without grouping, cause dynamic assemblies and load contexts to be retained, resulting in accumulating process memory consumption. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this if the application exposes an aggregation endpoint that is reachable without authentication. Repeated requests can cause memory growth that may exhaust available resources and affect application availability. Disabling grouping in the client-side interface does not prevent direct requests containing these descriptors. The issue is fixed in version `2026.3.1015`.
products: progress software:telerik ui for asp.net core
title: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption in Telerik UI for ASP.NET Core Server-side Aggregation

desc: An authorization bypass in Revive Adserver 6.0.0 through 6.0.8 allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to access or modify resources belonging to another agency. Global input registration gives GET parameters precedence over POST parameters, while submitted administration forms use POST values. By supplying authorized object identifiers in the query string and different identifiers in the POST body, an attacker can cause permission checks and subsequent operations to target different objects. This permits unauthorized cross-agency changes, campaign ownership reassignment and disclosure of campaign and banner data. The regression was introduced in commit 156dee7bc3283c128f35e5a31bb305054cc8de1b and is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by restoring POST precedence in global input registration.

Blind SQL injection in Revive Adserver 6.0.8 and earlier allows an authenticated manager restricted to one agency to extract arbitrary database values through the banner-zone.php and campaign-zone.php administration pages. Permission checks and database queries obtain identifiers through inconsistent request-input precedence, allowing an authorized numeric identifier to pass validation while a different, attacker-controlled value reaches an SQL query. Extracted data can include password hashes and active session identifiers. Reusing an unexpired administrator session can grant administrative access, allowing modification of configuration and disruption of ad delivery. The issue is fixed in Revive Adserver 6.0.9 by consistently selecting POST values before GET values in both global input registration and common input helpers, and excluding cookies from these helpers. Both commits e301dbbb7 and 0aa9d0124 are required for the complete correction.

desc: When parsing request variables such as query-string and form parameters, HHVM did not check that appending a nested array succeeded before descending into it. A remote, unauthenticated attacker could send a GET or POST request which would crash the HHVM server process before any application code runs, leading to denial of service. This issue affected HHVM prior to 23c061f4e804a51badd5f85227e65185651253b5.

repmgr 4.0.0 through 5.5.0 is affected by an OS command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) in event notifications. When event_notification_command is configured, repmgr substitutes the %a (node name), %c (connection string) and %d (details) placeholders into the command and runs it through the shell. %a and %c are inserted without escaping, and %d escapes only double quotes, so shell command substitution still works inside the quoting the documentation recommends. The node name and connection string come from node records in the repmgr.nodes table. An attacker with the credentials of a non-superuser repmgr database user can write a crafted node record and run OS commands, as the operating system user that runs repmgr or repmgrd (usually postgres), on other cluster nodes that process an event using these placeholders. The %a placeholder of failover_validation_command has the same flaw. Deployments whose repmgr database user is a superuser gain no new capability, because a superuser can already run OS commands, and deployments that do not use these placeholders are not affected. The issue is fixed in repmgr 5.5.1. After upgrading, operators must remove any quotes they placed around these placeholders, because a placeholder left inside double quotes is still open to command injection.

proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a frame of an unknown or reserved type, or a HEADERS frame, until its entire declared length had arrived, without limiting that length, and re-scanned all buffered data each time more bytes arrived. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could declare a very large frame and deliver it slowly, causing unbounded memory growth and CPU usage that grows quadratically with the number of fragments, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instruction only after the entire literal had been received. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send an insert instruction on the QPACK encoder stream that declares an arbitrarily large literal and then keep sending data, causing the decoder to buffer it without bound for the lifetime of the connection and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service. The issue occurs regardless of the advertised QPACK dynamic table capacity, including when the dynamic table is disabled. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

In proxygen's HTTP/3 session, when a HEADERS block referenced QPACK dynamic table entries that had not yet been received, header decoding for that stream was paused, but the session continued to read the stream from the QUIC transport. The unread data bypassed the session's ingress buffer limit, returned flow-control credit to the peer, and was re-scanned in full on every read. With QPACK blocked streams enabled (the default), a remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send a HEADERS block that references a dynamic table insert it never sends, followed by a continuous stream of data, causing memory growth until the request timed out and CPU usage that grows quadratically, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

mvfst did not adequately merge or compact out-of-order STREAM frame data, and a small received fragment could keep a much larger receive buffer alive. QUIC flow control limits the number of buffered stream bytes, but not this per-fragment memory and bookkeeping. A remote, unauthenticated QUIC peer could send many small, non-contiguous stream fragments to make an endpoint consume memory far in excess of its advertised receive window and spend increasing CPU time reassembling stream data, leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.0.

An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or Handshake) that the TLS handshake had already moved past. Because the transport treated this data as delivered, it did not count against the CRYPTO stream buffer limit. A remote, unauthenticated client could complete a handshake, withhold its acknowledgment of the server's HANDSHAKE_DONE frame so that Handshake keys stay in use, and keep sending Handshake-level CRYPTO data at increasing offsets, causing unbounded memory growth on the server and leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

desc: soapbar is a SOAP library for Python — client, server, and WSDL handling. Prior to version 0.13.0, verify_envelope_bsp() derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted wsse:BinarySecurityToken, validated only that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful verify_envelope_bsp() therefore proved only that the envelope was signed by whoever supplied the embedded certificate — never that it was signed by a trusted party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs a forged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification. Any consumer that treats a successful BSP verification as authentication can be impersonated (signature forgery / authentication bypass). verify_envelope() (which pins a caller-supplied x509_cert) was not affected — the flaw was specific to the BSP variant whose trust anchor came from the message. This issue has been patched in version 0.13.0.
title: soapbar: verify_envelope_bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)

desc:
The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed, and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is freed again on the error path.

An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation, though, so the issue can only be reached when the system is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who supplies the pattern or the subject string has little control over which allocation fails, so the expected impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.
title: Double free after allocation failure in regcomp and regexec

desc:
Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra null byte one past the end of the destination array when the converted multibyte string and its terminating null byte exactly fill that array.

These conversions store each wide input character into the caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the initial shift state, which also stores the terminating null byte, and the functions then append a second null byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a string whose converted length exactly fills the destination.

The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.
title: One-byte buffer overflow in wide scanf %s and %[ conversions

desc: The Ninja Forms - File Uploads add-on for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion (and arbitrary file read via S3/Dropbox/Google Drive exfiltration) in versions up to, and including, 3.3.36. The flaw spans NF_FU_Fields_Upload::process() in includes/fields/upload.php — which returns early (leaving the client-supplied files[] intact) whenever a public submission carries a nonempty extra.saveProgress — and NF_FU_External_Abstracts_Service::process_upload() in includes/external/abstracts/service.php, whose authoritative-path reload only fires when the client sends upload_id. By omitting upload_id, an attacker's data[file_path] survives into the Background Upload queue and is used by both upload_file_to_s3() (as SourceFile) and the maybe_delete_server_file() unlink() call in includes/external/abstracts/backgroundupload.php, with no canonicalization or upload-directory containment check (the plugin's own is_path_within_upload_dir() helper is only applied on admin paths). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server which may make remote code execution possible — specifically, deleting wp-config.php forces WordPress into its setup screen, enabling full site takeover.
title: Ninja Forms - File Uploads <= 3.3.36 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'files[].data.file_path' Parameter via 'extra.saveProgress'

desc:
Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in the sketch deserialization of Apache DataSketches Java.



Several deserializers trusted sizes and counts declared in the serialized input. A small crafted input could make an application allocate an excessive amount of memory, leading to an OutOfMemoryError. A crafted string passed to FrequentLongsSketch.getInstance(String) could also make deserialization, or a later update, loop indefinitely. Only applications that deserialize sketches from untrusted sources are affected.



This issue affects Apache DataSketches Java: through 9.0.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.1.0, which fixes the issue.
title: Apache DataSketches Java: Uncontrolled resource consumption when deserializing crafted sketch images

desc:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog member with the Limited role to remove or change entries that member may only read, including entries published by other members. The entry editor checked the member's weblog role but not whether that role permits work on the entry.
Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later.
title: Apache Roller: Limited weblog members can remove or change published entries

desc: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Roller. When Roller sends a weblog update ping, its XML-RPC client deserializes Java object data contained in the ping target's response, so a party that controls that response can run code in the Roller server process. This issue affects Apache Roller from 4.0 through 6.1.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.1.7, which removes the unsafe deserialization.
title: Apache Roller: Deserialization of untrusted data in weblog update ping responses

desc: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated visitor to recover the email addresses of people who left approved comments. The search index stored commenter email addresses, and the public weblog search accepted queries on that field, including wildcard queries that confirm an address one character at a time. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later and rebuild the search index.
title: Apache Roller: Commenter email addresses recoverable through public search

desc: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated visitor to read an entry after its author has withdrawn it to draft through the AtomPub API. The entry was removed from the weblog but stayed in the search index, and public search showed its content. AtomPub is disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which shows only published entries in search results.
title: Apache Roller: Unpublished entries remain readable through search after AtomPub unpublish

desc: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in Apache Roller 5.0.1 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated attacker to create an administrator account if a logged-in Roller administrator opens a link that the attacker controls. The request-token check applied only to POST requests, and administrative actions also accepted GET requests. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which requires POST and a valid token for actions that change data.
title: Apache Roller: Cross-site request forgery through GET requests to administrative actions

desc: Improper Authentication in Apache Roller 5.1.0 through 6.1.6 allows a user whose account an administrator has disabled to sign in again through OpenID and read unpublished entries. The OpenID sign-in path did not check whether the account was enabled. Only sites that enable the non-default OpenID authentication mode are affected; later major versions do not include OpenID 2.0. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later.
title: Apache Roller: Disabled accounts can sign in through OpenID

desc: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog administrator to store script that runs in the browsers of the weblog's visitors. Blogroll links imported from an OPML file were not checked, and the default theme printed them without escaping. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which accepts only web links on import and escapes them on output.
title: Apache Roller: Stored cross-site scripting through imported blogroll links

desc: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 6.1.2 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog administrator to store script that runs in the browsers of the weblog's members when they open their main menu. The HTML-stripping routine kept a tag that was not closed, and the main menu printed the weblog description without escaping. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later.
title: Apache Roller: Stored cross-site scripting through the weblog description

desc: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows any logged-in user to learn other users' email addresses. The user search in the authoring interface shows only user names, but it also matched the search text against email addresses, so a user could confirm an address one character at a time. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which matches only user names for users who are not administrators.
title: Apache Roller: Exposure of other users' email addresses through the user search

desc: Missing Authorization in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows any logged-in user to read unpublished entries of a weblog they have no role in. The entry preview checked that the user was logged in, but not that the user had a role in the weblog being previewed. The attacker must know the weblog name and the entry's link name. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which requires a role in the weblog to preview its entries.
title: Apache Roller: Unpublished entries of other weblogs readable through preview

desc: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in the Planet feed aggregator administration of Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated attacker to make the Roller server fetch a URL the attacker chooses, including internal addresses, by inducing a logged-in global administrator to open a crafted web page. The action that adds a Planet subscription can be triggered cross-site; in recent releases it accepts GET requests, which Roller's CSRF token check does not cover. The action fetches the supplied URL and saves the subscription, and any fetched content that parses as a feed is then published without authentication in the aggregated Planet feed. The Planet aggregator is enabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which requires POST requests with a valid CSRF token for Planet administration changes and turns the Planet aggregator off by default.
title: Apache Roller: Cross-site request forgery in Planet administration lets an attacker make the server fetch arbitrary URLs

desc: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 5.0.1 through 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with the Author role on a weblog to store script in entry tags submitted through AtomPub. Roller's tag filter allowed HTML characters in tag names, and the bundled gaurav, fauxcoly and frontpage themes and the showEntryTags macro print tag names without escaping, so the script runs in the browser of anyone who views the weblog. This matters when weblog authors are not trusted with script (weblogAdminsUntrusted=true, the default since 6.1.4). AtomPub is disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which removes HTML characters from tag names, including names stored earlier.
title: Apache Roller: Stored cross-site scripting through AtomPub entry tags

desc: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with the Author role on a weblog that uses a custom theme to store script that runs in the browser of anyone who opens the file's resource URL. The fix for CVE-2026-82387 serves uploaded media as a download unless it is an image, audio, video, PDF or plain text, but media files found through a custom theme were served with the type their path implies, and the upload form let the uploader choose that path. Media uploads are disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which serves these files under the same rules as other media and no longer accepts the path from the upload form.
title: Apache Roller: Stored cross-site scripting through custom-theme resource URLs

desc: A flaw was found in the login-failure storage component of Keycloak, the identity and access management solution. This issue specifically affects deployments using MySQL or MariaDB databases in a multi-node configuration. When multiple failed login attempts occur simultaneously for the same account, a synchronization error can cause the system to enter a repetitive loop that locks the user's record in the database. This results in legitimate login attempts for that user being blocked and failing with an error. Furthermore, because some failures are not correctly recorded during this loop, the system's brute-force protection may not accurately count all failed attempts.
products: red hat:red hat build of keycloak
title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: login-failure upsert trusts mysql/mariadb affected-row count

desc: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog administrator to read another user's stored password hash by authoring a custom weblog template that reaches the wrapped persistent object behind the template's weblog or entry data, rather than the reduced set of fields the wrapper is meant to expose. Roller treats weblog administrators as untrusted and exposes weblog and entry data to templates only through wrapper classes, but a public accessor on those wrapper classes returned the underlying persistent object directly, including the stored password hash of the weblog's creator and of any author whose entry renders on the page. No non-default configuration is required; this affects any weblog whose administrator can author templates. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which removes template access to the underlying wrapped objects.
title: Apache Roller: Weblog template access to wrapped objects exposes another user's password hash

desc: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with no weblog permissions to read files readable by the Roller process and cause the server to issue outbound HTTP requests to attacker-chosen destinations, by submitting a crafted Atom entry to the AtomPub endpoint. The entry body is parsed with a parser configuration that permits external parameter entities and external DTD subsets, and the parse happens before any per-weblog authorization check and before any check of whether the AtomPub feature is enabled, so the endpoint is reachable by any authenticated account on a default installation. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which parses AtomPub entries with a hardened XML configuration and rejects AtomPub requests while the feature is disabled.
title: Apache Roller: XML external entity processing in AtomPub entry parsing

desc: A flaw was found in BusyBox. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to authenticate as any existing WordPress user — including any administrator whose email address is known or guessable — resulting in full site compromise. This issue represents an incomplete fix for a prior vulnerability: the 2.29.0 remediation moved the target email out of POST data into a server-side transient, but because any Subscriber can still overwrite the outbound API URL that populates that transient, the full authentication bypass chain remains exploitable in three AJAX requests.
