desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From version 0.30.0 until 0.32.0, the compose-lint GitHub Action prints the resolved directory from a failed sarif-file subdirectory creation without effective command suppression. Version 0.30.0 has no stop-commands window, while version 0.31.0 prints this error outside its stop-commands window. A pull request can place a committed symlink on that path to a directory whose name contains a newline followed by a workflow command, causing the SARIF-directory error to issue commands in the job log. Only the Action with sarif-file pointing into a subdirectory is affected; a workspace-root SARIF file, the compose-lint package, the pre-commit hook, and the Docker image do not expose this message. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.
title: compose-lint: A symlink in a pull request can issue workflow commands through the compose-lint Action's SARIF-directory error message

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint escapes GitHub Actions workflow-command openers only after ASCII spaces and tabs, while the runner strips all leading Unicode whitespace before interpreting a line. Untrusted Compose values or repository paths beginning with Unicode whitespace followed by :: can therefore reach the text report, fix guidance, the fix dry-run diff, and stderr diagnostics as workflow commands when the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image runs directly in CI. The GitHub Action is not affected because it disables command processing, and the flaw does not change the lint pass or fail result. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.
title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can still issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's output

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint's argument parser writes rejected repository paths to stderr without the output sanitizer when a path is passed without a preceding -- separator. A pull request can supply a path containing workflow-command syntax; a carriage return can position that command at the start of a new line recognized by the GitHub Actions runner, allowing the package, Docker image, or a pre-commit hook with misconfigured args to issue the command in the job log. The default pre-commit configuration includes -- and is not affected, the GitHub Action is not affected, and the lint pass or fail result is unchanged. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.
title: compose-lint: A file path in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's command-line error messages

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint does not sanitize the ##[ workflow-command opener inside strings written by --format json or --format sarif to stdout. A pull request can place that opener in a service name or other Compose value, and the GitHub Actions runner recognizes it even in the middle of a serialized line when the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image prints JSON or SARIF to the job log. Writing the output to a file and using the compose-lint GitHub Action are not affected, and the flaw does not change the lint pass or fail result. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.
title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's JSON and SARIF output on stdout

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. In version 0.31.0, compose-lint does not neutralize the Azure Pipelines ##vso[ logging-command opener on any output path. A pull request can place that opener in a Compose value or file name, allowing output from the package, pre-commit hook, or Docker image to issue logging commands when printed to an Azure Pipelines job log. The maintainer did not reproduce the behavior on an Azure Pipelines agent. The GitHub Action is not affected because it runs only on GitHub Actions, and releases before 0.31.0 are outside this advisory because they did not claim Azure Pipelines coverage. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.
title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can reach Azure Pipelines as logging commands through compose-lint 0.31.0's output

desc: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in XplodedThemes WPIDE – File Manager & Code Editor wpide allows Cross Site Request Forgery.This issue affects WPIDE – File Manager & Code Editor: from n/a through 3.6.4.
title: WordPress WPIDE – File Manager & Code Editor plugin <= 3.6.4 - Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability

desc: An insufficient input validation vulnerability in the listed NETGEAR Orbi Models router allows an authenticated administrator connected to the local network to execute unauthorized commands and modify the router’s software and functionality, potentially compromising the integrity of the affected device.
title: Insufficient Input Validation Vulnerability in NETGEAR Orbi RBR350

desc: A missing authentication vulnerability in the listed NETGEAR RAX models allows an network adjacent attacker who has authenticated to wifi network to obtain sensitive information and tamper with device configuration, including administrator credentials, without authenticating to the device. This affects the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the router.
title: Missing Authentication Vulnerability in NETGEAR Nighthawk RAX30 models

desc:
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to

decompress an archive, a Python script shadowing the stdlib can be

created. Then if an error occurs during decompressing the next file,

the newly created Python script is executed. This is especially true

if the created Python is called traceback.py. The problem is that

Python adds the current directory to sys.path when python -m MODULE is

run, and the archive is also decompressed in the current directory.



The fix removes sys.path[0] in gzip, tarfile and zipfile command line

interface to prevent shadowing standard library modules from extracted

files.
title: Prevent shadowing stdlib in gzip/tarfile/zipfile CLI during extraction

desc:
In Kura versions <= 5.6.2, the "Command" file-upload handler at `POST /admin/denali/file/command` extracts a client-supplied ZIP archive into the configured `command.working.directory`. The path-containment check `validateFileName()` compares canonical paths with `String.startsWith()` without appending a trailing path separator, so an entry that canonicalises to a sibling directory sharing the same string prefix (e.g. `/tmpevil/x` when the intended directory is `/tmp`) is accepted. The handler then calls `parent.mkdirs()` and `new FileOutputStream(newFile)`, creating directories and writing attacker-controlled bytes outside the intended extraction root.



The command service is disabled by default since Kura 4.0.0 [1]. The issue does not apply when the command service is disabled. The caller must be authenticated with `rest.command` permission.

In Eclipse Kura versions 5.1.0 through 5.6.2, the Configuration REST API v2 (org.eclipse.kura.rest.configuration.provider) does not restrict access to the configuration of the UserAdmin persistence component to identities holding the kura.admin permission. An authenticated identity holding only the rest.configuration permission can read the password hashes of all identities, including administrators, which are stored as unsalted SHA-256 digests. The same identity can also modify identities and permission assignments, and restore previous configuration snapshots, which allows escalation to full administrative privileges. The issue is fixed in Eclipse Kura 5.6.3.

In Eclipse Kura versions 5.4.0 through 5.6.2, the Service Listing V1 REST API read the JSON body of every request into memory, with no limit on its size. The endpoints parse the body before they check whether the caller is authenticated. A remote attacker without valid credentials can therefore send a few dozen large JSON requests at the same time, exhaust the Java heap with an `OutOfMemoryError`, and cause a denial of service. Likewise, a remote attacker, can send a deeply nested JSON request and trigger a `StackOverflowError` because of an unbound recursion in Service Listing V1.
An exposed dangerous function in Ivanti EPMM before version 12.11.0.0, 12.10.0.1, and 12.9.0.3 allows a local authenticated attacker to trigger a denial of service.

Joomla Extension - j2commerce.com - Gift voucher and single-use coupon could pay for more than one order in J2Store 6.0.0 - 6.6.5 - A logged-in customer could redeem a single gift voucher, or a single-use coupon (`max_uses` / `max_customer_uses` = 1), on more than one order. By starting several checkout sessions and carrying each to the confirm step before submitting any of them, every order independently saw the voucher's full balance or the coupon's unused slot, because the balance/usage calculations and the final placement check both only looked at orders that had already left the "New" state.
title: Joomla Extension - j2commerce.com - Gift voucher and single-use coupon could pay for more than one order in J2Store 6.0.0 - 6.6.5

desc: The embedded HTTP server does not clear the security identity established during a request before its worker thread handles the next request. A remote unauthenticated attacker can have their request processed with the identity of a previously authenticated user, gaining that user's privileges. Only applications served by the embedded HTTP server that authenticate programmatically or via basic authentication are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: Caller identity leaks across requests in embedded HTTP server

desc: The embedded HTTP server does not invalidate the previous session identifier when an application changes the session id, e.g. after login. An attacker who can plant a session identifier in a victim's browser can hijack the victim's authenticated session. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: Session fixation in embedded HTTP server

desc: When Hessian remoting endpoints are served by the embedded HTTP server, configured authentication and transport security requirements are silently ignored. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods without credentials or over an unencrypted connection. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server rather than Tomcat and rely on these settings are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.
title: Apache TomEE: Missing authentication for Hessian endpoints in embedded HTTP server

desc: When an EJB is exposed over the optional Hessian protocol inside an existing web application, some configured authentication and transport security settings are silently not enforced. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods. Only deployments using the Hessian module with such settings are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication bypass of Hessian EJB endpoints due to ignored security settings

desc: When Hessian remoting is configured with BASIC authentication, the authentication check is not applied to Hessian endpoints of applications deployed under a non-root context path. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed EJB methods without credentials. Users are recommended to block network access to Hessian endpoints from untrusted clients, or to migrate to another remoting protocol.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication bypass for Hessian endpoints in non-root web applications

desc: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server dispatches some requests to REST endpoints configured for HTTP Basic authentication without verifying credentials. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke protected resources, bypassing authentication. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server with Basic authentication are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication bypass in the embedded HTTP server for endpoints protected by HTTP Basic authentication

desc: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not restrict static resource paths to the configured resource directories. A remote unauthenticated attacker can read arbitrary files accessible to the server process. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: Path traversal in embedded HTTP server static resource handling

desc: In Eclipse Kura versions 3.1.0 to 5.6.2, the iBeacon and Eddystone advertisement decoders wrongly parse the AD-structure length field of an over-the-air BLE advertising payload. Any unauthenticated attacker within BLE radio range can broadcast a two-byte advertising payload that drives the Kura beacon-scanner thread into a tight infinite loop, pinning a CPU core and permanently halting beacon ingestion until the gateway is restarted. To trigger the attack, the iBeacon/Eddystone scanner component should be installed and active. By default the components are not installed or enabled.

The embedded Derby network service ignores its configured bind address and listens on all network interfaces. When the service is enabled, a remote attacker with network access can connect to the database server and read or modify data. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Derby network service listens on all interfaces

desc: The EJBd remote protocol returns datasource connection details, including database credentials, to remote clients that look up a datasource. A remote client able to reach the EJBd endpoint can obtain the database credentials and connect to the database directly. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Database credential disclosure via remote JNDI lookup

desc: Cleartext transmission of sensitive information in the Agent of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before version 2024 SU8 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to in a MITM position to read and modify HTTP traffic.

Apache TomEE running on JDK 21 or later skips EJB method authorization checks, allowing callers to invoke EJB methods without the configured access restrictions being enforced. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: EJB method authorization is silently skipped on JDK 21+

desc: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not limit the size of incoming request bodies or of multipart requests, and does not remove the temporary files it creates for multipart parts. A remote unauthenticated attacker can cause excessive memory or disk usage, leading to denial of service. Deployments using the Tomcat connectors are not affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: DoS via unbounded request body and multipart handling in embedded HTTP server

desc: The remote EJB client does not verify that the hostname of the server it connects to matches the server's TLS certificate. An attacker able to intercept network traffic between an EJB client and server can impersonate the server and read or modify the traffic, including credentials and invocation data. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Missing TLS hostname verification in ejbds client connections

desc: mailcow: dockerized before 2026-11 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows domain administrators to execute commands in the shared rspamd container by storing a malicious domain-wide footer. Attackers can embed a Jinja macro with an os.execute default value, rendered by the rspamd MOO_FOOTER prefilter, to read or inject mail for every tenant and disable filtering.
title: mailcow: dockerized before 2026-11 Template Injection RCE via Domain-Wide Footer

desc: Nango before 0.71.3 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary SQL by supplying a crafted task group key to the orchestrator API. Attackers can send a malicious group.key to POST /v1/immediate, which TaskEventsHandler.notify() interpolates into a Postgres NOTIFY statement, running stacked queries against the scheduler database.
title: Nango before 0.71.3 SQL Injection via Orchestrator Task Group Key

desc: Aptabase before commit 61d4c01 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge sign-in links by using the publicly known example AUTH_SECRET. Attackers can enumerate registered e-mails via /api/_auth/signin, forge HS256 JWTs redeemed by /api/_auth/continue, impersonate users, export analytics data, and transfer app ownership.
title: Aptabase before commit 61d4c01 Authentication Bypass via Known Example AUTH_SECRET

desc: ABP Framework 2.9.0 before 10.6.2 and 10.7.0 pre-releases before 10.7.0 contain a path traversal vulnerability in DefaultBlobFilePathCalculator that allows unauthenticated attackers to access files outside the blob container. Attackers can send %5C-encoded backslashes through the Blogging api/blogging/files/{name} endpoint on Windows hosts to read files like appsettings.json containing signing keys and connection strings.
title: ABP Framework before 10.6.2 and 10.7.0 Path Traversal via Blogging File Endpoints

desc: postal-mime before 4.2.1 contains a parser differential vulnerability in its address parser that truncates the domain at folding whitespace or comments preceding a dot. Remote attackers can craft From headers that pass SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment for their own subdomain while PostalMime.parse() reports a spoofed victim sender address.
title: postal-mime before 4.2.1 Sender Spoofing via Address Parser Domain Truncation

desc: Nodemailer 3.0.0 before 10.4.1 contains an address parsing flaw in addressparser that truncates domains at folding whitespace or comments before a dot, allowing attackers to bypass recipient domain restrictions. Attackers can submit crafted to, cc, bcc or replyTo addresses that pass RFC 5322 domain checks but deliver mail to an attacker-chosen address under the application's sender identity.
title: Nodemailer 3.0.0 before 10.4.1 Recipient Allow-List Bypass via addressparser

desc: Dolibarr 20.0.0 through 23.0.4 and 24.x before 24.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in api_expensereports.class.php payment endpoints that lets authenticated users access other users' expense report payments. Attackers with only expense report read and create rights can call getAllPayments, getPayments, addPayment, or updatePayment to read, create, or modify payments, falsifying reimbursement state.
title: Dolibarr 20.0.0 through 23.0.4 and 24.x before 24.0.2 IDOR via ExpenseReport Payment API

desc: Meteroid before 2.2.0 contains a cross-tenant authorization bypass vulnerability in the CouponsService UpdateCouponStatus gRPC handler, whose UPDATE query filters only on coupon id and ignores tenant ID. Authenticated users with catalog:manage or a tenant-scoped API key can supply another tenant's coupon ID to disable, archive, or re-enable that coupon and receive its details.
title: Meteroid before 2.2.0 Cross-Tenant Authorization Bypass via UpdateCouponStatus

desc: Meteroid before 2.2.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the ApiTokensService GetApiTokenById gRPC handler that fails to apply the caller's tenant context. Authenticated users with settings:read permission can supply another tenant's API token ID to obtain its Argon2 secret hash and owning tenant ID.
title: Meteroid before 2.2.0 Cross-Tenant API Token Hash Disclosure via GetApiTokenById

desc: Firekylin through 2.18.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows editor-role users to read administrator-only secrets because the admin API base guard permits all GET actions. Editors can query options.js for TOTP secrets, push credentials, and cloud storage keys, or user.js for other users' app_key/app_secret to publish posts as administrators via admin/post_push.
title: Firekylin through 2.18.1 Improper Authorization via Admin REST API GET Actions

desc: Parabol before 15.21.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addReactjiToReactable GraphQL mutation that allows authenticated users to tamper with reactions on other organizations' content. Attackers can pair their own meetingId with a reactableId of another tenant's reflection, comment, or sequential team prompt response to add or remove their reactions.
title: Parabol before 15.21.2 Missing Authorization via addReactjiToReactable Mutation

desc: TaxHacker through 0.8.5 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in app/(app)/settings/actions.ts that allows authenticated users to modify other users' data by supplying an arbitrary userId. Attackers can invoke Server Actions like deleteCategoryAction or editFieldAction with a victim's UUID to delete categories, clear transaction assignments, or alter LLM prompts.
title: TaxHacker through 0.8.5 IDOR via Settings Server Actions userId

desc: ZenTao PMS through 22.7 contains a missing object-level authorization vulnerability in module/build/control.php that allows authenticated users to modify builds in projects they do not belong to. Attackers holding build privileges in any project can supply sequential buildID values to delete, edit, or relink stories and bugs on builds in foreign or private projects.
title: ZenTao PMS through 22.7 IDOR via Build Module Mutation Methods

desc: An insecure default initialization of resource in the Tomcat shutdown listener of Ivanti Sentry before versions 11.0, 10.8.3, and 10.7.4 allows a local authenticated attacker to cause a denial of service.

Missing authorization checks in the visual alert feature of FlockOS, Flock's hosted public safety platform, prior to 2026-09-28, allowed an authenticated user with permission to manage saved searches in their own organization to read, modify or delete another organization's saved-search alerts and change their recipients, given the alert's identifier, and to create alerts attributed to another organization. Flock remediated the issue in the hosted service on 2026-09-28; no customer action is required.
title: Cross-organization access to saved-search alerts in FlockOS

desc: An information exposure flaw in the public access-list sign-up feature of the Flock Safety Platform, present from 2026-06-23 to 2026-10-22, allowed a remote, unauthenticated attacker who had a community's public sign-up link and a registered vehicle's license plate to retrieve that registrant's name, email address, home address and approval status. Each lookup required solving a CAPTCHA. No license plate reader detections, images or video were exposed. Flock remediated the issue in the hosted service on 2026-10-22; no customer action is required.
title: Information exposure in Flock Safety Platform public access-list sign-up

desc: An uncontrolled XML entity expansion vulnerability in the Flock Installer app for Android before version 2.35.0 allows an attacker who has a valid technician account and controls or impersonates the camera being set up to crash the app, on devices running Android 10, 11 or 12, by returning a camera configuration response that contains nested XML entity declarations. The vulnerability does not allow the attacker to read or change data on the device, and no customer license plate, video or location data is exposed. Android 13 and later reject the response. The issue is fixed in version 2.35.0; update to 2.35.0 or later.
title: Uncontrolled XML entity expansion in the Flock Installer app for Android

desc: A path traversal vulnerability in Ivanti Sentry before versions 11.0, 10.8.3, and 10.7.4 allows a remote authenticated attacker with administrative privileges to create arbitrary directories and files with root privileges.
SQL injection in the Core of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before version 2024 SU8 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution.
Missing authentication in Ivanti Cloud Services Application version 5.0.8 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to add and delete arbitrary trusted EPM Core certificate entries.

A out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the dr_mp3 drmp3_init_internal functionality of dr_libs (version(s): 0.7.3). A specially crafted .mp3 file can lead to an out-of-bounds read. An attacker can provide a malicious file to trigger this vulnerability.

A out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists in the dr_wav drwav__read_cue_to_metadata_obj functionality of dr_libs (version(s): 0.14.5). A specially crafted .wav file can lead to an out-of-bounds write. An attacker can provide a malicious file to trigger this vulnerability.

The admin service of the standalone OpenEJB server accepts stop requests without any authentication. Any local user or process able to connect to the admin port can stop the server, leading to denial of service; the admin service is enabled by default in the standalone server and bound to the loopback interface. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Unauthenticated server shutdown via the admin port

desc: When JAX-WS or JAX-RS endpoints are published by the embedded OpenEJB HTTP server rather than Tomcat, some configured authentication methods are silently ignored and the endpoint is published without authentication. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the exposed operations without credentials. Only deployments that use the embedded HTTP server and rely on such an authentication method are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: Missing authentication for web service endpoints in embedded HTTP server

desc: With the default configuration and no users defined in the default user database, TomEE silently adds an administrative user with a well-known password at startup. A remote attacker can use these credentials to authenticate to web applications that use the default realm and grant access to any authenticated user or to the TomEE administrative role. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Well-known administrative credentials created at startup

desc: The optional request routing feature forwards requests to their configured destination without applying the security constraints of that destination or the protection of the web application's private directories. If a route copies client-controlled parts of the request path into its destination, a remote attacker can reach protected resources or read application configuration and class files. Only installations with such a routing configuration are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Security constraint bypass via request routing

desc: The embedded server generates HTTP session identifiers with a non-cryptographic random number generator by default. A remote attacker who observes a session identifier can predict the identifiers issued to other users and hijack their sessions, if the application relies on HTTP sessions for authentication. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Predictable HTTP session identifiers in embedded server

desc: The Jakarta Security OpenID Connect authentication mechanism generates the state and nonce values with a non-cryptographic random number generator and insufficient entropy. A remote attacker who predicts these values can forge an authentication callback that logs a victim into the attacker's account, and the replay protection for ID tokens is weakened. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Predictable OpenID Connect state and nonce values

desc: The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store accepts an empty password as valid if the directory server allows unauthenticated binds, which some directory servers do by default. A remote attacker can then authenticate as any existing user without knowing the password. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication bypass with empty password in LDAP identity store

desc: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.4.0 through 5.6.2, the Identity REST APIs (identity/v1, and identity/v2 since 5.5.0, provided by org.eclipse.kura.rest.identity.provider) do not check identity and permission management requests against the permissions of the requesting identity. An authenticated identity holding the rest.identity permission, but not kura.admin, can assign any permission to any identity, including kura.admin to itself. It can also change the password of, or delete, identities holding more privileges than its own, including administrators, and create or delete permissions. This allows escalation to full administrative privileges and can lock legitimate administrators out of the device. The issue is fixed in Eclipse Kura 5.6.3.

A negative MicroProfile JWT clock skew setting is not rejected and disables validation of the token expiration and other time-based claims. In such configurations, an attacker in possession of an expired token can still authenticate with it. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Expired MicroProfile JWT tokens accepted with negative clock skew

desc: When MicroProfile JWT role-based access control is used, the access constraints of JAX-RS resources are not always enforced as declared: resources that declare an empty set of allowed roles are accessible to every caller, resource classes that inherit the same method from a common superclass share their constraints, and class-level constraints declared on a superclass are ignored. A remote attacker can invoke resources that should be denied to them, in some configurations without authentication. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Authorization bypass in MicroProfile JWT role checks for JAX-RS resources

desc: After a successful WS-Security UsernameToken authentication, the caller identity stays associated with the worker thread once the request completes when web services are served by the standalone OpenEJB HTTP server. A remote unauthenticated attacker whose request is later processed on the same thread can invoke protected EJB methods with the identity of a previously authenticated user. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Privilege escalation via WS-Security caller identity leaking between requests

desc: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server does not isolate HTTP sessions between web applications. A remote attacker can use a session established in one web application in another one, which then trusts session state set by the first application. Only deployments hosting several web applications on the embedded HTTP server are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: HTTP sessions shared across web applications in embedded HTTP server

desc: When resolving security roles of a realm-authenticated caller, the caller's user name is also treated as a role name in addition to the roles assigned by the realm. An authenticated attacker who can obtain an account whose user name equals a role name, for example through self-registration, is granted that role wherever authorization is evaluated through the Jakarta Authorization policy. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Privilege escalation via user name matching a role name

desc: The Jakarta Security identity store backed by the Tomcat user database compares the supplied password with the stored value as plain text and ignores the configured credential handler. When digested passwords are stored, an attacker who obtained a stored digest, for example from a leaked users file or backup, can authenticate with the digest instead of the password. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication with the stored password digest in Tomcat user identity store

desc: The development-time LiveReload support listens on all network interfaces without authentication and accepts websocket connections from any origin. A network attacker, or a web page visited by the developer, can observe the names of changed files in the watched folder and the server version, and reach the deployed applications through the additional port. This only affects LiveReload enabled in the embedded Maven plugin. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Unauthenticated LiveReload endpoint reachable from the network

desc: The embedded OpenEJB HTTP server reports every request as authenticated when an application requests authentication programmatically. A remote unauthenticated attacker can access functionality protected this way. Only applications served by the embedded HTTP server that rely on programmatic authentication are affected. Users are recommended to block network access to the embedded HTTP server from untrusted clients, or to migrate to the Tomcat based TomEE distributions.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication bypass via programmatic authentication in embedded HTTP server

desc: Improper Input Validation in Zoom Workplace for Windows may allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.

The optional SSH administration service grants full access to the administration shell to every user that authenticates against its configured login domain, without checking for an administrative role. An attacker holding the credentials of any user in that domain, including a low-privileged application user, can execute arbitrary code as the server process. Users are recommended to disable the SSH administration service, or to block network access to it from untrusted clients and restrict its login domain to administrative users.
title: Apache TomEE: Code execution by any authenticated user via the SSH administration shell

desc: The JDBC based JAAS login module accepts a login without a password for accounts whose stored password is NULL. A remote attacker who knows the user name of such an account can authenticate as that user and obtain its roles. Only deployments using this login module with NULL passwords in the user table are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication bypass for accounts without a stored password in SQL login module

desc: When a non-default stateful session bean passivation strategy is configured, passivated bean state is written to predictably named files in the shared system temporary directory, reusing files that already exist there, and is deserialized on activation. A local attacker who can write to that directory can read passivated session state or supply data that the server deserializes, potentially leading to code execution as the server process. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Local code execution via predictable passivation files in the shared temporary directory

desc: When MicroProfile JWT authentication is used for servlets that declare a run-as identity, the security state established for a request is not always cleared from the processing thread when the request does not complete normally. A remote attacker holding a valid token can cause later, unrelated requests served by the same thread to invoke enterprise beans with the elevated run-as identity. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Privilege escalation via leaked MicroProfile JWT run-as identity

desc: Argument injection in Ivanti EPMM before version 12.11.0.0, 12.10.0.1, and 12.9.0.3 allows a remote authenticated attacker with admin privileges to delete arbitrary files on disk.
Origin Validation Error in Zoom Workplace for Windows may allow an unauthenticated user to conduct an escalation of privilege via network access.

OS command injection in Ivanti Sentry before versions 11.0.0, 10.8.3, and 10.7.4 as well as in Ivanti EPMM before versions 12.11.0.0, 12.10.0.1, and 12.9.0.3 allows a remote authenticated attacker with admin privileges to achieve remote code execution.

Improper input validation in Ivanti EPMM before version 12.11.0.0, 12.10.0.1, and 12.9.0.3 allows a remote authenticated attacker with admin privileges to set arbitrary Linux kernel parameters as root.
Cleartext storage of sensitive information in Ivanti UWM before version 2026.4 allows a local authenticated attacker to retrieve another local user's session token.

Improper input validation in Ivanti EPMM before version 12.11.0.0, 12.10.0.1, and 12.9.0.3 allows a remote authenticated attacker with admin privileges to permanently disable all Apache HTTPS services resulting in denial of service.
Argument injection in Ivanti Sentry before version 11.0, 10.8.3, and 10.7.4 allows a remote authenticated attacker with admin privileges to execute arbitrary on-disk binaries.

The bundled JAAS login modules leak whether a username exists and compare credentials in a non-constant-time manner. A remote unauthenticated attacker can enumerate valid accounts and may infer credential material through timing analysis. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Username enumeration and timing side channel in JAAS login modules

desc: The stateful session bean passivation mechanism derives the on-disk file name from a client-supplied identifier without validating it. A remote attacker with access to the remote EJB service can cause session state to be read from or written to files outside the passivation directory. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Path traversal via stateful EJB passivation

desc: Stateful session bean identifiers are not generated from a cryptographically secure random source. A remote attacker with access to the EJB remote endpoint who holds one valid identifier can derive those of other clients' sessions and invoke methods on their beans, exposing or modifying other users' session state. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Stateful session bean hijacking via predictable session identifiers

desc: The internal system EJBs used for remote deployment and configuration did not enforce their administrative role check when the server ran with the default profile. A remote unauthenticated attacker able to reach the remote EJB endpoint could deploy arbitrary applications and execute code. Only installations that enabled the system applications and a remote EJB endpoint are exposed. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Missing authorization on internal deployer EJBs in default profile

desc: Docker Desktop before version 4.94.0 could write the signed-in user's Docker Hub access token (a JWT) in cleartext to application logs and diagnostics bundles. IPC payloads that were bare JSON strings or arrays were not redacted before logging, and a Docker Desktop component logged the token when it requested it from the backend. An attacker with read access to these files could obtain the token and use it to read and modify the user's Docker Hub data as that user while the token remains valid. Docker Desktop 4.94.0 redacts these payloads. The fix does not rewrite logs written by earlier versions, which can still contain tokens after upgrading.
title: Docker Desktop logs can expose the Docker Hub access token

desc: A flaw was found in Podman. An attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by supplying a container image containing crafted metadata labels. Podman's auto-update mechanism improperly trusts these image labels to determine which system services to restart. If a user runs the malicious container and auto-update processes it, arbitrary system services are restarted with the user's privileges, potentially allowing an attacker to shut down the host system when Podman runs with administrative privileges.
products: red hat:red hat openshift container platform 4
title: Podman: untrusted image labels allow auto-update to restart arbitrary systemd units

desc: The Jakarta Security LDAP identity store does not neutralize special characters in the caller name before using it in directory queries. A remote unauthenticated attacker can alter the queries to enumerate accounts, infer directory attribute values, or influence which directory entry the login is validated against. Only applications using the LDAP identity store are affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: LDAP injection in LDAP identity store

desc: Authentication configured for an EJB JAX-WS endpoint in the TomEE deployment descriptor is not enforced when the endpoint is published within an existing web application. A remote unauthenticated attacker can invoke the web service operations, unless the application protects the endpoint with its own web.xml security constraints or EJB method permissions. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Missing authentication on EJB web service endpoints deployed in a web application

desc: The security constraint generated for EJB JAX-WS endpoints with configured authentication protects only some HTTP methods. A remote unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication by sending requests with another HTTP method. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 10.3.0 or 11.0.0-M2, which fix the issue.
title: Apache TomEE: Authentication bypass on EJB web service endpoints via HTTP method

desc: In Eclipse Kura versions 5.0.0 through 5.6.2, the Wire Graph update functionality of the Kura Web UI, and the Wire Service REST API v1 (available since 5.1.0, org.eclipse.kura.rest.wire.provider), determine whether a configuration update targets a Wire Component, Driver or Asset from the factory identifier supplied in the request, instead of the actual factory of the existing component. An authenticated identity holding only the Wires management permission (kura.wires.admin for the Web UI, rest.wires.admin for the REST API) can therefore modify the configuration of existing components that are not part of the Wire Graph, including security-relevant ones, or replace existing components. This allows escalation to full administrative privileges and can disrupt the device. Modifying arbitrary components requires at least one Driver to be installed on the device. The issue is fixed in Eclipse Kura 5.6.3.

Eclipse Kura downloads deployment packages (DPs) from a remote URL without any limit on the size of the data it receives. A malicious or compromised HTTP(S) server, or an attacker able to tamper with a plain-HTTP download, can stream an arbitrarily large (or endless) response. Kura writes the response to local storage until the filesystem is full. On gateways the temporary directory is often a RAM-backed tmpfs, so this can also exhaust memory. The result is denial of service of the device: failed configuration persistence, failed logging and possible crashes of the framework or other services.



The same missing size limit is present in the REST upload endpoint `POST /deploy/v2/_upload`, which copies the request body to the temporary directory with no limit.



Workarounds: only install DPs from trusted HTTPS sources, restrict who can install packages (Web UI `kura.packages.admin` permission, REST `kura.permission.rest.deploy`, cloud DEPLOY-V2 access).

V programming language standard library net.http through version 0.5.2 prior to commit 4077484 contains a TLS certificate validation bypass vulnerability that allows on-path attackers to intercept HTTPS traffic by exploiting the default false value of SSLConnectConfig.validate and FetchConfig.validate, which completes TLS handshakes without verifying certificates in both the mbedtls and OpenSSL backends. Attackers can present an expired, self-signed, wrong-hostname, or untrusted-root certificate to successfully complete the handshake via http.get, http.post, or http.fetch, enabling interception or modification of HTTPS traffic unless validate: true is explicitly configured.
title: V Programming Language net.http TLS Certificate Validation Bypass

desc:
Summary


Cloudflare tokio-quiche was found to contain an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in its HTTP/3 DATAGRAM handling. For every previously unseen flow identifier (quarter stream ID) received in a DATAGRAM frame, tokio-quiche creates and retains new, per-flow state. A remote peer can send DATAGRAMs with many distinct identifiers, causing the per-connection flow map and associated channel state to grow without bound.

Impact


Exploitation can exhaust process memory and cause a denial of service. The vulnerable code is used in both client and server configurations, so either role can be affected by a malicious peer. QUIC DATAGRAM support in tokio-quiche is enabled by default through QuicSettings::enable_dgram; applications can disable it by setting this field to false. The vulnerable HTTP/3 path is reachable only when DATAGRAM support is negotiated with the peer. Core quiche and HTTP/3 deployments without DATAGRAM support are not affected. 






Mitigation


Disable DATAGRAMs in tokio-quiche’s QuicSettings::enable_dgram.






Remediation


Upgrade to tokio-quiche version 0.23.0 or later. The fixed code creates flow state only for valid DATAGRAM-capable request streams, which are bounded by QUIC’s stream limits. To tolerate packet reordering, servers retain early DATAGRAMs in a bounded, expiring buffer, while clients discard DATAGRAMs for unknown flows.
title: Unbounded HTTP/3 Datagram flow map growth in tokio-quiche

desc: The sourcecache expansion module in MISP Modules (misp-modules) contains a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. When a user with permission to create or modify attributes of type 'link' or 'url' submits an attribute value, the module passes the URL directly to its internal archiving function without any validation of the target address. An attacker can therefore craft a URL pointing to loopback addresses (e.g., 127.0.0.1), private network ranges, link-local addresses, or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., 169.254.169.254). The MISP server will issue an HTTP request to that target and store the response body in the event, effectively exfiltrating data from internal services to the attacker through the MISP interface. Non-HTTP schemes such as file:// are also accepted, potentially allowing local file disclosure. The vulnerability requires an authenticated MISP user with the ability to create or edit attributes of the affected types. The security impact is information disclosure from internal services reachable by the MISP server, including sensitive data such as cloud credentials, internal application data, or local files.
title: MISP sourcecache module SSRF allows fetching arbitrary internal URLs via attribute enrichment

desc: Custom Post Types and Custom Fields creator (WCK) before 2.4.1 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers with access to any WCK meta box to read custom-field values on posts they cannot edit by exploiting the wck_show_update_form AJAX handler, which lacks the capability checks enforced by other handlers and relies on a shared, non-unique nonce action. Attackers can send a crafted admin-ajax.php request with a valid wck-edit-entry nonce, a target meta key, and an arbitrary post ID to disclose sensitive post-meta or option values belonging to other users, including private or draft post data.

desc: A flaw was found in BusyBox. When resuming a download over File Transfer Protocol (FTP), the wget utility fails to verify that the resume offset does not exceed the file size reported by the server, resulting in an integer calculation error. A malicious FTP server or an on-path network attacker can exploit this issue by returning crafted file size metadata, triggering a heap-based buffer overflow with attacker-controlled data. Successful exploitation may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code or crash the application, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
title: Busybox: heap buffer overflow in wget ftp resume when the resume offset exceeds the reported file size

desc: NVIDIA NeMo Export-Deploy for all platforms contains a vulnerability in multimodal deployment where an attacker could cause a server-side request forgery. A successful exploit of this vulnerability might cause information disclosure.

A vulnerability has been identified in SIMATIC BATCH V9.1 (All versions), SIMATIC Information Server 2020 (All versions), SIMATIC Information Server 2022 (All versions), SIMATIC PCS 7 V9.1 (All versions), SIMATIC Process Historian 2020 (All versions), SIMATIC Process Historian 2022 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC Runtime Professional V17 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC Runtime Professional V18 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC Runtime Professional V19 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC Runtime Professional V20 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC Runtime Professional V21 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC V8.0 (All versions), SIMATIC WinCC V8.1 (All versions). desc: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-base RTCP SDES packet parser. desc: A flaw was found in GStreamer's MXF demuxer. desc: 7-Zip before 26.06 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the LZX decoder that lets attackers corrupt memory when a continuation CAB volume declares a smaller window. desc: OS command injection in the pass and bitwarden credential providers in Eclipse Foundation Eclipse Otterdog through 1.7.1 allows a user able to modify an organization configuration to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the operator running otterdog, including access to their credential vault, via a crafted secret reference (pass:<path> or bitwarden:<item>@<field>) or credential identifier that is resolved when otterdog apply is run.

desc:
The Vaadin Rich Text Editor exports a video embed without escaping its value, and then parses the resulting HTML into live DOM. A value crafted to break out of the href attribute therefore runs script in the viewer's browser. An attacker who can edit shared content pastes a video embed carrying the payload, the delta is stored, and the script runs when any user opens the page, including in read only mode.

Only content persisted through asDelta() is affected. The default HTML value, set and read through setValue and getValue, is sanitized on the server with a safelist that has no iframe, so the embed does not survive that path. Vaadin 24 and older are not affected: they build the HTML value from the editor's own innerHTML, which the browser escapes.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

Product version
Vaadin 25.0.0 - 25.0.13
Vaadin 25.1.0 - 25.1.13
Vaadin 25.2.0 - 25.2.12
Vaadin 25.3.0 - 25.3.4

Mitigation
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
No fixed release on this line, upgrade to 25.2.13 or newer
Upgrade to 25.2.13
Upgrade to 25.3.5
title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in the Vaadin Rich Text Editor via an Unescaped Video Embed

DownloadEvent.setFileName(String) in Vaadin Flow writes the download file name into the Content-Disposition header without escaping it. When the name is pure US-ASCII the header is built as attachment; filename="<name>" with the name inserted verbatim, so a double quote in the name ends the quoted string early and the rest of the name is read by the browser as further header parameters. The inline(String) variant, present from Vaadin 25.0, builds the name the same way. An application that passes an untrusted file name to either method, for example when re-serving a file under the name it was uploaded with, lets an attacker add a filename* parameter. Browsers prefer filename* over filename, so the file is saved under a name and extension of the attacker's choosing, which defeats any file name or extension restriction the application enforces. The attacker cannot change the attachment or inline disposition itself and cannot split the header.

Users of affected versions should apply the following mitigation or upgrade. Releases that have fixed this issue include:

desc: A vulnerability has been identified in Mendix Studio Pro 11 (All versions >= V11.15.0 < V11.16.0), Mendix Studio Pro 11.12 (All versions >= V11.12.6 < V11.12.7). An address beginning with "-" is parsed by curl as an option instead of a hostname, allowing an attacker who can attach a crafted LUKS/clevis block device (for example, a local unprivileged user with an active console or desktop login session) to have an administratively-privileged Cockpit user unknowingly trigger curl option injection when editing the device's Tang keyserver settings. This can lead to arbitrary file read or write as the Cockpit session user.
title: Cockpit: cockpit-storaged: tang keyserver address from an untrusted luks header clevis token reaches curl's argument vector as an option

desc: A use-after-free flaw was found in GStreamer core buffer value deserialization. Applications that parse untrusted caps or structure data can reach a freed-buffer read and may crash. desc:
Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes vulnerability in the device API, device forms, signing key and product forms and JITP settings in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user who manages devices in any organization to write into other organizations via submitted org_id, product_id and deployment_id fields. The device API create and update actions and the dashboard device forms pass the request parameters to NervesHub.Devices.Device.changeset/2, which casts the organization, product, deployment group and update state as given. The signing key and product forms merge the session's organization into the submitted parameters so that a submitted org_id wins, and the JITP changeset accepts any product_id. Each request requires the manage role only in the user's own organization, and any account can create one.

A device placed on another organization's deployment group, or moved into its product, is sent that organization's firmware with a download URL. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization, and cannot upload firmware to it.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.
title: Mass assignment of organization, product and deployment group IDs allows users to write into other organizations and receive their firmware

desc:
Improper Session Invalidation vulnerability in the dashboard pages, device console and local shell channels in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an organization member who is removed or given a lower role to keep acting at their old role through anything they had open at the time. The dashboard reads the member's role once when a page mounts, in the assign_org_to_scope hook of NervesHubWeb.Auth, and the console, local shell and device event stream channels check membership once at join. Removing a member or changing their role tells none of them, so open pages keep carrying out actions and open consoles keep running commands on the device until the page reloads or the socket disconnects.

The dashboard also opens consoles over NervesHubWeb.UserSocket with a token that holds only the user's id, is accepted for 24 hours, and is not revoked by signing out, which disconnects only the session's LiveViews. Whoever holds a token taken from a page can open consoles as that user, within the user's current membership, until it expires.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.
title: Improper session invalidation keeps removed or demoted members' open pages and device consoles working at their old role

desc:
Improper Authentication vulnerability in Google sign-in and email confirmation in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an attacker who registers another person's email address to share that person's account once they sign in. NervesHub.Accounts.update_or_create_user_from_ueberauth/1 signs a Google user in to any account carrying the same email that is not yet linked to a Google account, links it and marks the email confirmed, without the account's owner ever having proved they own the address. NervesHubWeb.SessionController.confirm/2 likewise signs in whoever follows a confirmation link. An attacker registers the address from the sign-up form, changes their own account's email to it, or registers it as an organization admin from an invite link, and keeps the password; when the address's owner signs in with Google or follows the confirmation link, they land in that account.

The Google path also creates accounts with registrations closed and never checks Google's email_verified claim, and the API's password sign-in in NervesHubWeb.API.UserController issues tokens to accounts whose email was never confirmed. The attacker gains only what the victim is granted afterwards, and nothing on accounts whose owners never use either path.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.3.
title: Improper authentication lets Google sign-in and confirmation links sign users in to accounts registered with their email address by someone else

desc:
Missing Authorization vulnerability in the device and deployment group pages in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated organization member with the view role to change devices and deployment groups via LiveView events reserved for the manage role. The event handlers that add and delete device certificates, add and remove tags, overwrite or clear a device's manual location, remove a device from its deployment group, move matched devices into a deployment group or remove unmatched ones, import devices from a CSV, and start, retry or delete firmware delta builds carry out the change without calling authorized!/2, and the pages render the controls to every member.

A view member can add a certificate that lets whoever holds its key connect as the device, delete a certificate so the device can no longer authenticate with it, and change which deployment group, and so which firmware release, a device receives. Everything stays within the organizations the member belongs to.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.
title: Missing authorization in device and deployment group page events allows view-role members to change devices and deployment groups

desc:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user with the manage role in one organization and only the view role in another to move devices into the second organization's product via the "Move device(s) to product" action. The target-product event in NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.Index looks the product up with NervesHub.Products.get_by_id/2, which checks that the user is a member of the product's organization at any role, and move-devices-product then changes each selected device's organization and product. The device API's move requires manage in the target organization, and an earlier fix added the check on the organization the devices leave but not on the one they enter.

A moved device keeps its key and certificate, joins the target organization's matching deployment groups, and is sent their firmware with a download URL, which the view role cannot otherwise obtain. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.
title: Incorrect authorization in the devices page bulk move allows view-role members to move devices into another organization and receive its firmware

desc:
Session Fixation vulnerability in the CLI login flow in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an API token for another user's account via a crafted login link. Starting a CLI login with POST /api/auth/cli_session needs no authentication and returns a polling token, a confirmation URL that carries that token, and a confirmation code. When a signed-in user opens that URL and clicks Confirm, NervesHub.Accounts.verify_cli_session_token/2 creates an API token for the user's account and stores it on the login, and the next poll of GET /api/auth/cli_session/<token> returns it to whoever started the login.

The confirmation code is only displayed and is never compared with anything, so it cannot show that the person confirming is the one who started the login. The confirm form carries a CSRF token and the page cannot be framed, so the attacker has to persuade the user to open the link and click the button themselves.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.5.0 before 2.5.3.
title: Session fixation in the CLI login flow allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain a user's API token

desc: A vulnerability was identified in sooperset mcp-atlassian up to 0.24.0. This issue affects the function validate_safe_path of the file src/mcp_atlassian/utils/io.py. Upgrading to version 0.24.1 is capable of addressing this issue. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

desc: SAP Cloud SDK for AI (Node.js) could inadvertently include sensitive authentication credentials in error messages generated by certain internal operations under specific failure conditions. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to reuse the disclosed credentials against the associated SAP service, resulting in a high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability.

desc: The agent_memory module accepts a caller-supplied tenant parameter in create_client(tenant=...). Prior to version 0.50.0, the tenant parameter was not validated before being used to construct filesystem paths for secret resolution. A value containing path traversal sequences (for example, attacker-corp/../victim-corp) could cause the resolved path to escape the intended directory and access another tenant's secrets under:Plain Text/etc/secrets/appfnd/hana-agent-memory/<tenant>/Successful exploitation could allow unauthorized access to another tenant's mounted credentials, including OAuth client IDs and client secrets. This vulnerability could enable cross-tenant access to sensitive credentials.

desc: The Cargo Shipping Location for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 6.0 does not properly restrict access to a REST API endpoint that updates order shipment statuses, relying on an attacker-controllable value for authorization, allowing unauthenticated users to manipulate order statuses and shipment metadata.

desc: A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which provides the core authentication and authorization logic for the identity provider. The issue occurs when a user initiates a login after visiting the password reset page, causing the system to skip mandatory security checks for Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE). This could allow an attacker who intercepts a login code to gain unauthorized access to the user's account without needing the required security verifier.
products: red hat:red hat build of keycloak
title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: client-level mandatory pkce bypass via login-actions entry point

desc: The ARMember Premium – Membership Plugin, Content Restriction, Member Levels, User Profile & User signup plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Registration Custom Field (Profile Cover) in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
products: armember:armember premium – membership plugin, content restriction, member levels, user profile & user signup
title: ARMember Premium <= 7.8.1 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Registration Custom Field

desc: The Avada (Fusion) Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form Notification Dynamic-Data action_hook → Media Upload Chain (ID3 Metadata / html_attributes) in all versions up to, and including, 3.16.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that a Fusion Form is embedded on an admin-authored page (granting manage_options context to the Dynamic Data action hook callback), and that a Post Cards element configured to display attachment post types is present on a publicly accessible page so the planted shortcode payload is rendered.
title: Avada (Fusion) Builder <= 3.16.1 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Form Notification Dynamic-Data action_hook

desc: The WPML Multilingual CMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Race Condition in versions up to, and including, 4.9.7. This is due to the `process_iframe_request` function's language-per-domain SSO handler generating the cross-domain sign-in token via `wp_create_nonce('wpml_sso')` on the logout landing page, where the browser has already discarded its authentication cookies — so `wp_get_session_token()` returns an empty string and the token collapses to the shared anonymous nonce for the current 12-hour tick rather than a user-bound secret — and then storing it in the `wpml_sso_user_<token>_<sha256('wpml_sso'.$domain)>` transient mapped to the victim's `user_id` with no binding to the specific sign-out action or requesting client. Because an unauthenticated attacker can independently derive the identical token by triggering the logout confirmation flow on `wp-login.php?action=logout`, and because the `is_iframe_request()` gate conditions (the per-domain SSO `started` transient and domain-hash derived from the public constant `SSO_NONCE`) are fully computable within the 60-second `SSO_TIMEOUT` window, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the forged `wpml_sso_token_domain` parameter with a `wpml_user_signed_in` status to a secondary language-domain endpoint before the legitimate `wpml_user_signed_out` iframe fires, causing WordPress authentication cookies to be issued for the victim. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to gain access to accounts of users — including administrators — who are actively in the process of logging out during the race window.
title: WPML Multilingual CMS <= 4.9.7 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass in Language-per-Domain SSO via 'wpml_sso_token_domain' Parameter

desc: The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the remove_csv_file_after_email_send function in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.2 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete files within the wp-content/uploads directory on the server, which can lead to loss of uploaded content. On hardened Apache configurations, deletion of uploads/.htaccess can re-enable PHP execution inside the uploads directory. This attack is only possible when the Save-and-Continue addon is active (EVF_SAVE_AND_CONTINUE_VERSION is defined) and the 'Disable storing entry information' setting is enabled on the target form. Escaping the uploads directory and deleting files in the site root can be possible under rare circumstances.
products: wpeverest:everest forms – contact form, payment form, quiz, survey & custom form builder with ai
title: Everest Forms <= 3.6.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via 'everest_forms_{form_id}_old_{field_id}' Parameter

desc: The Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 3.5.54 via the uacf7_wpcf7_mail_components function.
