Attackers can exploit the dgr_receive API's unchecked memcpy operation using synthetic datagrams or DGR traffic over internal IPC or custom transports to trigger an out-of-bounds write, leading to denial of service or potential remote code execution.
title: ION-DTN 2.2.1b-4.2.0 Integer Overflow Heap Corruption via DGR

desc: NASA JPL ION-DTN 2.1.0 through 4.2.0 contains a heap buffer under-allocation vulnerability in the Asynchronous Message Service daemon (amsd) that allows a rogue or misconfigured peer to trigger an out-of-bounds write by sending crafted Meta-AMS (MAMS) configuration management messages that are processed without cryptographic authentication. Attackers can exploit the insufficient buffer size calculation for the internal state-event object to crash the active Configuration Server thread, causing a denial of service and potentially destabilizing subsequent shared-memory allocations in amsd.
title: ION-DTN 2.1.0-4.2.0 Heap Buffer Under-allocation DoS in amsd

desc: NASA JPL ION-DTN 3.6.2 through 4.2.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in the Network Management daemon (nm_mgr) string-formatting logic that allows a malicious or misconfigured agent to trigger an out-of-bounds write by sending deeply nested AMP payloads that exceed fixed-size buffer allocations through unbounded strcat operations. Attackers can transmit oversized AMP reports, tables, or macros over the UDP CLA/AMP path or trigger the flaw locally via interactive UI rendering to crash nm_mgr and cause a denial of service halting telemetry collection and operator visibility.
title: ION-DTN 3.6.2-4.2.0 Heap Buffer Overflow via nm_mgr AMP Rendering

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 10.1.0 until 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, loadOptionsById_Transaction and getUserInfoByCredentialId_Transaction perform application-scoped WebAuthn lookups without constraining them to the requested tenant, and WebAuthN.signIn does not verify tenant membership. In a multi-tenant deployment using WebAuthn with a shared user pool, an ordinary user who possesses their own valid passkey in one tenant can submit its assertion to another tenant's sign-in endpoint in the same application and be authenticated there despite having no membership in the target tenant. This issue is fixed in versions 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.
title: SuperTokens Core: WebAuthn sign-in accepts a passkey across tenant boundaries

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 11.3.0 until 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, a licensed deployment with a configured SAML client can authenticate an identity from an assertion that did not satisfy the audience check. When the identity provider uses assertion-level signing, an attacker who has a still-valid IdP-signed assertion naming the victim for any audience and the attacker's own valid assertion for the target audience can combine them because validateSamlResponseAudience accepts an audience from one assertion while extractAllClaims takes the final NameID and attributes from another; response-level signing does not expose this multi-assertion variant. Independently, an assertion from an identity provider configured for the target deployment but issued to another SuperTokens deployment using the shared default saml_sp_entity_id can satisfy the target's audience check. Successful exploitation authenticates the attacker as the victim IdP user. This issue is fixed in versions 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.
title: SuperTokens Core SAML: identity taken from an assertion that never passed the audience check, allowing sign-in as any IdP user

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 7.0.0 until 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, createNewSession can resolve a primary user before unlinkAccounts detaches a login method and then insert the session after unlink has enumerated and revoked the existing sessions. A user who controls the linked login method can exploit this race to retain a signed, database-backed, refreshable session as the former primary identity after that method is unlinked; the session persists until expiry or explicit revocation. This issue is fixed in versions 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.
title: SuperTokens Core: A session created concurrently with account unlink survives the unlink

desc: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in axew3.com WP w3all phpBB wp-w3all-phpbb-integration allows SQL Injection.This issue affects WP w3all phpBB: from n/a through 3.1.9.
title: WordPress WP w3all phpBB plugin <= 3.1.9 - SQL Injection vulnerability

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 11.0.0 until 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, and 12.1.2, Dashboard.isValidUserSession treats any stored session row as valid without comparing DashboardSessionInfo.expiry to the current time. DashboardQueries.getSessionInfoWithSessionId also selects by app and session identifier without an expiry predicate, leaving the periodic DeleteExpiredDashboardSessions cleanup as the only expiration enforcement. An attacker who obtains a dashboard administrator session after its 30-day lifetime can continue using POST /recipe/dashboard/session/verify until the row is removed, and frequent Core restarts can prevent the 12-hour cleanup sweep from running. The stale session retains full dashboard read and write access, but the flaw does not provide a way to guess or acquire the random session identifier. This issue is fixed in versions 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, and 12.1.2.
title: SuperTokens Core: Dashboard session tokens are never checked for expiry: `isValidUserSession` ignores the stored `expiry`, so a long-expired admin session still authenticates

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 11.3.0 until 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, SAML.handleCallback does not consume RelayState, record assertion identifiers, or enforce Response.InResponseTo. In the SP-initiated flow, an attacker who obtains a legitimately issued, still-valid SAML response and its matching RelayState can resubmit the pair to /recipe/saml/callback before the assertion's NotOnOrAfter time; in the IdP-initiated flow, the assertion can be replayed without RelayState. The missing Response.InResponseTo check also permits an in-progress login to be completed with an assertion for a different identity and fails to enforce allowIDPInitiatedLogin=false. The callback does not validate Destination or SubjectConfirmationData Recipient and NotOnOrAfter, and each accepted callback mints a fresh, independently redeemable authorization code carrying the captured user's identity. This issue is fixed in versions 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.
title: SuperTokens Core: SAML callback accepts a replayed RelayState + SAMLResponse, minting a fresh authorization code on each replay

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 11.3.0 until 11.3.7, 11.4.7, and 12.0.10, SAML.verifySamlResponseSignature calls OpenSAML SignatureValidator.validate without first applying SAMLSignatureProfileValidator. The Core can therefore accept a cryptographically valid signature that references a different XML element from the Response or Assertion whose NameID and attributes are used for authentication. An ordinary user of the configured identity provider can move a genuinely signed element elsewhere in the document while supplying an attacker-authored identity-bearing element, causing XML Signature Wrapping authentication as another IdP user. Both response-level and assertion-level signing paths are affected, and SP-initiated login remains reachable without enabling allowIDPInitiatedLogin. This issue is fixed in versions 11.3.7, 11.4.7, and 12.0.10.
title: SuperTokens Core: SAML XML Signature Wrapping authentication bypass — any IdP user can authenticate as any other user

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. From 6.0.0 until 6.0.24, 7.0.23, 8.0.7, 9.0.6, 9.1.6, 9.2.7, 9.3.5, 10.0.8, 10.1.9, 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1, Multitenancy.checkPermissionsForCreateOrUpdate in src/main/java/io/supertokens/multitenancy/Multitenancy.java does not adequately authorize updates to a parent connection URI domain or the base tenant. In a licensed multi-tenant deployment with multiple applications under one non-default connection URI domain and separate api_keys, an attacker holding one application's valid API key can update the parent domain because the CUD-target branch checks the domain without requiring the source application and tenant to be public. Because api_keys is not protected, the attacker can replace the parent key and then sibling application keys, read or modify sibling users, obtain sessions as those users, establish persistence through a sibling dashboard user, and lock out the sibling application's own key. In the advisory's v2 create or update handlers, omitting the optional identifier produces a base-tenant target that skips the permission branches and enterprise-feature gate, allowing changes to firstFactors, required secondary factors, and recipe-enabled flags that affect login integrity and availability. The base-target variant still rejects coreConfig and does not establish key theft. This issue is fixed in versions 6.0.24, 7.0.23, 8.0.7, 9.0.6, 9.1.6, 9.2.7, 9.3.5, 10.0.8, 10.1.9, 11.0.9, 11.1.4, 11.2.4, 11.3.8, 11.4.8, 12.0.11, 12.1.2, 12.2.1, and 12.3.1.
title: SuperTokens Core: App-scoped API key can overwrite the parent connection URI domain's credentials and take over sibling applications

desc: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Melapress WP Activity Log wp-security-audit-log allows Stored XSS.This issue affects WP Activity Log: from n/a through 5.6.7.
title: WordPress WP Activity Log plugin <= 5.6.7 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability

desc: Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in Tobias WP2LEADS wp2leads allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects WP2LEADS: from n/a through 3.5.17.
title: WordPress WP2LEADS plugin <= 3.5.17 - Privilege Escalation vulnerability

desc: decode_sequence_of() in lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 and later grows the decoded element array one entry at a time, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in the KDC) by sending an unauthenticated AS-REQ or TGS-REQ with a large number of elements in a SEQUENCE OF field over TCP.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kdc unauthenticated cpu dos via quadratic asn.1 sequence of decoding

desc: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free decoded arguments on certain error paths, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) via crafted AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests that trigger authentication failures.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak dos via auth_gssapi_init error paths

desc: clean_client() in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) restarts its scan from the head of the client list after each removal, resulting in quadratic CPU cost. Remote attackers can cause a denial of service (CPU consumption in kadmind) by accumulating a large number of AUTH_GSSAPI client entries.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind unauthenticated cpu dos via auth_gssapi client states cleanup

desc: The AUTH_GSSAPI handler in lib/rpc/svc_auth_gssapi.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.2 and later allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by sending repeated failed AUTH_GSSAPI_INIT requests. Each failed request allocates client state that is only freed after a 15-minute expiration timeout, allowing an attacker to accumulate memory faster than it is reclaimed.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory exhaustion via failed auth_gssapi_init requests

desc: The RPCSEC_GSS authentication routines in lib/rpc/authgss_prot.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4 and later do not free partially decoded buffers on failure, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPCSEC_GSS messages.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak dos in rpcsec_gss buffer decode failure

desc: xdr_krb5_tl_data() in lib/kadm5/kadm_rpc_xdr.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free partially decoded data on failure, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (memory leak in kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger a decode failure.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind authenticated memory leak dos in xdr_krb5_tl_data() decode failure

desc: The policy RPC stubs in kadmin/server/server_stubs.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.5.3 and later do not reject a NULL policy name decoded by xdr_nullstring(), which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (kadmind crash via NULL pointer dereference) by sending a policy request with an empty policy name that reaches authorization checks or logging code.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind authenticated dos exploiting dereference of null policy name pointers

desc: The GSS-RPC layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not enforce size limits on XDR-decoded data, which allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption in kadmind) via crafted RPC requests that trigger unbounded memory allocations during XDR decoding.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind authenticated memory exhaustion dos via unbounded rpc xdr allocation

desc: The GSS-RPC transport layer in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.4 and later does not release the previous authentication context when a client switches from an RPCSEC_GSS or AUTH_GSSAPI flavor to a non-GSS flavor on the same TCP connection. This allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory exhaustion in kadmind) by repeatedly establishing and abandoning GSS authentication contexts.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kadmind unauthenticated memory leak dos via gss-rpc auth flavor switching

desc: krb5_ktkdb_get_entry() in lib/kdb/keytab.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.2.8 and later does not free decrypted key material when a post-decryption check fails, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in the KDC or kadmind) via requests that repeatedly trigger key decryption failures.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 kdc unauthenticated memory leak dos in kdb keytab key decryption error path

desc: clnttcp_call() in lib/rpc/clnt_tcp.c in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) does not free the RPC reply verifier between retries, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory leak in GSS-RPC client programs) by injecting RPC replies with mismatched XIDs or by triggering authentication retries.
title: Krb5: mit krb5 gss-rpc client memory leak on xid mismatch retries

desc:
A flaw was found in ansible-core's ansible.builtin.git module. The module
invokes git (ls-remote, clone, fetch) with the repository URL as a positional
argument and without a "--" separator, so a repository URL that begins with a
dash is interpreted by git as a command-line option. A caller that passes an
attacker-controlled repository URL to the module can trigger argument
injection (for example --upload-pack/--exec), resulting in arbitrary command
execution on the host running the module.

desc: The Android implementation of the Flutter/Dart receive_sharing_intent package, versions 1.4.1 through 1.9.0, contains a path traversal vulnerability in FileDirectory.getDataColumn that allows a malicious co-resident application to write files outside the intended cache directory by supplying a crafted _display_name value from an untrusted ContentProvider. Attackers can use a path-shaped display name ../databases/proof.txt combined with a controlled content stream to write to arbitrary locations within the receiving application's private sandbox under its UID, achieving file overwrite without user interaction.
title: receive_sharing_intent 1.4.1-1.9.0 Path Traversal via FileDirectory

desc:
During ABI bootstrap, the bootstrap node's approve-csr.service approves and signs every CSR without identity validation.

An attacker on the install network can retrieve the unauthenticated Ignition file (ports 22623/22624), extract a limited kubeconfig, submit a CSR for CN=system:admin, receive the signed certificate, and gain full cluster-admin access.

Exploitable only during the narrow bootstrap window.

assisted installer for red hat openshift container platform 2
red hat:red hat openshift container platform 4
red hat:red hat openshift container platform 5
title: Openshift/installer: openshift installer: unconditional csr approval during agent-based installation (abi) bootstrap

desc: A flaw was found in the rrule validation of schedules in automation controller. Several non-anchored regular expressions with lazy wildcard prefixes are applied to the user-supplied rrule value; when the expected DTSTART/RRULE tokens are absent, validation time grows quadratically with the length of the value. An authenticated user can submit a large token-free rrule through the REST API, including the schedule preview endpoint, which requires no resource-level permissions; validation runs synchronously in the API web worker, so a single such request occupies a worker for an extended time and repeated requests can exhaust the web worker pool, denying access to the API and web UI while the attack is sustained. The impact is limited to availability.
products: red hat:red hat ansible automation platform 2
title: Automation-controller: automation-controller: quadratic regex in schedule rrule validation allows an authenticated user to exhaust api web workers (denial of service)

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From 0.2.0 until 0.32.0, compose-lint automatically follows a .compose-lint.yml policy-file symbolic link outside the project and includes part of the target line when that external file fails YAML parsing. A pull request can point the policy file at a runner credential file, causing about 30 characters around an attacker-uncontrolled parse position to appear in standard error, JSON errors, and SARIF tool execution notifications uploaded by the GitHub Action. The run exits with an error and the attacker cannot select the exact disclosed line, but public logs or Code Scanning output can reveal part of the target. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.
title: compose-lint: A `.compose-lint.yml` symlinked outside the project is read, and a parse error quotes part of the target

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From 0.2.0 until 0.25.0, compose-lint follows a project-controlled symbolic link used as the Compose file outside the project. The same issue affects compose.override.yml and a COMPOSE_FILE entry from 0.22.0, and an env_file target from 0.23.0. If an external Compose-related target fails YAML parsing, the error quotes an attacker-uncontrolled line into standard error, JSON errors, and SARIF notifications, while an external env_file can expose credential-like key names through CL-0020 and CL-0021 findings. The attacker selects the target path but not the exact parser-failure line, values from env_file are not printed, and the pass or fail result is unchanged. This issue is fixed in version 0.25.0.
title: compose-lint: A committed symlink makes compose-lint quote a file from outside the project into its output

desc: SuperTokens Core is an open source authentication server. Prior to 11.3.6, 11.4.6, and 12.0.8, app-specific management requests using an unknown tenant path and an older supported cdi-version can bypass API-key and public-tenant enforcement. In src/main/java/io/supertokens/webserver/WebserverAPI.java, checkIPAccess and assertThatAPIKeyCheckPasses suppress TenantOrAppNotFoundException, while the later app-specific handler resolves app/public storage and the public-tenant guard applies only to CDI versions 5.0 and later. An unauthenticated caller able to reach the Core endpoint can therefore use PUT /ghosttenant/recipe/role and GET /ghosttenant/recipe/roles to create and enumerate application roles without a valid API key. This issue is fixed in versions 11.3.6, 11.4.6, and 12.0.8.
title: SuperTokens Core: Unknown tenant path bypasses API key and public-tenant enforcement

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From 0.22.0 until 0.32.0, compose-lint substitutes values from a sibling .env file into image fields and quotes the resolved value in CL-0004 and CL-0019 finding messages and fix text. In a workflow that writes secrets into that file and then lints untrusted pull-request content, an attacker can reference a secret variable so its whole value reaches the job log, JSON output, SARIF artifacts, and Code Scanning alerts. Fork pull requests normally lack secrets, so exploitation requires a secret-bearing workflow such as pull_request_target, same-repository branches, or a retained .env on a self-hosted runner, and the pass or fail result is unchanged. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.
title: compose-lint: A pull request can make compose-lint quote a secret from a CI-generated `.env` into its findings

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From 0.32.0 until 0.33.0, compose-lint's incomplete remediation for .env secret disclosure checks the 20,000-finding limit before replacing resolved values with their variable references. A pull request can combine a secret-referencing image field with aliased content that produces more than 20,000 findings, causing the early-stop path to emit already graded findings with the resolved secret value in text, JSON, SARIF, and Code Scanning output. Exploitation requires a workflow that writes secrets into the sibling .env and lints untrusted changes, and the run exits 2 unless --allow-partial-coverage is used. This issue is fixed in version 0.33.0.
title: compose-lint: Incomplete fix for GHSA-jf3h-8jvx-vcrg: a run stopped at the finding limit quotes a secret from a CI-generated `.env`

desc:
Redpanda Connect versions 4.39 to 4.110 contain a missing authentication vulnerability that enables unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). In streams mode, the management HTTP API is exposed on `0.0.0.0:4195`, but authentication is disabled by default and there is no authentication gate protecting the stream CRUD routes. An unauthenticated attacker with network access to TCP/4195 can `POST` a malicious pipeline definition to `/streams/{id}` that includes code-executing processors such as `command`, `subprocess`, `ffi`, or unsafe `sql_raw`, thereby achieving arbitrary RCE on the host with the permissions of the Redpanda Connect service account. Because pipelines can also return command output in-band via HTTP, this vulnerability enables full host compromise, credential theft, and data exfiltration with no user interaction or credentials required.  

Starting with v4.111, the API endpoint was reconfigured as opt-in, so this and later versions are no longer vulnerable by default. However, RCE remains achievable on v4.111 and later if the management API is manually enabled via the `--bind-http` flag.
title: CVE-2026-123270

desc: Thor Vector Graphics (ThorVG) is a production-ready vector graphics engine. Prior to 1.1.2, the bundled jpgd JPEG decoder accepts duplicate component selectors in an SOS scan header, causing each duplicate to increase m_blocks_per_mcu without checking the buffers sized from the frame components. A crafted grayscale JPEG can repeat its component in the SOS header, causing decode paths in src/loaders/jpg/tvgJpgd.cpp to write beyond heap buffers sized for one component. The issue is reachable through direct JPEG decoding and through JPEG images embedded in Lottie content, and confirmed impact is memory corruption followed by a process crash. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.2.
title: ThorVG: Heap buffer overflow (OOB write) in bundled jpgd JPEG decoder

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. Prior to 0.31.0, compose-lint prints attacker-controlled service names, environment keys, file lines, and other Compose text without neutralizing GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines workflow-command openers. When a workflow processes a pull request, legacy ##[ commands or a line-leading double-colon command can create false annotations, hide log regions, mask selected strings, or invoke other commands recognized by the runner. The affected text report paths do not alter the compose-lint exit code or pass or fail result, but they can misrepresent the CI output presented to reviewers. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.
title: compose-lint: Compose file text can issue GitHub Actions workflow commands through the compose-lint Action

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From 0.22.0 until 0.31.0, compose-lint follows a sibling .env symbolic link outside the project without applying its normal containment check. From 0.28.0, the same gap also affects an include project_directory link outside the project. A pull request can reference a variable from the linked file, causing substitution to place runner file or process-environment data into finding messages written to logs, JSON, SARIF artifacts, and Code Scanning alerts. Reading /proc/self/environ can expose the remainder of the linter process environment because NUL-separated entries are treated as one value, although disclosure requires a workflow that processes untrusted changes with useful environment data and GitHub normally withholds secrets from fork pull requests. The pass or fail result is not changed. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.
title: compose-lint: .env read through a symlink outside the project can expose the CI job's environment

desc: compose-lint is a Docker Compose security linter that identifies dangerous misconfigurations before deployment. From 0.9.0 until 0.18.0, compose-lint's YAML parser recognizes lone carriage returns and Unicode line separators U+0085, U+2028, and U+2029 as line breaks while fix position conversion counts only newline characters. A pull request can place one of these separators in a quoted value so fix --apply shifts each later edit and deletes the line after the selected target, including an unselected network or other security setting. The resulting Compose file can remain valid, post-edit checks can pass, and the command can report a successful fix even though the dry-run diff was the only place showing the extra deletion. This issue is fixed in version 0.18.0.
title: compose-lint: `fix --apply` can delete a line the user did not select, including a security setting

desc: Tasmota through 16.0.0, fixed in commit 1cb7ebc, contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass Referer-based CSRF protection in HttpCheckPriviledgedAccess() by crafting a Referer header where the device hostname or IP appears as a substring immediately after http://.evil.com/. Attackers can lure an administrator on the device's network to a malicious page to issue arbitrary console commands and reconfigure Wi-Fi, MQTT, settings, or firmware on devices lacking a WebPassword.
title: Tasmota 16.0.0 CSRF via Referer Header Validation Bypass

desc: Tasmota through 16.0.0, fixed in commit e97e1e4, contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in SendReceiveDeviceGroupMessage() that allows unauthenticated attackers on the local network to corrupt heap memory by sending crafted Device Groups messages over UDP port 4447 that cause the log_remaining counter to go negative and writes to exceed the fixed 512-byte buffer. Attackers can exploit this flaw to crash the device or potentially achieve native code execution on ESP8266 and ESP32 platforms that lack ASLR and heap cookies.
title: Tasmota 16.0.0 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via Device Groups UDP

desc: Eclipse Langium versions 3.2.0 through 4.4.0 contain an inefficient algorithmic complexity issue (CWE-407) in the opt-in IndentationAwareTokenBuilder and IndentationAwareLexer. When producing DEDENT tokens, the token builder recomputes line numbers by re-scanning the entire preceding document text. A document whose indentation changes on most lines then takes quadratic time to tokenize. Because tokenization is synchronous, a crafted document of a few hundred kilobytes can block the Node.js event loop for tens of seconds. That causes a DoS for every user served by the same process. Languages built with the DefaultLexer and DefaultTokenBuilder are unaffected.

OctoPrint provides a web interface for controlling consumer 3D printers. From 2.0.0rc1 until 2.0.0rc7, an authenticated user can supply a crafted default port or baudrate through a connect request to the bundled Serial Connector plugin. OctoPrint persists these values in printerConnection.preferred.parameters.port or printerConnection.preferred.parameters.baudrate and renders them as HTML when another user views the saved connection parameters, allowing script execution in that user's browser and actions within the user's OctoPrint access. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.0rc7.
title: OctoPrint: Stored XSS via saved connection parameters

- Triggered automatically during a migration or upgrade operation
- Can result in unauthorized data disclosure, modification, or deletion

desc:
http.cookiejar.CookieJar deleted a stored cookie when a response carried an
already expired Set-Cookie header for it, using the Domain and Path

could therefore delete cookies belonging to other domains from a shared
cookie jar, such as the one used by urllib's HTTPCookieProcessor. The fix
consults the cookie policy before an expired cookie may delete an existing
one, as required by RFC 6265 section 5.3.
title: `http.cookiejar` applies expired `Set-Cookie` to cookie store before policy validation

A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a crafted H.265 media file or stream that, when processed by an application using GStreamer, causes unpredictable parser behavior and may crash the application. This can lead to a denial of service for any application using GStreamer to play back H.265 content.

The attack needs to be performed locally. Upgrading to version 1.1.4 will fix this issue. The name of the patch is 0b2fae333d6b022da7ed4c43e2d41aa03f91dff3. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. The project maintainer explains: "[T]he attack requires write access to the index directory by a user other than the one running the application. That is a real shared-hosting scenario and worth defending against, which is why it is fixed but it is a hardening measure rather than a remotely reachable vulnerability, and the "Code Execution" impact additionally assumes the symlink target is a web-served .php file."

desc: rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.19 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.1 contain a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows unauthenticated network attackers to execute arbitrary code by pushing a crafted serialized job onto the Redis-backed Laravel Horizon queue, which runs without authentication in affected deployments. Laravel's CallQueuedHandler unserializes the job without class restrictions, allowing attackers to instantiate the existing App\\Jobs\\TaskDownloadRun class and invoke an attacker-controlled Artisan command. Attackers can leverage the bundled laravel/tinker package to execute arbitrary PHP and operating system commands as the queue worker's user, write a persistent web shell into the web-served storage/app/public directory, and read database credentials, stored device credentials, and API tokens. Where Redis is not directly reachable, authenticated attackers can deliver the payload through the application by configuring a device target that points at the rConfig server's loopback address.
title: rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.19 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.1 RCE via Unauthenticated Redis Queue Poisoning

desc: A flaw was found in GStreamer's MXF demuxer plugin (gst-plugins-bad). When processing a specially crafted MXF media file, the demuxer indexes its internal delta-entry and slice-offset tables using values from the file without validating that they are within the bounds of the allocated arrays. A local attacker who tricks a user into opening a malicious MXF file can cause the application to crash (denial of service) and may be able to read limited amounts of heap memory adjacent to the affected arrays.
title: Gstreamer1-plugins-bad-free: gstreamer1-plugins-bad-free: out-of-bounds read in mxfdemux via unchecked delta_id and slice index

desc:
Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in ash-project ash_ai allows a caller of an AshAi tool to read internal error details, including module names and data values, by making a tool call fail.

AshAi.ToToolError gained an implementation for Ash.Error.Unknown.UnknownError that returns the error's error field as is, and AshAi.Tool.Errors.format/1 sends that text to MCP clients (tool calls and resource reads in AshAi.Mcp.Server) and to the model in AshAi.ToolLoop. Ash stores the full Exception.format/2 output of a raised exception, or inspect/1 of a bare {:error, term} return, in that field. A tool result that cannot be JSON-encoded raises a Protocol.UndefinedError whose text includes the inspected value, which can be a whole record with fields the tool never returns. None of these errors were logged. The fix logs them under an error id and returns only that id to the caller.

This issue affects ash_ai: from 1.5.0 before 1.5.1.
title: AshAi sends unrecognized tool errors verbatim to MCP clients and the model, disclosing internal details

desc: A flaw was found in GStreamer's gst-plugins-good, specifically in the H.264 RTP depayloader element. When processing MTAP16 or MTAP24 multi-time aggregation RTP packets, a signed/unsigned integer conversion error causes the remaining-length counter to underflow to a large positive value when the packet is truncated. This allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds heap read of up to approximately 64 KiB of process memory by sending a single malformed RTP packet. Successful exploitation can crash the receiving GStreamer pipeline (denial of service), and in relay or transcoding deployments where output is accessible to the attacker, may expose adjacent heap contents.
title: Gstreamer1-plugins-good: gstreamer1-plugins-good: out-of-bounds heap read in mtap16/mtap24 h.264 rtp depayloader via signed/unsigned underflow

desc: Apache Airflow 3.3.1 shipped a fix for CVE-2026-67260 that checks the scheduler's decoded `next_kwargs` value is a dictionary, but performs that check only after deserializing the whole stored payload. Deserialization reconstructs nested objects of classes permitted by the deserialization allow-list — which by default includes Airflow's own classes — and runs their constructors inside the scheduler process before the check can reject the value. A Dag author, who controls a task's `next_kwargs` through the task execution API, can therefore still trigger constructor execution in the scheduler when the `awaiting_input` timeout sweep processes the task, and in the API server when the task instance is served to a worker using an older Execution API version; no non-default configuration is required. Versions before 3.3.0 are not affected. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-67260: deployments that upgraded to 3.3.1 for that issue must also upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.

desc: Apache Airflow's scheduler fully deserializes XCom values written by task code while evaluating task dependencies. Deployments that treat Dag authors as less trusted than Deployment Managers are affected, and the scheduler must be evaluating a task dependency that reads a task-written XCom value. Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to version 3.4.0 or later, which restricts dependency evaluation to primitive XCom values.
title: Apache Airflow: Deserialization of task-controlled XCom values in the Scheduler during dependency evaluation

Only deployments with both `core.multi_team = True` and `secrets.use_cache = True` are affected.

Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later. Deployments that cannot upgrade can set `secrets.use_cache = False`.

desc:

This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-45360, which only hardened the `reference` field; deployments that applied that fix remain affected through the `callback` and `interval` fields.

Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to 3.4.0 or later.

desc:
Description

`DefaultStateSerializer`, used to persist and restore stateful bolt checkpoints, configured Kryo with class
registration disabled and an instantiation strategy that constructs objects without invoking their
constructors, then deserialized whatever bytes the state store returned. A party able to write to the
topology's keyspace in the state store, for example a co-tenant of a shared Redis instance or anyone with
network access to it, could therefore place a serialized object graph that executes code inside the worker
JVM when the state is restored.

This requires the Redis-backed state provider, which is not the default. Write access to a state-store key
is a data-plane privilege; code execution in the worker JVM is not, so the two are not equivalent.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where the state serializer requires registered classes.

Note that this is a behaviour change for existing state: checkpoints written by an affected version may fail
to restore, and a migration step may be required. Users who cannot upgrade immediately should restrict
network and credential access to the state store to the cluster itself.

Credit

The ASF -- found using Claude agents to study the security of open-source projects, validated and reported by Apache Storm.
title: Apache Storm Client: Deserialization of Untrusted Data from the State Store

desc:
Description

Nimbus instantiates the class named by a topology's `topology.scheduler.strategy` when scheduling it. The
allowlist intended to constrain that choice, `nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist`, was treated as
"allow any class" when unset, and it had no entry in the shipped `defaults.yaml`, so unset was the shipped
state. An authenticated submitter could therefore cause Nimbus to instantiate any class on the Nimbus
classpath that has a no-argument constructor.

Storm's own production artifacts contain classes with side effects suitable for this: instantiating
`org.apache.storm.testing.InProcessZookeeper` starts a ZooKeeper server with its own threads and sockets
and nothing closes it, and `org.apache.storm.LocalCluster` behaves similarly. Repeated submissions
therefore consume threads, sockets and memory in the most privileged daemon in the cluster.

Mitigation

Upgrade to 3.1.0, where an unset allowlist means the strategies shipped with Storm rather than any class.

Note that this is a behaviour change: a cluster running an out-of-tree scheduler strategy without an
explicit allowlist will have those topologies refused until the class is added to
`nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist`. The rejection message names the refused class and the
configuration key.

Users who cannot upgrade immediately should set `nimbus.scheduler.strategy.class.whitelist` explicitly to
the strategies they intend to permit.
title: Apache Storm Nimbus: Submitter-Controlled Class Instantiation in Nimbus via a Fail-Open Scheduler Strategy Allowlist

desc:

A user who can read audit events but is denied Variable and Connection access can retrieve those values through the event-log API.

Users of apache-airflow are recommended to upgrade to 3.4.0 or later. Audit-log entries written before the upgrade keep the cleartext values: purge the affected entries and rotate the secrets they contain. Airflow 2.x is also affected; Airflow 2 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix, so Airflow 2 users should upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: CLI argv masking misses Variable values and --conn-extra, persisting secrets in audit logs

desc:

Anyone able to write to the Celery broker could enqueue a forged callback and execute arbitrary code on every CeleryExecutor worker, without Airflow credentials. Deployments using the CeleryExecutor are affected.

Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later, in which the worker claims the callback through the Execution API, validating the token, before running it.
title: Apache Airflow: CeleryExecutor: forged callback workloads run on Celery workers without workload-token validation

desc: Apache Airflow's asynchronous connection test checked permissions when the test was queued — only create permission when the connection ID did not exist yet — but, when the test completed with `commit_on_success`, wrote the tested connection under that ID. A user allowed to create but not edit connections could overwrite a connection someone else had created in the meantime. Only deployments that enable the non-default `[core] test_connection` setting are affected. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: Connections API: async connection test authorizes create at enqueue but overwrites a later-created connection at commit

desc: Apache Airflow's secrets masker stopped descending into nested structures after five levels, so a secret registered with the masker — for example a Connection password or a Variable value — that appeared more than five containers deep under non-sensitive keys was shown in cleartext in task logs and rendered template fields. A user who can read task logs or rendered templates, but is not meant to see those secrets, could read them. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later. Airflow 2.x is also affected; Airflow 2 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix, so Airflow 2 users should upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: Secrets masker: pattern-based masking bounded at depth 5 returns deeply-nested registered secrets in cleartext

desc: Apache Airflow's logout endpoint attempted to revoke the presented token on the server, but any failure during revocation was silently ignored and logout still reported success. When the auth manager redirects logout to an external logout URL (for example the FAB or Keycloak auth managers), server-side revocation is the only thing that invalidates the Airflow token; it failed on database errors and, reliably, for tokens from an external issuer accepted via `[api_auth] trusted_jwks_url` whose token identifier is longer than 32 characters. Anyone holding a copy of a user's token from before logout could keep using it against the Airflow API until it expired. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: Logout token revocation fails open; errors silently swallowed

desc: Apache Airflow's API endpoint for deleting an asset's queued events checked Dag edit permission against the `dag_id` query parameter, but deleted the queued events of every Dag the caller could read. An authenticated user with edit permission on one Dag and read access to others could suppress asset-triggered runs of Dags they cannot edit. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-75157: users who upgraded to apache-airflow 3.3.2 for that fix are still affected and should upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: API: asset queuedEvents DELETE checks Dag edit on a ?dag_id query value but deletes rows for every readable Dag

desc: Apache Airflow's asset API endpoints returned the IDs of Dags that are scheduled on, produce, or consume an asset without checking whether the caller may read those Dags. An authenticated user with asset read access could learn the IDs of Dags they are not authorized to see. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later. Airflow 2.x is also affected; Airflow 2 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix, so Airflow 2 users should upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: API: asset endpoints return scheduled/producing/consuming Dag IDs the caller cannot read

desc: Apache Airflow's Task Execution API stored XCom values written by a task without the reserved-key check applied elsewhere, so a Dag author's task could write an XCom that, when a user later viewed it through the API with deserialization enabled, made the API server instantiate classes from the `airflow.*` namespace with arguments the Dag author chose. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-59242: users who applied that fix in apache-airflow 3.3.1 remain affected through this route and should upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: Execution API: set_xcom skips the reserved-key check, so task-written XComs instantiate airflow.* classes on the API server

desc: Apache Airflow's secrets masker matched sensitive key names only in their snake_case form, so values stored under camelCase keys such as `privateKey`, `connectionString`, `webhookUrl` or `accessKey` — for example in a Connection's extra or a Variable — were not redacted in task logs, rendered template fields or API responses. A user who can read task logs or rendered templates, but is not meant to see those credentials, could read them in cleartext. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later. Airflow 2.x is also affected; Airflow 2 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix, so Airflow 2 users should upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: Secrets masker: camelCase key names (privateKey, connectionString, webhookUrl) not matched against the sensitive-field list

desc: The `example_dag_decorator` example Dag shipped with Apache Airflow validated an IP address fetched over HTTP with Python's `ipaddress` module and then placed it into a shell command. `ipaddress` accepts IPv6 zone identifiers containing arbitrary characters, so when example Dags are loaded (`load_examples` enabled), a user who can trigger that Dag with a custom `url` parameter could point it at a server whose response injects shell commands run on the worker. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2025-54941; users who upgraded for CVE-2025-54941 should upgrade again. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later, or to disable example Dags (`load_examples = False`), which is recommended for production.
title: Apache Airflow: Shell command injection in the example_dag_decorator example Dag via an IPv6 zone identifier

desc:
The Apache Airflow connections API did not mask the apprise provider's `config` connection extra, which can embed notification-service credentials. A user with permission to read connections could retrieve it in cleartext, although Airflow 3 treats connection credentials as write-only.

Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later. Airflow 2.x is also affected; Airflow 2 has reached end of life and will not receive a fix, so Airflow 2 users should upgrade to Apache Airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: Connections API: apprise connection "config" extra returned in cleartext

desc: Apache Airflow did not reject reserved serialization keys inside a Dag run's `conf`. A user allowed to trigger a Dag that uses a deadline alert with an asynchronous callback could pass a `conf` that, once the deadline was missed, either crashed the scheduler repeatedly or was rebuilt into objects inside the Triggerer. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow 3.4.0 or later.
title: Apache Airflow: Reserved serialization keys in Dag run conf crash the scheduler or are rebuilt as objects in the Triggerer via deadline callbacks

desc: OpenAM (OpenAM Consortium Edition) 14.0.5 and earlier contains an open redirect vulnerability (CWE-601) in the Liberty ID-FF service provider single sign-on flow. The goto parameter of the /preLogin endpoint is stored as the RelayState of the Liberty ID-FF authentication request without validation, and after the user completes single sign-on at the identity provider, the assertion consumer service redirects the browser to that value. A remote unauthenticated attacker can induce a user to access a crafted URL and, after the user authenticates, redirect the user to an arbitrary website, which may be used for phishing. Only deployments in which a Liberty ID-FF hosted service provider is configured are affected; Liberty ID-FF is not configured by default. This issue is fixed in 14.0.6, which disables the legacy Liberty ID-FF endpoints.

title: Vulnerabilities in spring-context, logback-core and Another JSON Schema Validator might affect IBM Storage Defender Copy Data Management

desc: IBM TRIRIGA Application Platform 5.0.0 through 5.0.9 IBM TRIRIGA could allow a remote authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code due to improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command.

desc: IBM Db2 11.5.0 through 11.5.9, and 12.1.0 through 12.1.5 is vulnerable to a denial of service when executing a specially crafted query with a Materialized Query Table.

This vulnerability allows an authenticated user to embed arbitrary JavaScript code in the Web UI thus altering the intended functionality potentially leading to credentials disclosure within a trusted session.

desc: IBM Qiskit SDK 1.4.2 through 2.6.2 could allow a local attacker to execute arbitrary code due to deserialization of untrusted data.

title: IBM WebSphere eXtremes Scale Liberty deployment is affected by Cross Site Scripting(XSS) attacks.

desc: IBM i 7.6, 7.5, 7.4, and 7.3 could allow an authenticated user to indirectly disable system auditing, which they otherwise don't have authority to disable.
title: IBM i is Affected by a Protection Mechanism Failure

desc: IBM watsonx Orchestrate Cartridge for Cloud Pak for Data 4.8.4 through 4.8.5, and 5.0.0 through 5.4.2 could disclose sensitive source code information that should not be accessible.
products: ibm:watsonx orchestrate cartridge for cloud pak for data
desc_es: IBM watsonx Orchestrate Cartridge for Cloud Pak for Data, desde la versión 4.8.4 hasta la 4.8.5 incluida, y desde la versión 5.0.0 hasta la 5.4.2 incluida, podría divulgar información sensible del código fuente que no debería ser accesible.
title: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM watsonx Orchestrate with watsonx Assistant Cartridge

desc: IBM watsonx Orchestrate Cartridge for Cloud Pak for Data 4.8.4 through 4.8.5, and 5.0.0 through 5.4.2 could allow an authenticated user to perform unauthorized actions due to improper trust of server-side permission methods.
products: ibm:watsonx orchestrate cartridge for cloud pak for data
desc_es: IBM watsonx Orchestrate Cartridge para Cloud Pak for Data 4.8.4 hasta la versión 4.8.5 incluida, y 5.0.0 hasta la versión 5.4.2 incluida, podría permitir a un usuario autenticado realizar acciones no autorizadas debido a una confianza inadecuada en los métodos de permiso del lado del servidor.
title: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM watsonx Orchestrate with watsonx Assistant Cartridge

desc: IBM Safer Payments 6.4.0.00 through 6.4.2.11, 6.5.0.00 through 6.5.0.09, 6.6.0.00 through 6.6.0.07, 6.7.0.00 through 6.7.0.03, and 6.8.0.00 could allow an authenticated user to obtain sensitive information, caused by improper user input validation. By using a set of API requests the user could exploit this vulnerability to decrypt sensitive information.
desc_es: IBM Safer Payments 6.4.0.00 hasta la versión 6.4.2.11 incluida, 6.5.0.00 hasta la versión 6.5.0.09 incluida, 6.6.0.00 hasta la versión 6.6.0.07 incluida, 6.7.0.00 hasta la versión 6.7.0.03 incluida, y 6.8.0.00 podría permitir a un usuario autenticado obtener información sensible, causado por una validación de entrada de usuario incorrecta. Mediante el uso de un conjunto de solicitudes de API, el usuario podría explotar esta vulnerabilidad para descifrar información sensible.
title: IBM Safer Payments could allow an authenticated user to obtain sensitive information

desc: IBM Engineering Requirements Management DOORS Next 7.1, and 7.2 could allow a remote attacker to force the Web server to return contents of a sensitive requested file due to improper input validation.
desc_es: IBM Engineering Requirements Management DOORS Next 7.1 y 7.2 podría permitir a un atacante remoto forzar al servidor web a devolver el contenido de un archivo solicitado sensible debido a una validación de entrada incorrecta.
title: IBM Engineering Requirements Management DOORS Next for J2EE File Disclosure Rule

desc: BabelDOC from 0.3.61 before 0.7.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU and memory by supplying unbounded bfrange and cidrange spans. Attackers can submit a crafted PDF whose embedded ToUnicode CMap declares a huge range, driving billions of loop iterations and stalling the translation worker.
title: BabelDOC from 0.3.61 before 0.7.0 Denial of Service via ToUnicode CMap Parsing

desc: Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Shorewall and Shorewall6 modules' list.cgi, which renders table fields and COMMENT lines unescaped. Authenticated users with table edit permission can store JavaScript via savecmt.cgi or table entries that executes when other users, including root, view the list page.
title: Webmin through 2.670 Stored XSS via Shorewall and Shorewall6 list.cgi

desc: SunEditor before 3.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the DocumentType constructor that injects header textContent into innerHTML without HTML escaping. Attackers can store entity-encoded HTML in h1-h6 headers that executes JavaScript when editors using document:header mode initialize, enabling session cookie theft.
title: SunEditor before 3.4.0 Stored XSS via DocumentType Header textContent

desc: SunEditor before 3.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the html.clean() sanitizer's _normalizeURL() function decodes named entities like : to an empty string. Attackers can inject href values such as javascript: that pass the _isSafeURL() check but are decoded by browsers, executing JavaScript when victims click stored links.
title: SunEditor before 3.4.0 Stored XSS via : Entity Sanitizer Bypass

desc: ClassroomIO through 1.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users of any organization to clone other tenants' courses via the POST /course/:courseId/clone endpoint. Attackers who know a target course id can copy its sections, lessons, exercises, and quiz answer keys into their own organization, exposing private course content.
title: ClassroomIO through 1.0.0 Cross-Organization Course Disclosure via Clone Endpoint

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the classic document controller that allows low-privilege authenticated users to recategorize other patients' documents. Attackers can invoke move_action_process to move a document into a patients|demo category, then retrieve it with an empty patient_id to exfiltrate PHI and tamper with charts.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Missing Authorization in Classic Document Controller

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the non-patient POST /fhir/DocumentReference/$docref route that allows low-privileged users to generate any patient's CCDA. Attackers with only demographics and documents permissions can supply a victim patient parameter, then download the full-chart CCDA from Patient Documents to exfiltrate clinical data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Improper Authorization in FHIR DocumentReference $docref

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the RingCentral RCFaxClient disposeDocument() method of oe-module-faxsms that allows authenticated attackers to read and write arbitrary files via the file_path parameter. Attackers can use action=download to read credentials and source code, or action=setup with base64 content to write web-executable files for code execution.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Arbitrary File Read/Write via oe-module-faxsms disposeDocument

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a broken access control vulnerability in portal/portal_payment.php that allows low-privilege authenticated users to bypass billing ACL checks by tampering patient identifiers. Attackers can modify the pid and form_pid parameters to view payment pages and record fraudulent payment receipts for arbitrary patients, corrupting billing records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Broken Access Control via portal_payment.php

desc: SunEditor before 3.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the FileUpload plugin create() method that assigns server-returned file names to innerHTML without escaping. Attackers can upload files with HTML-laden names that bypass html.clean() and execute JavaScript in victims' browsers when content or gallery items load, enabling session theft.
title: SunEditor before 3.4.0 Stored XSS via FileUpload Plugin Filename

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clinicians lacking high-sensitivity permission to read and modify encounter-bound forms via load_form.php. Attackers can request the Clinical Notes or Care Plan direct loader to obtain restricted content and a CSRF token, then submit save.php to tamper with clinical records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Authorization Bypass via load_form.php High-Sensitivity Encounters

desc: SunEditor before 3.4.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in ModalAnchorEditor's #createBookmarkList, which inserts entity-decoded h1-h6 header textContent into the bookmark list via innerHTML without escaping. Attackers can store HTML-encoded payloads in editor headers that execute JavaScript when a victim opens the link modal and types # in the URL input.
title: SunEditor before 3.4.0 Stored XSS via Link Modal Bookmark List

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an arbitrary local file read vulnerability in REST document download, where the controller passes stored uploaded document bytes to Symfony's BinaryFileResponse as a filesystem path instead of returning them as content. Authenticated users with document upload and download access can upload a document containing an absolute pathname, such as the sqlconf.php location, then download it to read server files and recover database credentials.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Arbitrary File Read via REST Document Download

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass allowing low-privileged SMART standalone-launch users to bind arbitrary patient UUIDs into the OAuth token context. Attackers with only the patients|demo ACL can select a victim during authorization and read that patient's clinical notes and documents through patient-scoped DocumentReference and Binary FHIR endpoints.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Cross-Patient PHI Exfiltration via SMART Patient Launch

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability because the prescription REST API routes check the patients.med ACL instead of patients.rx and request no specific permission bit, so read-only Medical/History access passes the check. Authenticated staff users can reuse the UI-exposed APICSRFTOKEN to enumerate prescription UUIDs, forge prescriptions for arbitrary patients, and deactivate existing prescriptions tenant-wide.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Improper Authorization via Prescription REST API

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in Rainforest patient portal payments that trusts browser-supplied patientId, encounter, and amount values instead of deriving them from the portal session. Authenticated portal patients can tamper with JSON sent to portal_payment.rainforest.php so the payin.authorized webhook writes forged ar_activity credits to other patients' encounters exceeding the amount actually paid.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Cross-Patient Payment Tampering via Rainforest Portal Payments

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the patient portal onsitedocuments API that allows authenticated patients to read other patients' documents by overriding query criteria. Attackers can send empty pid_Equals and denialReason_IsNotLike parameters to remove patient scoping and locked filters, exposing consent bodies, signatures, file paths, and template data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Cross-Patient Document Disclosure via Onsite Documents API

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to read cross-patient FHIR QuestionnaireResponse data by sending the APICSRFTOKEN header. Attackers can reuse the session-exposed api_csrf_token_js value to skip FHIR scope checks and call GET /fhir/QuestionnaireResponse, exfiltrating site-wide questionnaire answer PHI.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Authorization Bypass via FHIR QuestionnaireResponse APICSRFTOKEN

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in portal onsite-document APIs that allows any authenticated core user to access cross-patient documents. Attackers can omit the patientId parameter and supply arbitrary record IDs to list, read, and overwrite other patients' portal documents, signatures, and template data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Missing Authorization in Portal Onsite-Document APIs

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a broken object-level authorization vulnerability in the SOAP note update API, which does not verify that the supplied SOAP note ID (sid) belongs to the supplied patient and encounter. Authenticated users with encounters/notes permission can send PUT requests to /api/patient/:pid/encounter/:eid/soap_note/:sid with another patient's sid to overwrite that clinical note and reassign its pid.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Broken Object Authorization via SOAP Note Update API

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in portal/lib/persist.php that allows authenticated portal patients to modify other patients' settings by supplying an arbitrary setting_patient value. Attackers can insert or overwrite patient_settings rows for victims to suppress notifications, tamper with consent flags, or alter portal preferences.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 IDOR via portal/lib/persist.php setting_patient

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addRecall action of /interface/main/messages/save.php that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify arbitrary patients' recall data. Attackers can submit a crafted new_pid with recall, contact, provider, facility, and notification preference fields to overwrite records of patients they cannot access.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Missing Authorization via addRecall in save.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to delete arbitrary patient recall records via the delete_Recall action. Attackers can send POST requests to /interface/main/messages/save.php with a target pid and r_ID to remove recall data without ACL or ownership checks.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Missing Authorization via delete_Recall in save.php

desc: MRBS (Meeting Room Booking System) before 1.12.3 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the error parameter of view_entry.php. Attackers can send crafted links to logged-in users to read CSRF tokens, modify or delete bookings, or perform administrative actions.
title: MRBS before 1.12.3 Reflected XSS via error parameter of view_entry.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference in portal/lib/paylib.php, which writes the request-supplied form_pid (or the patient_id_cc value in Sphere data) to onsite_portal_activity without checking it against the session patient. Authenticated portal patients can submit portal-save, review-save, AuthorizeNet, Stripe, or Sphere requests to insert or modify forged payment-audit records in other patients' billing records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 IDOR via form_pid in portal/lib/paylib.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the Fee Sheet drug-inventory lookup (DrugSalesService::sellDrug) that interpolates the prod[N][warehouse] POST field into an ORDER BY clause. Low-privileged authenticated users can submit Fee Sheet product lines with constant subqueries to run a time-based blind oracle, extracting patient data and users_secure bcrypt hashes.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 SQL Injection via Fee Sheet warehouse parameter

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a broken object level authorization vulnerability in portal/report/portal_custom_report.php that allows authenticated portal patients to read other patients' problem list entries. Attackers can enumerate sequential IDs in issue_ parameter names to retrieve other patients' problem titles, clinical notes, ICD diagnosis codes, and IPPF contraceptive records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 BOLA via portal_custom_report.php Exposes Patient Problem Lists

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in interface/billing/sl_eob_patient_note.php that allows any authenticated user to read and modify patient billing notes. Attackers with low-privilege accounts can enumerate the patient_id parameter and submit POST requests using the embedded CSRF token to view or tamper with confidential billing data.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Missing Authorization via sl_eob_patient_note.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in interface/billing/sl_eob_invoice.php that allows any authenticated user to read and modify billing data for any encounter. Attackers can iterate the id parameter to read patient names and billing notes, and post payments, adjustments, deletions, or billing notes against any patient's account.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Missing Authorization and IDOR via sl_eob_invoice.php

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows patient-scoped SMART tokens to read other patients' questionnaire responses because FhirQuestionnaireResponseService does not implement IPatientCompartmentResourceService. Attackers holding a patient/QuestionnaireResponse.rs token can request responses by uuid or list the unfiltered bundle to obtain cross-patient clinical assessment answers.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 FHIR Patient Compartment Bypass via QuestionnaireResponse

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the server send HTTP requests by registering an OAuth2 client with an unvalidated jwks_uri. Attackers can trigger the fetch via the token introspection endpoint with an unsigned client_assertion to probe internal services and reach cloud metadata endpoints.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Unauthenticated SSRF via OAuth2 Client jwks_uri

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users with CAMOS access to inject HTML by saving malicious CAMOS content through ajax_save.php. Attackers can store a script payload that executes unencoded when the entry is printed via the non-print_html branch of rx_print.php, performing actions and reading data as the victim user.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Stored XSS via CAMOS Rx Print View

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the Standard REST API patient insurance and employer search, which concatenates query-string parameter names into SQL as column identifiers without escaping. Authenticated clients, including low-privilege patient-portal OAuth2 tokens, can send crafted parameter names to /api/patient/{puuid}/insurance or /api/patient/{puuid}/employer to extract patient PHI, user records, and API client secrets.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 SQL Injection via Patient Insurance and Employer REST API

desc: Trendyol kafka-konsumer from 2.3.3 before 2.6.18 contains a denial of service vulnerability in batch_consumer.go that panics when a single record exceeds MessageGroupByteSizeLimit. Attackers able to produce to the consumed topic can publish one oversized record that terminates the consumer before offset commit, causing a persistent crash loop.
title: Trendyol kafka-konsumer 2.3.3 before 2.6.18 Denial of Service via Batch Consumer Panic

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsiteDocumentController::Query() that allows authenticated portal patients to bypass the lowercase pid authorization guard by supplying a capitalised Pid parameter. Attackers can request the api/onsitedocuments endpoint with Pid set to another patient's id to overwrite the session-pinned criteria and read other patients' onsite documents containing PHI.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Patient Portal IDOR via Case-Sensitive Pid Parameter

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a local file inclusion in the ESign router (library/ESign/Router.php), which passes the unsanitized module parameter into a require_once of '<module>/Controller.php', and the fax module's faxProcessUploads writes attacker-named files to a predictable temp path without extension checks. Authenticated attackers can upload a PHP file named Controller.php, then request interface/esign/index.php with a traversing module parameter to include it and execute arbitrary code.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Remote Code Execution via ESign LFI and fax upload

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains missing authorization and insecure direct object reference vulnerabilities in the oe-module-prior-authorizations module that allow authenticated low-privilege users to access and modify other patients' records. Attackers can request public/reports/list_report.php to view all patients' names, MRNs, insurance and prior-auth data, or submit arbitrary id values to public/index.php to overwrite other patients' prior-authorization records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Missing Authorization and IDOR in Prior-Authorizations Module

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in interface/billing/sl_eob_process.php that allows authenticated users to write and read files by supplying unsanitized eraname values. Attackers without billing privileges can inject ../ sequences to create ERA report .html files anywhere the web user can write and parse arbitrary .edi files echoed into the report.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Path Traversal via sl_eob_process.php eraname

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in PortalPatientController::Read() that allows authenticated patients to read other patients' pending demographic change requests. Attackers can supply another patient's ID in the patientId query string parameter to retrieve PHI including names, addresses, SSNs, and insurance information.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 IDOR in Patient Portal PortalPatientController

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in library/ajax/upload.php that allows any authenticated user to read and overwrite document data by supplying an arbitrary doc_id. Low-privilege users can enumerate doc_id values with the fetch and save actions to disclose patient health information and tamper with medical records across all patients.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 IDOR via DICOM library/ajax/upload.php Endpoint

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in many encounter-form view and save endpoints that lack patient/encounter ownership checks. Authenticated clinical users can enumerate sequential form id values in requests such as soap/view.php and save.php to read and overwrite other patients' clinical records.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Cross-Patient IDOR via Encounter Form Viewers and Save Handlers

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the FHIR GET /fhir/Person/:uuid route that allows patient-portal users to read any staff member's demographics by bypassing compartment enforcement. Attackers holding a patient SMART token with patient/Person.read can harvest staff Person UUIDs from Appointment references to retrieve names, home addresses, phone numbers, and personal emails.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 FHIR Patient Compartment Bypass via Person Endpoint

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in its SMART on FHIR implementation because checkUserHasAccessToPatient() in BearerTokenAuthorizationStrategy.php unconditionally returns true. Authenticated users or malicious SMART apps can manipulate token launch context to bind requests to arbitrary patient UUIDs, gaining unauthorized read/write access to other patients' FHIR resources.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Authorization Bypass via checkUserHasAccessToPatient in SMART on FHIR

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in interface/forms/eye_mag/report.php that allows authenticated users to inject scripts by adding unescaped document notes. Attackers with document-note write access can store malicious JavaScript in a retina document note that executes when clinicians generate the Eye Exam patient report, exposing session cookies.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Stored XSS via Eye Exam Document Notes

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a broken access control and path traversal vulnerability in the fax/sms module disposeDocument action via an unvalidated file_path parameter. Authenticated low-privilege users can read sqlconf.php to recover database credentials and write arbitrary files as the web user, enabling remote code execution.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Arbitrary File Read/Write via disposeDocument

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsiteDocumentController::Query() that allows authenticated portal patients to read other patients' documents by overriding Pid_Equals criteria. Attackers can supply Pid_Equals, Pid_GreaterThan, or Pid_In request parameters to the onsitedocuments API to retrieve signed consent forms, signatures, and PHI of any patient.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 IDOR via Portal OnsiteDocument Pid_Equals Mass-Assignment

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in FHIR Media/:uuid and QuestionnaireResponse read routes that skip ACL checks. Non-patient API tokens lacking OpenEMR ACLs can request resources by uuid, bypassing compartment filtering to read any patient's documents and questionnaire responses.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 Missing Authorization via FHIR Media and QuestionnaireResponse Routes

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in portal/lib/persist.php that allows authenticated portal patients to write settings for other patients. Attackers can modify the setting_patient parameter in a JSON POST request to another patient's PID, altering that patient's portal settings such as the portal theme.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 IDOR in Portal Patient Settings via persist.php

desc: Frappe Framework before 15.121.1 and 16.x before 16.35.0 contains a broken access control vulnerability in File list and report queries that fails to restrict private file records to authorized users. Authenticated users can query File list or report views to obtain metadata of private files they are not permitted to access.
title: Frappe before 16.35.0 Broken Access Control in File List/Report Queries

desc: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a mass assignment vulnerability in the patient portal OnsiteDocument query API that lets request parameters set bitwise criteria filters whose values are placed unquoted into the SQL WHERE clause. Authenticated patient portal users can inject SQL via parameters such as Id_BitwiseAnd to read any database table, including other patients' records and staff password hashes.
title: OpenEMR before 8.4.0 SQL Injection via OnsiteDocument Query API

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in OnsitePortalActivityController::Update() that checks the request's patientId instead of the stored record's owner. Authenticated portal patients can send PUT requests to the onsiteportalactivity API with another patient's activity id and their own patientId to disclose tableArgs and checksum data, overwrite narratives and status, and take ownership of the record.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 IDOR via OnsitePortalActivityController Update Endpoint

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the CCDA/CCD preview stylesheets, where cda.xsl copies event-handler attributes whose values evade a character denylist and ccd.xsl copies table-cell attributes unsanitized into preview HTML. Authenticated users can upload a crafted CCDA/CCD document with onmouseover, onclick, or onfocus handlers to execute script in a clinician's session when previewed.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Stored XSS via CCDA/CCD Preview XSLT Attributes

desc: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the FaxSMS module's RCFaxClient and SignalWireClient disposeDocument functions that allows authenticated low-privilege users to read and overwrite arbitrary files via the unsanitized file_path parameter. Attackers can request action=download to retrieve cleartext files like sqlconf.php database credentials and keys, or use action=setup to overwrite web-server-writable files with ciphertext.
title: OpenEMR before 8.3.0 Arbitrary File Read and Write via FaxSMS disposeDocument

desc: OpenEMR from 7.0.1 before 8.4.0 contains a flaw in src/Common/Auth/OneTimeAuth.php that ignores the enforce_onetime_use and max_access_count flags, never revokes consumed service_auth tokens, and checks login_pin without rate limiting or strict comparison. Attackers holding a captured token can replay it or brute-force the PIN to open patient-portal sessions exposing PHI.
title: OpenEMR 7.0.1 before 8.4.0 OneTimeAuth Token Replay and PIN Brute Force

desc: OpenRemote before 1.32.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows realm administrators to access and modify global resources by calling admin endpoints lacking super administrator checks. Attackers can change the global keycloakUrl via /configuration/manager to redirect other realms' console authentication for credential phishing, inject CSS, replace map tiles, and delete logs.
title: OpenRemote before 1.32.2 Improper Authorization Allows Realm Admins to Modify Global Resources

desc: Scriban and Scriban.Signed before 7.5.3 contain uncontrolled recursion flaws in which postfix member, indexer, and call chains bypass ExpressionDepthLimit, array comparison lacks depth and cycle checks, and object.eval bypasses RecursiveLimit.
