desc: Vikunja 2.0.0 before 2.7.1 accepts form-encoded bodies on the /api/v2 login and OIDC callback endpoints without CSRF or Origin checks, enabling login cross-site request forgery. An attacker with an account can lure a victim to a page posting the attacker's credentials or OIDC code, switching the victim into the attacker's account and exposing data the victim then adds.
title: Vikunja 2.0.0 before 2.7.1 Login CSRF via /api/v2 Login and OIDC Callback

desc: Vikunja veans before 2.7.1 contains a symlink following vulnerability that allows attackers to make veans init write files outside the repository via crafted repo symlinks. Attackers can ship symlinked .veans.yml, .claude, or .opencode entries to overwrite user files like ~/.bashrc or install veans hooks and plugins globally.
title: Vikunja veans before 2.7.1 Symlink Following in veans init

desc: The Subscribe2 – Form, Email Subscribers & Newsletters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the ‘data[ip]’ parameter in all versions up to, and including, 10.47 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
title: Subscribe2 – Form, Email Subscribers & Newsletters <= 10.47 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'data[ip]' Parameter

desc: A vulnerability was detected in TOTOLINK CA300-PoE 6.2c.884. Affected by this issue is the function UploadCustomModule of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi. The manipulation of the argument File results in buffer overflow. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used.
title: TOTOLINK CA300-PoE cstecgi.cgi UploadCustomModule buffer overflow

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: conntrack: tcp: use UNACK timeout for non-closing RST packets

Commit be0502a3f2e9 ("netfilter: conntrack: tcp: only close if RST
matches exact sequence") keeps an established conntrack entry in
ESTABLISHED when an in-window RST does not match the expected sequence
number exactly, so the endpoint can validate the RST with a challenge
ACK.

The timeout selection nevertheless uses the CLOSE timeout for every RST
packet.  The bug is that timeout selection is based on the packet type,
not on the state transition result: even when RST validation keeps
new_state in ESTABLISHED, the timeout is still forced to
TCP_CONNTRACK_CLOSE.

Linux TCP independently rate limits challenge ACKs per socket.  A second
non-exact RST can therefore arrive after the first challenge ACK has
restored the timeout but before the rate limit expires.  The second RST
lowers the timeout to 10 seconds again while the endpoint suppresses the
second challenge ACK, allowing the conntrack entry to expire while both
TCP endpoints remain established.

Using the ESTABLISHED timeout for such RSTs would avoid this short
expiration window, but it could also retain stale entries for the
five-day default because conntrack cannot reliably match the endpoint's
exact TCP state.

Use the UNACK timeout for RST packets that leave the conntrack entry in
TCP_CONNTRACK_ESTABLISHED.  Exact-match RSTs and accepted RST packet
trains still fall through to timeouts[new_state], which preserves the
CLOSE timeout when conntrack accepts the RST as closing the flow.

This avoids the aggressive 10-second expiration window for non-exact
RSTs while preserving the short timeout for RSTs that conntrack accepts
as closing the flow.
title: netfilter: conntrack: tcp: use UNACK timeout for non-closing RST packets

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy()

skb_zerocopy() moves frag descriptors from @from into @to and takes a
reference on each frag, but it does not copy skb_shinfo(from)->flags into
skb_shinfo(to)->flags.  A destination skb holding the same page-cache
backed frags as the source therefore reports skb_has_shared_frag() as
false.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  ESP input
checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding whether an uncloned
nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data(); with the marker lost, an skb that
skb_zerocopy() built for nfnetlink_queue or for an openvswitch upcall is
decrypted in place, letting an unprivileged user write into the page
cache of a root-owned read-only file.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when frag descriptors are copied, as done for
the other frag-transfer helpers.
title: net: skbuff: propagate shared-frag marker in skb_zerocopy()

desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in TOTOLINK CA300-PoE 6.2c.884. Affected by this vulnerability is the function setWiFiWdsAddConfig of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi. The manipulation of the argument ApCliKeyStr leads to buffer overflow. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.
title: TOTOLINK CA300-PoE cstecgi.cgi setWiFiWdsAddConfig buffer overflow

desc: A weakness has been identified in TOTOLINK CA300-PoE 6.2c.884. Affected is the function setWiFiRepeaterConfig of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi. Executing a manipulation of the argument ApCliKeyStr can lead to buffer overflow. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks.
title: TOTOLINK CA300-PoE cstecgi.cgi setWiFiRepeaterConfig buffer overflow

desc: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in eLightUp Meta Box – WordPress Custom Fields Framework meta-box allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Meta Box – WordPress Custom Fields Framework: from n/a through 5.15.3.
products: elightup:meta box – wordpress custom fields framework
title: WordPress Meta Box – WordPress Custom Fields Framework plugin <= 5.15.3 - Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability

desc: Missing Authorization vulnerability in ThemeGrill User Registration user-registration allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects User Registration: from n/a through 5.3.1.
title: WordPress User Registration plugin <= 5.3.1 - Broken Access Control vulnerability

desc: A flaw has been found in DataEase up to 2.10.27. Affected by this issue is the function StaticResourceServer.validateSvgContent of the file core/core-backend/src/main/java/io/dataease/visualization/server/StaticResourceServer.java of the component SVG Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.10.28 can resolve this issue. This patch is called 0709fe98d6608c3507daee3e92cf433e7ff61370. You should upgrade the affected component. The vendor confirms: "The reported tab/entity-based URL bypass is covered by our previously implemented SVG security hardening. The fix replaces the blacklist-based checks with namespace-aware element and attribute allowlists, restricts permitted references to document-local fragments, and applies a restrictive Content Security Policy to uploaded SVG responses."
title: DataEase SVG StaticResourceServer.java StaticResourceServer.validateSvgContent cross site scripting

desc: A security flaw has been discovered in TOTOLINK CA300-PoE 6.2c.884. This impacts the function setWiFiMultipleConfig of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi. Performing a manipulation of the argument Key1Str1 results in buffer overflow. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.
title: TOTOLINK CA300-PoE cstecgi.cgi setWiFiMultipleConfig buffer overflow

desc: Missing Authorization vulnerability in PluginUs.Net FOX woocommerce-currency-switcher allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects FOX: from n/a through 1.5.6.
title: WordPress FOX plugin <= 1.5.6 - Broken Access Control vulnerability

desc: Missing Authorization vulnerability in eLightUp Meta Box – WordPress Custom Fields Framework meta-box allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Meta Box – WordPress Custom Fields Framework: from n/a through 5.15.3.
products: elightup:meta box – wordpress custom fields framework
title: WordPress Meta Box – WordPress Custom Fields Framework plugin <= 5.15.3 - Broken Access Control vulnerability

desc: Missing Authorization vulnerability in ThemeGrill User Registration user-registration allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects User Registration: from n/a through 5.3.1.
title: WordPress User Registration plugin <= 5.3.1 - Broken Access Control vulnerability

desc: A vulnerability was detected in DataEase up to 2.10.27. Affected by this vulnerability is the function WhitelistUtils.endsWithAny of the file WhitelistUtils.java of the component Authentication Filter. Performing a manipulation of the argument File results in unrestricted upload. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.10.28 addresses this issue. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component. The vendor confirms: "This issue has been addressed by enforcing authentication on the standalone static-resource upload endpoint independently of the URI suffix whitelist."
title: DataEase Authentication Filter WhitelistUtils.java WhitelistUtils.endsWithAny unrestricted upload

desc: A security vulnerability has been detected in DataEase up to 2.10.27/3.1.0. Affected is the function ExtWhere2Str.extWhere2sqlOjb of the file engine/trans/ExtWhere2Str.java of the component Chart Data Handler. Such manipulation of the argument operator leads to sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version 3.2.0 is able to address this issue. Upgrading the affected component is advised. The vendor confirms: "The fix validates the complete compound operator and uses fixed AND / OR keywords instead of concatenating user-controlled logic into SQL."
title: DataEase Chart Data ExtWhere2Str.java ExtWhere2Str.extWhere2sqlOjb sql injection

desc: libexpat through 2.10.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in unknown_toUtf8() and unknown_toUtf16() in xmltok.c when handling application-registered unknown encodings. Attackers can supply a document ending in a truncated multibyte sequence so the convert callback reads past the parse buffer, leaking adjacent memory or crashing applications.
title: libexpat through 2.10.0 Out-of-Bounds Read via unknown_toUtf8 and unknown_toUtf16

desc: Treeio through 2.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in UpdateRecord.get_format_strings and ModuleSetting.loads that allows staff users to execute code via unverified pickle data. Attackers can store a crafted base64 pickle payload in an UpdateRecord format_strings field through the Django admin, executing Python code as the web server user when news feeds render.
title: Treeio through 2.0 Insecure Deserialization RCE via Admin-Editable Pickle Fields

desc: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the whitelisted erpnext.buying.utils.get_linked_material_requests method lacking document or company permission checks. Authenticated users, including portal users or users without roles, can supply item codes to retrieve open Purchase-type Material Requests belonging to other companies.
title: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.36.0 Missing Authorization via get_linked_material_requests

desc: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the whitelisted get_bom_items and get_bom_diff methods that skip BOM read permission checks. Any authenticated user, including portal or no-role users, can call get_bom_items with a BOM name to retrieve every raw material, quantity, rate and cost.
title: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.36.0 Missing Authorization via get_bom_items

desc: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in erpnext.crm.utils.get_open_activities that exposes ToDo and Event records. Any authenticated user, including portal or no-role users, can supply arbitrary ref_doctype and ref_docname values to enumerate activities and private calendar event details.
title: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.36.0 Missing Authorization via get_open_activities

desc: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the whitelisted get_linked_payments_for_doc method. Any authenticated user, including portal users, can supply arbitrary company, doctype, and docname values to read Payment Ledger Entry allocation data for other companies' invoices and vouchers.
title: Frappe ERPNext before 15.121.4 and 16.36.0 Missing Authorization via get_linked_payments_for_doc

desc: Fraunhofer HHI VVdeC through 3.2.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the decoder by supplying a collocated picture of different resolution. Attackers can craft a VVC bitstream enabling TMVP with a smaller collocated reference picture, causing getColInfo to read past the colMotion allocation when error concealment is enabled.
title: Fraunhofer HHI VVdeC through 3.2.1 Heap Out-of-Bounds Read via CodingStructure::getColInfo

desc: A vulnerability was found in ESEngine DeepSeek-Reasonix up to 1.33.0. Impacted is the function loadGitStatus of the file build.rs of the component Build Script Execution. desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: limit sessions on each connection

The pending setup limit only counts InProgress sessions. A client can
complete authentication repeatedly and retain an unbounded number of Valid
sessions on one connection.

Reserve a connection slot before allocating a session and retain a
connection reference while authentication is in progress. The first SMB3
channel takes over that reservation; binding to another connection reserves
one slot there. Reauthentication and authentication continuation reuse the
existing reservation. Return slots on allocation or insertion failure,
channel removal, and final session destruction.

Accept max_sessions_per_connection in reserved startup-request space and
default to 64 when older tools leave it zero. Keep the request size and
existing field offsets unchanged. Expose the configured limit in procfs.
The existing connection limits bound the aggregate number of sessions
without a separate global session allocation limit.
title: ksmbd: limit sessions on each connection

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: reclaim ended sessions on logoff and expiration

LOGOFF and previous-session replacement leave sessions Expired with a
zero credential expiry. Ended sessions can retain their memory and
connection slots when no further setup arrives on the owning connection.

Unpublish a logged-off session while the request reference keeps its
response signing and encryption keys alive. Remove its procfs entry
before dropping the table reference so a reader cannot remove its own
entry on the last put. Clear proc_entry after removal to avoid removing
it twice.

Reclaim ended sessions from the global table in the existing expiration
worker before it acquires conn_list_lock. Only select Expired sessions
with zero credential expiry and no references beyond the table
reference. Keep sessions whose Kerberos credentials expired available
for reauthentication.

Unlink the session from its setup connection and all channel
connections, so SMB2 sessions and sessions with only secondary SMB3
channels are covered. The session already holds connection references,
and sessions_table_lock prevents concurrent channel removal. Queue
sessions on a separate disposal list, leaving their hash nodes unhashed,
and remove procfs entries and drop table references outside the locks.

Keep the pending setup check before allocating a new session so
abandoned InProgress sessions can release their slots even at the
connection limit. Retain the timeout and reference checks and dispose of
those sessions outside the locks. Leave ended Expired sessions to the
expiration worker.
title: ksmbd: reclaim ended sessions on logoff and expiration

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: drain session procfs readers before dropping table references

Session registration failure and connection cleanup can drop the table
reference while the per-session procfs entry is still accessible. If a
reader holds the last remaining reference, its final put calls
proc_remove() from its own callback and waits for that callback to
finish.

Remove the procfs entry before dropping the table reference in the
registration failure path. Queue sessions removed during connection
cleanup and drain their procfs readers after releasing both session
locks, then return their table references. Keep the global hash node
unhashed while a session is queued so a concurrent unregister cannot
drop the reference again.

Previous-session replacement also destroys the file table before the
session is finally freed. Detach the idr under the lock used by procfs
file counters, and report zero files after it has been detached. This
prevents a reader from accessing the idr during or after its
destruction.
title: ksmbd: drain session procfs readers before dropping table references

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: hold a connection reference for each session channel

ksmbd_session_unregister() removes a session from the global and per-
connection tables before dropping the table reference. A concurrent
reference holder can keep the session and its channel list alive after
those removals.

Connection cleanup can no longer find the unpublished session to remove its
channels. Since a channel only stores a raw conn pointer, the connection
can be freed while another session reference holder is still accessing it,
for example during SMB3.1.1 binding or a procfs read.

Take a connection reference when registering a channel and release it on
insertion failure, channel removal, or final session destruction. Keep the
channels and signing keys until the session is destroyed so a response can
still be signed after the session has been unregistered.
title: ksmbd: hold a connection reference for each session channel

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tun: Require CAP_NET_ADMIN to attach to an ownerless device

Twenty years ago I made creating a tuntap device require CAP_NET_ADMIN
in commit ca6bb5d7ab22 ("[NET]: Require CAP_NET_ADMIN to create tuntap
devices.")

The idea was to allow the permissions on /dev/net/tun to be relaxed to
0666 and thus allow owners of tun devices assigned with TUNSETOWNER to
actually open it and get at their devices.

What we missed at the time was that persistent devices with *no* owner
were already essentially world-consumable, and anyone who could open
the device node could also attach to those.

Even then, using persistent devices with no explicitly set owner — on
the (false) presumption that CAP_NET_ADMIN would be required to open
them — wasn't an egregious userspace bug. There are cases where it does
make sense to separate the creation/configuration of the netdevice, from
the process which shovels packets into it.

Since then, TUNSETGROUP was added a year later in commit 8c644623fe7e
("[NET]: Allow group ownership of TUN/TAP devices."). Its commit message
noted that if both uid and gid are set, both have to match (in itself a
bizarre choice) — but still not that with *neither* set, no permission
at all was required.

Then in 2012 commit c8d68e6be1c3 ("tuntap: multiqueue support") allowed
new queues to be attached to a device from the moment of its creation,
with no way for userspace to close the race between creation and a
subsequent TUNSET{OWNER,GROUP}.

In 2024, commit 3ca459eaba1bf ("tun: fix group permission check") tried
to fix things to be saner: only require the user *or* the group to
match, in line with standard POSIX permissions, and require
CAP_NET_ADMIN if neither the user nor group authorised the access
(although it put the CAP_NET_ADMIN check first, and would wrongly have
reported the capability as having been used even when it was not).

That fix was reverted in commit a70c7b3cbc06 ("tun: revert fix group
permission check") due to allegedly causing a regression in an selinux
test suite which *expected* the attachment to succeed when authorised
by none of user, group, nor CAP_NET_ADMIN:
https://lore.kernel.org/netdev/CAFqZXNtkCBT4f+PwyVRmQGoT3p1eVa01fCG_aNtpt6dakXncUg@mail.gmail.com/

We should not break UAPI. But we don't have to consider an selinux test
case which deliberately exercises a security flaw to be UAPI worth
preserving either. To which end, I have fixed it in selinux-testsuite
commit b2f894f0016b ("tests/tun_tap: set an owner on the device for the
relabel tests").

So: fix the lack of CAP_NET_ADMIN check on devices which *haven't* been
assigned an owner or group, while leaving the weird tun ownership model
as it was (user *and* group have to match, if both are set). If someone
still wants to fix the latter (which wasn't actually the reason the
previous attempt was reverted), they can do it under separate cover.

Permit attaching to an existing device only if an owner and/or group was
set and the caller matches all that were set, or if the caller has
CAP_NET_ADMIN. The only behavioural change is that a device with no
owner or group now requires CAP_NET_ADMIN to attach — precisely the
loophole we want to close.

And put the CAP_NET_ADMIN check in the right place this time.
title: tun: Require CAP_NET_ADMIN to attach to an ownerless device

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: sch_teql: fix use-after-free on lower qdisc drop

The issue: teql_master_xmit() tests the slave's ndo_start_xmit() return
value against NETDEV_TX_OK alone. A slave that consumes the skb but
returns an error code (rc < NET_XMIT_MASK, e.g. NET_XMIT_DROP) is treated
as if the skb were still owned, so the loop restores skb->dev and calls
__skb_pull() on it. A VLAN slave returns the result of dev_queue_xmit()
from its ndo_start_xmit() (propagated since cbbef5e18307), and when the
lower qdisc drops the packet that value is NET_XMIT_DROP after the skb
has been freed, giving a use-after-free in teql_master_xmit().

The Fix: test for consumption with dev_xmit_complete(), which accepts
NETDEV_TX_OK and every rc < NET_XMIT_MASK, matching other callers that
need to distinguish consumed results from busy. Only NETDEV_TX_OK keeps
the packet counted in tx_packets/tx_bytes and advances the slave; a
consumed result that is neither a success nor NET_XMIT_CN ends the
attempt and is charged to tx_dropped, so lower-qdisc drops are no longer
reported as good transmits. NET_XMIT_CN is counted like success because
it can accompany acceptance of the current packet: pfifo_head_drop drops
the old head, enqueues the current skb and returns NET_XMIT_CN.

Conditions to recreate the bug:
With CONFIG_NET_SCH_TEQL,
CONFIG_VLAN_8021Q and CONFIG_DUMMY enabled, add lkrdummy0 (dummy) and
lkrvlan0 (VLAN id 37 on lkrdummy0); set a pfifo limit 0 root on lkrdummy0
and a teql0 root on lkrvlan0; bring teql0 up with an address and send one
UDP packet to it. The VLAN xmit returns NET_XMIT_DROP from the lower
qdisc while holding a freed skb.
title: net/sched: sch_teql: fix use-after-free on lower qdisc drop

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: validate the data area in SMB2_read()

SMB2_read() copies le32_to_cpu(rsp->DataLength) bytes from
(char *)rsp + rsp->DataOffset without checking that the range lies
within the response actually received. A READ response with
DataOffset == 0 makes smb2_get_data_area_len() zero the data length, so
smb2_check_message() accepts a frame as short as the fixed response,
while SMB2_read() still uses the server-supplied DataLength, capped only
by CIFS_MAX_MSGSIZE and the caller's length.

A malicious server can answer the synchronous read used by the
mfsymlinks (or SFU) symlink parser with an 81-byte READ response
carrying DataOffset 0 and DataLength 1067, making the client copy 1067
bytes from a 448-byte receive object (KASAN slab-out-of-bounds; up to
16 KiB in the general case).

Clamp a zero (or header-overlapping) DataOffset to read_rsp_size, as
handle_read_data() does for the asynchronous path, and reject the
response unless DataOffset + DataLength fits within rsp_iov.iov_len.
The SMB1 helper was fixed the same way in 5be5bdda5863.
title: smb: client: validate the data area in SMB2_read()

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: reject short SESSION_SETUP responses

smb2_check_message() accepts frames shorter than struct smb2_pdu when
the SMB2 status is non-zero, before the minimum-PDU check added by
b4694f269e66d. A 64-byte STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED SESSION_SETUP
response is therefore accepted even though it cannot contain the
SecurityBufferOffset and SecurityBufferLength fields.

The parser then reads those fields from stale bytes left in the reused
receive buffer by an earlier frame. With a long stale
SecurityBufferLength, decode_ntlmssp_challenge() copies up to about
64 KB from beyond the receive object and sends the data back to the
server in the NTLMv2 AUTHENTICATE target info.

Reject short MPR SESSION_SETUP responses before the short-error path,
and validate SecurityBufferOffset + SecurityBufferLength against the
received response length before decoding the challenge.

The ordering bypass is not new: the short-error early return predates
b4694f269e66d, and the unvalidated SecurityBufferLength read predates
the 2016 raw NTLMSSP split in 166cea4dc3a4, so all supported stable
trees are affected. Reproduced on 6.6.87.2; the path is unchanged on
mainline.
title: smb: client: reject short SESSION_SETUP responses

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: defer connection scavenging while session locks are busy

The expiration worker holds conn_list_lock for reading while checking
for authenticated sessions. Without this change, the check can wait for
conn->session_lock or sessions_table_lock.

In destroy_previous_session(), the status updates after
ksmbd_conn_wait_idle_sess() run with both session locks held for
writing. Both the KSMBD_SESS_GOOD error path and the
KSMBD_SESS_NEED_SETUP success path call ksmbd_all_conn_set_status(),
which takes conn_list_lock for reading.

A writer queued on conn_list_lock can block these new read acquisitions.
The worker then waits for a session lock held by
destroy_previous_session(), which waits behind the writer. The writer
cannot proceed until the worker releases conn_list_lock.

Try both session locks instead of waiting in the scavenging check. Keep
the connection when either lock is busy and let the periodic worker
retry later.
title: ksmbd: defer connection scavenging while session locks are busy

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: line6: Clear prev_fbuf on capture buffer release

A KASAN slab-use-after-free read was reported in submit_audio_out_urb()
when generating an impulse test signal:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in create_impulse_test_signal sound/usb/line6/playback.c:76 [inline]
  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in submit_audio_out_urb+0x1848/0x1b20 sound/usb/line6/playback.c:249
  Read of size 2 at addr ffff888008d74870 by task syz.2.3214/7785

  Allocated by task 11:
   kmem_cache_alloc_noprof+0x2f0/0x390 mm/slub.c:4144
   line6_buffer_acquire+0x1a1/0x220 sound/usb/line6/pcm.c:158
   line6_pcm_acquire+0xb6/0x230 sound/usb/line6/pcm.c:329
   line6_startup_work+0x3c/0x50 sound/usb/line6/driver.c:728

  Freed by task 7785:
   kfree+0xf8/0x390 mm/slub.c:6566
   line6_buffer_release sound/usb/line6/pcm.c:176 [inline]
   line6_buffer_release+0xa5/0xf0 sound/usb/line6/pcm.c:170
   __line6_pcm_release sound/usb/line6/pcm.c:305 [inline]
   line6_pcm_release+0x5a/0x80 sound/usb/line6/pcm.c:313
   snd_toneport_monitor_put+0x11b/0x190 sound/usb/line6/toneport.c:183

line6pcm->prev_fbuf points into the capture PCM stream buffer
(line6pcm->in.buffer), which is updated during audio_in_callback() to
feed rate synchronization, software monitoring, and impulse test signal
generation on playback side.

When all capture streams are closed, line6_buffer_release() frees
pstr->buffer with kfree().  However, it does not clear line6pcm->prev_fbuf.
If playback is subsequently started (e.g. via impulse test signal
volume control snd_line6_impulse_volume_put()), submit_audio_out_urb()
dereferences the stale pointer line6pcm->prev_fbuf under in.lock,
resulting in a slab-use-after-free read.

Clear prev_fbuf and prev_fsize in line6_buffer_release() when releasing
the capture stream buffer under in.lock, ensuring that no stale buffer
pointer can be accessed by submit_audio_out_urb().
title: ALSA: line6: Clear prev_fbuf on capture buffer release

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: reserve space for the UTF-16 terminator in stream info

smb_strtoUTF16() always writes a terminating zero UTF-16 unit after the
converted characters, but get_file_stream_info() budgets only
sizeof(struct smb2_file_stream_info) + streamlen * 2 for a stream entry
and sizeof(struct smb2_file_stream_info) + 7 * 2 for the trailing
"::$DATA" entry. When an entry exactly fills the 448-byte small response
buffer, the terminator is written two bytes past the allocation.

Reserve one extra UTF-16 unit in both budget checks. The terminator is
not part of the wire format, so the reported lengths are unchanged.
title: ksmbd: reserve space for the UTF-16 terminator in stream info

desc:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix fiemap wild read on empty truncated response

smb3_fiemap() treats -E2BIG from SMB2_ioctl() as a truncated range blob
and loops for the next chunk. If the server reports
STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW with OutputCount == 0, SMB2_ioctl() returns
-E2BIG with out_data == NULL and out_data_len == 0, and the existing
length checks accept the empty result. The loop then evaluates

	next = out_data[num - 1].file_offset + ...

with num == 0, reading 16 bytes before NULL.

Reject a truncated range blob that contains no range, so the resume
offset is never computed from an empty response. Also require the last
range in a truncated blob to advance the resume offset without
overflowing, and to stay within the requested range; a malicious or
broken server could otherwise make no progress or underflow len and loop
forever. Free the previous response buffer before retrying.

Reproduced on 6.6.87.2 with a malicious SMB2 server that answers
FSCTL_QUERY_ALLOCATED_RANGES with STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW and
OutputCount == 0; an FS_IOC_FIEMAP ioctl on the mount oopses in
cifs_fiemap() with CR2 = fffffffffffffff8. The code path is unchanged
on mainline.
title: smb: client: fix fiemap wild read on empty truncated response

desc:
RRD::CGI::Image versions through 0.01 for Perl pass CGI query parameters containting "tz" to tzset(), , so a FIFO or device path blocks the CGI process.

The normalize_params method sends any query key matching /tz/i to tz(), which sets $ENV{TZ} to that value, with no validation. It then calls tzset(). glibc treats a TZ value starting with / or : as a file path and opens it, so a value naming a FIFO or a blocking device stalls the process inside tzset().

desc:
SQL::Abstract versions before 2.000003 for Perl allow SQL injection via an arrayref column value in insert and update.

With the array_datatypes option off, which is the default, insert(), update() and values() treat an arrayref column value as literal SQL. Its first element goes into the SQL text unescaped and the rest become bind values. A JSON array, or a repeated form field decoded as an arrayref, is such a value.

An application that passes request data as column values to insert or update with the default options allows SQL injection.

Releases before 2.000003 also treat an arrayref in generate() as literal SQL, including through AUTOLOAD when allow_autoload is on, whatever array_datatypes is set to.
title: SQL::Abstract versions before 2.000003 for Perl allow SQL injection via an arrayref column value in insert and update

desc: The Appointment Booking Plugin – LatePoint | Calendar & Scheduling for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.6. The attacker can first identify the target customer's email by sending `params[order_intent_key]=IS NOT NULL` to the public `steps__start_from_order_intent` route, which returns the name and email from the first matching order intent, and can then self-arm the required 15-minute password-reset freshness window by triggering a reset for that customer directly.

desc: The AutomatorWP – No-Code Workflow Automation, Integration & Webhooks Plugin, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 6.0.4. desc: The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.2 via the `data[secondary_groupids]` parameter of the `wpforo_action_profile_update` POST handler. This is due to a type-confusion flaw in the secondary_groupids authorization guard within the `Members::update()` function in `classes/Members.php`, where casting a scalar CSV string (e.g. `"0,1"`) with `(array)` before `array_map('intval', …)` and `array_filter()` produces an empty array — causing the guard's outer conditional, and the else-branch that would otherwise strip the field from the update, to be bypassed entirely — while `encode()`/`decode()` downstream correctly explodes the original CSV and persists the attacker-supplied group IDs to `wp_wpforo_profiles.secondary_groupids`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to escalate their forum privileges to wpForo Administrator by injecting the privileged Admin group ID, granting access to the Forum Accesses editor and the ability to rewrite forum-wide capability policies for all members and edit arbitrary content owned by other users. Exploitation requires the attacker to have at least 3 approved wpForo posts to satisfy the plugin's default `min_number_posts_to_edit_account` antispam gate, along with a valid wpforo nonce obtained from their own account profile form.
title: wpForo Forum <= 3.2.2 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation to 'data[secondary_groupids]' CSV Parameter

desc: The WPSpeed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 2.6.10 This is due to a combination of two issues in the LightImages HTML optimizer: (1) Dispatcher::runOptimize() decides whether the current request is the site's home page by comparing only the URL path from REQUEST_URI against the path of the home URL, so on a plain-permalinks install the author archive URL /?author=<ID> is treated as the home page and the LightImages optimizer runs on it; and (2) LightImages::optimize() calls html_entity_decode() across the entire serialized DOMDocument output under the default-enabled img_processing_entity_decode setting, converting any entity-encoded markup present as plain text in the page (including WordPress's rendered author title) into live HTML. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to store entity-encoded markup in their own nickname/display_name through the normal profile endpoint and have that markup rehydrated into executing script when any logged-out visitor loads their author archive.

desc: The Advanced Form Integration — Connect Forms to 300+ Apps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.2 via deserialization of untrusted input . This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present. Exploitation requires that an administrator has previously configured at least one active NexForms integration (status=1) in the plugin's database table; in the free tier, only POST parameter keys containing the substrings 'name', 'email', 'first', or 'last' are routed to the vulnerable normalizer.
products: nasirahmed:advanced form integration — connect forms to 300+ apps
title: Advanced Form Integration <= 2.10.2 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection via $_POST Parameters

desc: A vulnerability was found in OpenBMB Internet of Agents up to 9d78e88e47160eb42ee1ee8538c05e1c2c47877a. This issue affects the function fetch_chat_record of the file im_server/app.py of the component Message Handler. The manipulation of the argument comm_id results in improper access controls. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.
title: OpenBMB Internet of Agents Message app.py fetch_chat_record access control

desc: The QA Assistants – Driven by data plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.0 via the 'dlevent_ver' parameter. This is due to unrestricted PHP deserialization via wrap_unserialize_static() calling unserialize() without an allowed_classes restriction, combined with serialize_escape() failing to sanitize path traversal sequences in the raw_name parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object. The Guzzle FileCookieJar gadget present in the plugin's bundled Composer dependencies can be leveraged to perform an Arbitrary File Write, writing attacker-controlled content to an attacker-chosen filename, which can result in Remote Code Execution. Exploitation requires triggering the qahm_cron_data_manage scheduled event via wp-cron.php to invoke the deserialization sink against a planted queue file, but this endpoint requires no authentication and fires automatically on a two-minute schedule.
title: QA Assistants <= 5.3.0 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection to Remote Code Execution via 'raw_name' and 'dlevent_ver' Parameters

desc: The Paystack WooCommerce Payment Gateway plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 5.8.5 via the 'key' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract customer PII — including billing name, email address, phone number, billing address, shipping address, and purchased product list — embedded into page HTML via wp_localize_script by enumerating sequential order IDs. This is only exploitable when the merchant has enabled the optional custom metadata feature in the Paystack gateway settings.
title: Paystack WooCommerce Payment Gateway <= 5.8.5 - Unauthenticated Sensitive Information Exposure in 'key' Parameter on order-pay Endpoint

desc: A flaw was found in the Trainer v2 TrainJob API. A user with permissions to create TrainJobs can exploit this by injecting `valueFrom.secretKeyRef` into environment variable definitions. This allows them to read and exfiltrate sensitive information (secrets) from the namespace, leading to a privilege escalation. This occurs when the TrainJob Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is broader than the Secret read RBAC.
title: Trainer: trainer: trainjob env passthrough enables valuefrom.secretkeyref injection for namespace secret exfiltration

desc: The TranslatePress – Translate Multilingual sites with AI Translation plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (storage); originals / language / original_language (exfiltration from endpoint)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
products: cozmoslabs:translatepress – translate multilingual sites with ai translation
title: TranslatePress <= 3.3.8 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Attribute via trp-ajax.php Dictionary Endpoint

desc: The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'engine' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.90 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. This is only exploitable when an administrator has configured a Data Project page to admit a lower-privileged role, which is the plugin's documented mechanism for sharing projects with subscribers and other users.
products: peterschulznl:wp data access – app builder for tables, forms, dashboards, charts & maps
title: WP Data Access <= 5.5.90 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) SQL Injection via 'engine' Parameter

desc: The GamiPress – Gamification plugin to reward points, badges & ranks in WordPress, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'input_<field_id>.<part> (Gravity Forms name-field part, or list-field row)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.1 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires a GamiPress achievement already configured against a Gravity Forms 'field value submission' event with the corresponding form published — a standard setup for sites using the integration.
products: rubengc:gamipress – gamification plugin to reward points, badges & ranks in wordpress, now with ai
title: GamiPress <= 8.1.1 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) SQL Injection via 'Gravity Forms Name/List Field' Parameter

desc: The Vanquish Upload Files for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.13 via the 'vanupfi_file_name' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The authorization bypass is achieved by supplying a non-existent order ID (e.g., '.pdf'), which causes wc_get_order() to return false and short-circuits the vanupfi_user_can_access_order_files() check, while the is_pdf() branch selector's loose strpos() substring match allows a traversal payload such as '../.pdf/../../../../wp-config.php' to satisfy the PDF branch and be streamed verbatim via readfile().
title: Vanquish Upload Files for WooCommerce <= 2.7.13 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Read via 'vanupfi_file_name' Parameter

desc: The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'ImageURL column value (populated from wp_usermeta.description in the demonstrated path)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.89 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires an administrator to have published a DataTables shortcode over a database column the attacker controls (e.g., wp_usermeta.description) with the Image URL media type assigned to that column — both are supported plugin features but are not enabled by default.
products: peterschulznl:wp data access – app builder for tables, forms, dashboards, charts & maps
title: WP Data Access <= 5.5.89 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'Image URL' Media-Type Column Renderer

desc: The aBlocks – Gutenberg Blocks, User Dashboard Builder, Popup Builder, Form Builder & Animation Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'headingTag' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
products: kodezen:ablocks – gutenberg blocks, user dashboard builder, popup builder, form builder & animation builder
title: aBlocks <= 2.18.0 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'headingTag' Block Attribute

desc: The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the Data Projects front-end simple form in versions up to, and including, 5.5.90 This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on the value of TEXT/TINYTEXT/MEDIUMTEXT/LONGTEXT columns rendered by the WPDA_Simple_Form_Item_Textarea::show_item() method, which emits the stored column value directly inside a <textarea> element after only replacing '&' with '&'. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
products: peterschulznl:wp data access – app builder for tables, forms, dashboards, charts & maps
title: WP Data Access <= 5.5.90 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via TEXT-family Column Value in Front-end Data Project Form

desc: The SEOPress – AI SEO Plugin & On-site SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'seopress_google_analytics_affiliate_tracking' and 'seopress_google_analytics_download_tracking' settings in versions up to, and including, 10.3. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on these settings as they are interpolated into the inline Google Analytics tracking snippet by seopress_google_analytics_js(): the affiliate value receives no sanitization at all (it is omitted from inc/admin/sanitize/Sanitize.php) and lands inside a <script> block, while the download value is only passed through sanitize_text_field() and lands inside a JavaScript regular-expression literal that preserves parentheses, semicolons and slashes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above (where an administrator has delegated the SEOPress 'analytics' capability under Settings > Advanced > Security — the precondition Wordfence accepted for CVE-2026-101357), to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
products: rainbowgeek:seopress – ai seo plugin & on-site seo
title: SEOPress <= 10.3 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'seopress_google_analytics_affiliate_tracking' and 'seopress_google_analytics_download_tracking' Parameters

desc: The aBlocks – Gutenberg Blocks, User Dashboard Builder, Popup Builder, Form Builder & Animation Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 2.18.0 via the 'id' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to extract the full rendered body content of any password-protected post of any post type by embedding the shortcode with the target post's ID. Author-level attackers and above can additionally publish a post embedding the shortcode, exposing the password-protected content to unauthenticated visitors.
products: kodezen:ablocks – gutenberg blocks, user dashboard builder, popup builder, form builder & animation builder
title: aBlocks <= 2.18.0 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Sensitive Information Exposure in 'ablocks_template' Shortcode

desc: The WebToffee WP Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.1 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to subsequently perform the plugin's ordinary local database export and restore operation on the same site, which is this plugin's primary intended function. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
title: WebToffee WP Backup and Migration <= 1.6.1 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) SQL Injection via User Profile Biography

desc: The Strong Testimonials plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'star_rating' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.16 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution requires an administrator to open the standard Preview link for a pending testimonial, a step the plugin's normal moderation workflow naturally invites.
title: Strong Testimonials <= 3.3.16 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'star_rating' Parameter

desc: The Unlimited Elements for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<title>/<description> inside the attacker-controlled RSS feed body' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.26 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable against any site whose administrator has placed the RSS Feed catalog widget pointing at a feed URL the attacker controls, as the plugin's own 2.0.25 escaping pre-processor intentionally excludes |raw prints in element content positions from its escaping logic, and XML entity-encoded payloads in feed item titles are decoded back to raw markup before reaching the sink.
title: Unlimited Elements for Elementor <= 2.0.26 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via RSS Feed Widget

desc: The Ultimate Member – User Profile, Registration, Login, Member Directory, Content Restriction & Membership Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'pm_note (any custom Textarea metakey with html disabled)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.14.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a privileged victim to click the attacker-rendered anchor on the target profile page, which triggers the DOM gadget that concatenates the unescaped data-src value into an HTML string passed to jQuery.
products: ultimatemember:ultimate member – user profile, registration, login, member directory, content restriction & membership plugin
title: Ultimate Member <= 2.14.1 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Custom Textarea Profile Field

desc: The WP Data Access plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the Simple Form autocomplete lookup label in versions up to, and including, 5.5.89 This is due to insufficient output escaping on the value returned by WPDA_Autocomplete::autocomplete_lookup() when it is emitted into a single-quoted HTML attribute by WPDA_Simple_Form_Item_Autocomplete::show_item() (the escape-output lint is explicitly suppressed on the echo line). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, who are permitted to edit a lookup row through a legacy Form, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user — including a higher-privileged user editing a linked record that uses the autocomplete relationship — accesses the injected page.
products: peterschulznl:wp data access – app builder for tables, forms, dashboards, charts & maps
title: WP Data Access <= 5.5.89 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Autocomplete Lookup Label

desc: The The Quiz and Survey Master (QSM) – Quiz Maker & Survey Maker plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary shortcode execution in all versions up to, and including, 11.2.7. This is due to the software allowing users to execute an action that does not properly validate a value before running do_shortcode. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary shortcodes. The submission nonce is dispensed to any unauthenticated caller by the public wp_ajax_nopriv_qsm_create_quiz_nonce endpoint, meaning it functions as a CSRF token rather than an authorization barrier and imposes no meaningful obstacle to exploitation.
products: expresstech:quiz and survey master (qsm) – quiz maker & survey maker
title: Quiz and Survey Master (QSM) <= 11.2.7 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Shortcode Execution via 'qsm_unique_key' Parameter

desc: The Komfortkasse for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 1.4.9 does not properly validate the authenticity of REST API requests, overriding WordPress's own nonce verification so that a request forged in a logged-in administrator's browser is accepted, which can be used to create a new administrator account and fully take over the site.
title: Komfortkasse for WooCommerce < 1.4.9 - Administrator Account Creation via CSRF

desc: The Advanced Custom Fields (ACF®) WordPress plugin before 6.8.11 does not perform a read-permission check when it renders and formats the values of its relational fields, allowing users with post-editing access (Contributor and above) to disclose the titles and non-public statuses of other users' unpublished posts.
title: Advanced Custom Fields < 6.8.11 - Contributor+ Unpublished Post Title and Status Disclosure via Relational Fields

desc: The Advanced Custom Fields (ACF®) WordPress plugin before 6.8.11 does not verify that a user is allowed to edit the target object before writing to it during bidirectional relationship synchronization, allowing users with contributor-level access and above to add or remove a reference to their own object on arbitrary posts, users, or terms they cannot otherwise edit.
title: Advanced Custom Fields 6.2.0 - 6.8.10 - Contributor+ Relationship Field Update on Arbitrary Objects via IDOR

desc: The Advanced Custom Fields (ACF®) WordPress plugin before 6.8.11 does not re-apply its field-group location rules when persisting values submitted through the post editor save path, allowing users with contributor-level access and above to write custom fields the site restricted to administrators onto their own posts.
title: Advanced Custom Fields < 6.8.11 - Contributor+ Admin-Restricted Custom Field Update via Post Save Path

desc: The Tournamatch WordPress plugin before 4.7.1 does not validate or restrict the path of a previously stored profile or team image before deleting it when a new image is uploaded, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to delete arbitrary files on the server, such as wp-config.php, which can lead to a full site takeover.
title: Tournamatch < 4.7.1 - Subscriber+ Arbitrary File Deletion

desc: The Tournamatch WordPress plugin before 4.7.1 does not restrict access to its team invitation listing, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve the email addresses of people invited to join teams.
title: Tournamatch < 4.7.1 - Unauthenticated Team Invitation Email Disclosure via REST API

desc: The Fiber Admin WordPress plugin before 4.0.1 does not validate or escape a request header before writing it into a PHP file it regenerates on an unprotected admin hook, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code when its custom database error page is enabled and they win a race against an administrator saving its settings.
title: Fiber Admin 3.1.0 - 4.0.0 - Unauthenticated RCE via Host Header

desc: The Fiber Admin WordPress plugin before 4.0.1 does not have authorisation checks in some of its AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to change the order of arbitrary posts, including drafts, private posts and navigation menu items, as well as the order of taxonomy terms when term ordering is enabled.
title: Fiber Admin < 4.0.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Post and Term Order Modification via fiad_cpo_update and fiad_cpo_tax_update

desc: The Add From Server Lite WordPress plugin before 6.0.0 does not restrict SVG uploads to users allowed to post unfiltered HTML, allowing users with the Author role and above to upload SVG files containing JavaScript and perform Stored XSS attacks.
title: Add From Server Reloaded < 6.0.0 - Author+ Stored XSS via SVG Upload

desc: The Magic Link  WordPress plugin before 2.2.6 does not check that the user requesting a login link is authorised to generate one for the chosen account, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to generate a working login link for an administrator and log in as them.
title: Magic Link < 2.2.6 - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation via Magic Link Generation

desc: The Event Tickets with Ticket Scanner WordPress plugin before 3.1.14 does not check that a user may manage WooCommerce orders before returning or removing ticket data for any order, allowing any role an administrator has granted access to the Event Tickets with Ticket Scanner WordPress plugin before 3.1.14's admin area (down to Subscriber) to view other customers' ticket codes and names and to remove tickets from their orders.
title: Event Tickets with Ticket Scanner < 3.1.14 - Authenticated Ticket Data Disclosure and Removal via executeWCBackend

desc: The Event Tickets with Ticket Scanner WordPress plugin before 3.2.9 does not properly escape a search value before using it in SQL queries in several of its admin listings, allowing users with access to its admin area (administrators by default, or any role granted access in its settings) to perform SQL injection attacks.
title: Event Tickets with Ticket Scanner < 3.2.9 - Authenticated SQLi via DataTables Search

desc: The iLeads SMS Gateway by Exsile WordPress plugin before 2.0.0 does not check capabilities or nonces in several AJAX actions that update a site option chosen by the request, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to change arbitrary WordPress options and escalate to administrator, for example by enabling registration with administrator as the default role.
title: Exsile SMS Gateway < 2.0.0 - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation via Arbitrary Option Update

desc: The WP Google Review Slider WordPress plugin before 18.11 does not perform nonce validation when updating its active Google Places configuration, allowing attackers to alter or destroy that configuration via a forged request, provided they can trick a site administrator into following a crafted link.
title: WP Google Review Slider < 18.11 - Google API Settings Update via CSRF

desc: The Directorist: AI-Powered Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads WordPress plugin before 8.11 does not validate that the requesting user owns the referenced listing before returning its metadata via an AJAX action, allowing authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to disclose another user's private and unpublished draft listing details, including contact information.
products: unknown:directorist: ai-powered business directory, listings & classified ads
title: Directorist < 8.11 - Subscriber+ Draft Listing Contact Information Disclosure via IDOR

desc: The Directorist: AI-Powered Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads WordPress plugin before 8.11 does not verify that a user owns a listing before processing a featured-listing checkout for it, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to publish and feature another user's pending listing when the featured listing fee is set to zero.
products: unknown:directorist: ai-powered business directory, listings & classified ads
title: Directorist < 8.11 - Subscriber+ Other Users' Pending Listing Publication via Featured Listing Checkout

desc: The Directorist: AI-Powered Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads WordPress plugin before 8.11 does not check that the acting user may edit each targeted user when handling an email-verification bulk action on multisite, allowing an Administrator of one site on the network to lock out users of other sites, including the network Super Administrator, until they re-verify their email.
products: unknown:directorist: ai-powered business directory, listings & classified ads
title: Directorist < 8.11 - Admin+ Cross-Site Account Lockout via Email Verification Bulk Action

desc: The Directorist: AI-Powered Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads WordPress plugin before 8.11 does not verify ownership of attachment IDs supplied when updating a listing's images, allowing authenticated users with Subscriber-level access and above to permanently delete arbitrary media library attachments, including those uploaded by administrators, along with their files.

title: Directorist < 8.11 - Subscriber+ Arbitrary Media Deletion via Listing Image Field

desc: The Directorist: AI-Powered Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads WordPress plugin before 8.11 does not verify that the user requesting an order's payment receipt owns that order, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to disclose other users' order and payment information, including amounts, payment method, payment status and transaction ID.
products: unknown:directorist: ai-powered business directory, listings & classified ads
title: Directorist < 8.11 - Subscriber+ Order and Payment Information Disclosure via Payment Receipt

desc: The Directorist: AI-Powered Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads WordPress plugin before 8.11 does not verify that the order targeted by its checkout payment-retry REST action belongs to the requesting user, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to create payment-attempt records against other users' orders.
products: unknown:directorist: ai-powered business directory, listings & classified ads
title: Directorist < 8.11 - Subscriber+ Payment Retry on Other Users' Orders via IDOR

desc: The Live Composer  WordPress plugin before 2.1.23 does not escape a pagination setting supplied through its post-listing module shortcodes before outputting it in an HTML attribute, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.
title: Live Composer < 2.1.23 - Contributor+ Stored XSS via Post Module Pagination

desc: The Live Composer  WordPress plugin before 2.1.23 does not sanitise and escape some of its custom post type slug settings before using them in front-end links, which could allow high privilege users such as admin to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks even when the unfiltered_html capability is disallowed (for example in a multisite setup).
desc_es: El plugin de WordPress Live Composer anterior a la versión 2.1.23 no sanea ni escapa algunas de las configuraciones de slug de sus tipos de publicación personalizados antes de usarlas en enlaces de interfaz, lo que podría permitir a usuarios con altos privilegios, como los administradores, realizar ataques de Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Almacenado incluso cuando la capacidad ’unfiltered_html’ está deshabilitada (por ejemplo, en una configuración multisitio).
title: Live Composer < 2.1.23 - Admin+ Stored XSS via Partner Slug

desc: The FV Flowplayer Video Player WordPress plugin before 7.5.57.7212 does not escape shortcode attribute values embedded in comments before rendering them into the media player markup, allowing an unauthenticated visitor to store a script payload in a comment that executes in the session of any visitor, including an administrator, who plays the commented video, when the non-default comment-shortcode-parsing setting is enabled.
title: FV Player < 7.5.57.7212 - Unauthenticated Stored XSS via Comment Popup

desc: The Soledad theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Social Profile Fields in all versions up to, and including, 8.7.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is scoped to the attacker's own user meta but is exposed publicly on their author archive page at /author/<slug>/, which is accessible to unauthenticated visitors regardless of whether the attacker has published any posts.
title: Soledad <= 8.7.7 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Social Profile Fields

desc: The Stackable – Page Builder Gutenberg Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'update_block_style' endpoint in all versions up to, and including, 3.19.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
title: Stackable <= 3.19.9 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'save' Parameter

desc: The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 4.1.2 via the init_routes due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to read paid course lesson and topic content without enrollment, retrieve quiz answer keys including the is_correct field before attempting a quiz, and enumerate the email addresses, usernames, and registration data of other users including instructors and administrators. Exploitation requires that the attacker hold a valid Tutor LMS API key/secret pair, which is issued to subscriber-level users through the plugin's API key management feature.
products: themeum:tutor lms – elearning and online course solution
title: Tutor LMS <= 4.1.2 - Insecure Direct Object Reference to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Sensitive Information Exposure via REST API Endpoints

desc: The Stop Spammers Classic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' POST parameter in versions up to, and including, 2026.6. An unauthenticated POST handled on init stores the attacker-supplied author field (after sanitize_text_field, which does not escape single quotes) into the ss_stop_sp_reg_stats option history. The Log Report admin page then renders that stored value inside a single-quoted JavaScript string within a double-quoted onclick attribute using esc_js(); because esc_js() uses _wp_specialchars with ENT_COMPAT it does not escape single quotes, allowing the stored value to break out of the JS string literal and inject arbitrary JavaScript. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute whenever an administrator with manage_options access clicks the 'Report to SFS' link on an attacker-poisoned log row (the StopForumSpam API key must be configured for that link to be rendered — the field is empty by default). Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the attacker's review containing the payload to be approved, either automatically (due to a previously approved review from the same account) or manually by an administrator, and the active single-product template must use a Kubio-rendered wp:post-content block.
title: Kubio AI Page Builder <= 2.9.4 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via kubio/shortcode Block via Product Review

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the Free Listing Submission feature to be enabled, which is shipped on by default via the Setup Wizard demo configuration.

desc: FileGator is a multi-user file manager. Prior to 7.15.0, GET /batchdownload in backend/Controllers/DownloadController.php uses batchDownloadStart() to stream a shared temporary archive selected by the request-supplied uniqid without checking that the current session created it. In deployments with distinct per-user home directories, a valid user with read, download, and batchdownload permissions who obtains another user's active archive id can cross that boundary and retrieve the victim's batch archive. The archive lifetime and id-acquisition requirement limit exploitation, but a successful replay also deletes the victim's pending archive. This issue is fixed in version 7.15.0.
title: FileGator: Missing authorization in GET /batchdownload allows cross-user retrieval of another user's archive

desc: FileGator is a multi-user file manager. Prior to 7.15.0, POST /upload in backend/Controllers/UploadController.php uses the request-supplied resumableFilename as an unnamespaced key in shared temporary storage. In a multi-user deployment configured with distinct per-user home directories, a low-privileged user with upload permission can set resumableTotalChunks and resumableTotalSize to zero so the assembly loop writes no data, after which the handler reads a pre-existing temporary file with that name, stores it in the attacker's home directory, and removes it. The same filename path can append data when chunks are supplied, allowing disclosure, modification, or deletion of another user's transient object, including a pending archive or the login rate-limit lockfile, while Tmpfs path sanitization limits the primitive to the temporary directory. This issue is fixed in version 7.15.0.
title: FileGator: Missing authorization in POST /upload allows cross-user read and deletion of temporary files

desc: Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databases and APIs and use the data to create charts. Prior to 5.2.3, public dashboard passwords were stored in plaintext, accepted through a URL query parameter, and checked without effective attempt throttling. The vulnerable surface is public password-protected dashboard storage and validation routes. An unauthenticated attacker targets a public password-protected dashboard and repeatedly submits candidate passwords or obtains password-bearing server or proxy logs. Unlimited online guesses enable brute force, while cleartext storage and URL transport expose the secret in application storage and server or proxy access logs. The target must be a public dashboard with password protection enabled. Even failed attempts reveal chart count and configuration without the password; a recovered password grants access to the protected dashboard and its chart data. This vulnerability is fixed in 5.2.3.
title: Chartbrew: Unauthenticated Brute Force of Password-Protected Dashboards Due to Missing Rate Limit and Plaintext Password Storage

desc: Chartbrew is an open-source web application that can connect directly to databases and APIs and use the data to create charts. In 5.2.2, the AI SQL blocklist omitted sibling PostgreSQL filesystem functions and failed to match double-quoted identifier forms of denied functions. The vulnerable surface is the AI query tool's PostgreSQL SQL-validation blocklist. A team Owner or Admin uses an AI-enabled PostgreSQL connection whose database role can call server-side file functions and causes generated SQL to use an unlisted sibling function or a double-quoted denied function. Unlisted sibling functions remain allowed, and double-quoted function identifiers bypass the denylist regular expressions and reach PostgreSQL. AI features must be enabled and the user must have elevated Chartbrew privileges. A PostgreSQL superuser or pg_read_server_files role can resolve absolute paths to files readable by the PostgreSQL OS user, while a non-superuser is limited to the source-stated PGDATA-relative scope. This vulnerability is fixed in 5.2.3.
title: Chartbrew: AI orchestrator run_query SQL blocklist bypass enables arbitrary file read on connected PostgreSQL (quoted-identifier + pg_stat_file/pg_ls_* sibling gap)

desc: Chartbrew is an open-source web application for creating charts from databases and APIs. In versions 4.8.5 through 5.2.2, API connection creation and update operations accept the internal  allowPrivateHost  field from user input. An authenticated user with permission to manage API connections can enable this field to bypass private and reserved-network destination restrictions. An upgrade migration also enables the override on pre-existing API connections. The per-connection setting takes precedence over  CB_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK_CALLS , so disabling that instance option does not protect connections with the override enabled. Successful exploitation allows requests to internal HTTP services reachable from the Chartbrew server, potentially disclosing information or triggering unauthorized actions depending on the target service. Recognized cloud metadata endpoints remain separately blocked. This issue is fixed in version 5.2.3.
title: Chartbrew: SSRF to Internal Network via User-Controlled allowPrivateHost Flag on API Connections

desc: UgCS server before 6.2 contains an authentication bypass in the HCI protocol login handler (LoginHandler) exposed on TCP port 3334. When the user database contains exactly one user (the default single-operator installation), a LoginRequest with empty userLogin and userPassword fields is interpreted as \"use the only user\" rather than as invalid credentials, and the server returns a fully authenticated session. Because the service listens on all interfaces (0.0.0.0) without TLS by default, an unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to port 3334 can obtain an authenticated session without knowing any credential and then issue privileged commands, including commanding connected drones and uploading flight routes.
title: UgCS server HCI authentication bypass with empty credentials

desc: Ryot is a self-hosted personal tracking application. Prior to 10.4.0, the createOrUpdateUserIntegration GraphQL mutation in crates/services/user/src/integration_operations.rs allows a low-privileged authenticated user to supply another user's integrationId to create_or_update_user_integration() without an ownership check. SeaORM treats the supplied primary key as an update target, and the operation assigns the caller's user_id while replacing the targeted integration's provider_specifics and other configuration, which can transfer ownership, overwrite configuration, or disable the victim's integration. Exploitation requires obtaining the victim's non-brute-forceable integration id, and the vulnerable update does not disclose existing stored credential values. This issue is fixed in version 10.4.0.
title: Ryot: `createOrUpdateUserIntegration` trusts a client-supplied `integrationId` with no ownership check, letting any user hijack/overwrite another user's integration (cross-tenant IDOR)

desc: A flaw was found in OpenShift Pipelines-as-Code (PAC). PAC does not verify whether the creator of a Repository custom resource has permission to create PipelineRuns. A namespace user with only Repository and Secret create/delete permissions can cause PAC to execute attacker-controlled PipelineRuns as the auto-provisioned pipeline ServiceAccount, which carries ClusterRole/edit by default. This results in namespace-scoped privilege escalation, enabling Secret read, resource creation/modification/deletion, and potential supply chain injection in CI/CD namespaces.
products: red hat:builds for red hat openshift
red hat:red hat openshift dev spaces
title: Pipelines-as-code: openshift-pipelines-operator-rh: pipelines-as-code: repository users can trigger namespace edit-equivalent execution via auto-provisioned pipeline serviceaccount

desc: Botan is a C++ cryptography library. Prior to 3.13.0, Botan's X.509 Distinguished Name decoder flattens the Attribute-Value Assertions in each Relative Distinguished Name and loses multi-value RDN grouping before DN name-constraint enforcement. An attacker controlling a name-constrained intermediate CA can issue a certificate with a multi-value RDN whose first Common Name matches the permitted constraint and whose second Common Name is attacker-chosen, causing the constraint check to accept the flattened first value. If the certificate contains no subjectAlternativeName extension, the second Common Name can then be accepted as a hostname; Botan does not fall back to Common Name hostname matching when any subjectAlternativeName is present. The exposure is limited to deployments using DN name constraints, which are uncommon outside internal PKIs, and to certificates without a subjectAlternativeName. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.
title: Botan: directoryName nameConstraint bypass via multi-AVA RDN flattening in matches_dn

desc: liboqs is a C-language cryptographic library that provides implementations of post-quantum cryptography algorithms. Prior to 0.16.0, the ct_select function in src/kem/frodokem/external/util.c for the FrodoKEM-640, FrodoKEM-976, and FrodoKEM-1344 AES and SHAKE reference variants lacks a value barrier in the Fujisaki-Okamoto implicit-rejection path. When compiled with Clang 17 or later at an affected optimization level such as -Os, the compiler can emit a secret-dependent conditional load, causing the real and rejection secret paths to leave distinguishable cache residency after successful and failed decapsulation.
